definition_en: based on the number ten, or a number written with a point to show parts smaller than one

senses.title: Based on the number ten
senses.definition: organized in groups of ten, with each place worth ten times the one before
senses.definitionCN: 以十为一组组织，每一位的值是前一位的十倍
senses.example: The decimal system makes calculation with large numbers manageable.
senses.exampleCN: 十进制让大数计算变得好处理。
senses.why: decimal comes from Latin decimus 'tenth', and the whole system is built on the tenth step.
senses.whyCN: decimal 来自拉丁 decimus「第十」，整个系统正建立在「每十进一」上。

senses.title: A number with a point
senses.definition: a number written with a point to separate whole units from parts of a unit
senses.definitionCN: 用一个小点把整数单位与不足一的部分分开写出的数
senses.example: Every price in the shop is written as a decimal with two places.
senses.exampleCN: 店里每张价签都写成保留两位的小数。
senses.why: the point marks where the counting of whole units stops and the counting of tenths begins.
senses.whyCN: 这个小点标出整数单位数到哪里为止、十分位从哪里开始。

senses.title: A decimal place
senses.definition: one of the positions to the right of the decimal point, each worth a tenth of the one before
senses.definitionCN: 小数点右边的某一位，每一位是前一位的十分之一
senses.example: Rounding to one decimal place removed the noisy last digit.
senses.exampleCN: 保留一位小数就把最后那个嘈杂的数字去掉了。
senses.why: every step to the right divides by ten, so each position is literally a tenth part of the previous one.
senses.whyCN: 每往右一步就除以十，因此每一位确实是前一位的十分之一。

senses.title: Decimal notation
senses.definition: the written form of a number using digits and a point rather than a fraction bar
senses.definitionCN: 用数字与一个小点而不是分数横线写出的形式
senses.example: Decimal notation is easier to compare on a screen than stacked fractions.
senses.exampleCN: 在屏幕上，小数记法比上下叠写的分数更容易比较。
senses.why: the notation is named after the base it uses, because its places advance by powers of ten.
senses.whyCN: 这种记法以它所用的底数命名，因为它的数位按十的幂前进。

senses.title: Decimal currency
senses.definition: a money system in which each unit divides into a hundred or a thousand subunits
senses.definitionCN: 每个单位细分为一百或一千个次一级单位的货币制度
senses.example: Decimal currency replaced shillings and pence in many countries.
senses.exampleCN: 十进制货币在许多国家取代了先令与便士。
senses.why: money became decimal when the old non-ten divisions were dropped for tenths and hundredths.
senses.whyCN: 当旧的非十进位细分被十与百取代时，货币就成了十进制的。

senses.title: A repeating decimal
senses.definition: a decimal in which one or more digits repeat without end
senses.definitionCN: 一个或几个数字无限重复的小数
senses.example: One third written as a decimal is a repeating decimal.
senses.exampleCN: 三分之一写成小数是一个循环小数。
senses.why: some fractions never divide evenly by ten, so the decimal expansion repeats forever.
senses.whyCN: 有些分数永远除不尽十，因此小数展开会一直重复。

senses.title: A decimal fraction
senses.definition: a fraction whose denominator is a power of ten, usually written with a point
senses.definitionCN: 分母是十的幂、通常用一个小点写出的分数
senses.example: The decimal fraction is only another way of writing the same value.
senses.exampleCN: 十进制分数只是同一个值的另一种写法。
senses.why: when the denominator is a power of ten, the fraction can be written in place-value form and called decimal.
senses.whyCN: 当分母是十的幂时，分数就能用位值形式写出，因此被称为十进制的。

senses.title: Decimal classification
senses.definition: a library system that divides all knowledge into ten main classes, numbered from zero to nine
senses.definitionCN: 把所有知识分成十个大类、以零到九编号的图书分类体系
senses.example: The librarian found the book under its decimal classification.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆员按这本书的十进制分类号找到了它。
senses.why: the system is called decimal because every level of division uses ten branches.
senses.whyCN: 这套体系之所以称十进制，是因为每一层细分都用十个分支。

senses.title: Decimal degrees
senses.definition: an angle or coordinate expressed as a decimal rather than in minutes and seconds
senses.definitionCN: 用小数而不是分与秒表示的角度或坐标
senses.example: The map stores the position in decimal degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 地图以十进制度保存该位置。
senses.why: the degree is kept as a unit and its fractions are written in tenths instead of minutes, hence decimal.
senses.whyCN: 度数保留为单位，其零头改用十分位而不是分来写，因此是十进制的。

intro.en: Decimal comes from Latin decimus 'tenth', from decem 'ten', with the adjective ending -al. The mathematical use spread in the seventeenth century with decimal arithmetic.
intro.cn: decimal 来自拉丁 decimus「第十」，出自 decem「十」，并带形容词词尾 -al。数学用法随十进制算术在十七世纪传播开来。

items.en: Decem meant 'ten'. The Indo-European source is usually reconstructed with a form meaning 'ten', but the exact shape is a reconstruction rather than a recorded item.
items.cn: decem 意为「十」。其印欧语来源通常被重构为一个意为「十」的形式，但确切形态是重构，不是有记录的词项。

items.en: Decimus meant 'tenth', the ordinal built on decem; it names the position reached after nine steps.
items.cn: decimus 意为「第十」，是建立在 decem 上的序数词；它命名走完九步后到达的位置。

items.en: The adjective decimalis was formed in medieval Latin from decimus to describe reckoning by tenths.
items.cn: 形容词 decimalis 在中世纪拉丁语中由 decimus 构成，用来描述按十分位计算的方式。

items.en: Decimal entered English mathematical writing in the seventeenth century, when decimal fractions and the written point became common.
items.cn: decimal 在十七世纪进入英语数学文献，当时十进制小数与书写的小数点开始普及。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word was applied to money systems and to the library classification that divides knowledge into ten classes.
items.cn: 在十九、二十世纪，这个词被用于货币制度，也被用于把知识分成十个大类的图书分类法。

items.en: The precise first citation of each applied sense is approximate; decem and decimus are securely attested Latin words.
items.cn: 每个应用义的确切首见书证都是约数；decem 与 decimus 则是有可靠记录的拉丁词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin word for ten and is easily mistaken; the second group names other number systems and written forms.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「十」的拉丁词，容易误认；第二组是其他数制与书写形式。

entries.definition: Historically to kill one in ten as punishment; it shares decem but has nothing to do with place value.
entries.definitionCN: 历史上指为惩罚而十人中杀一；同样出自 decem，但与位值无关。

entries.definition: A period of ten years; it comes from Greek dekas 'a group of ten', a different but related counting word.
entries.definitionCN: 指十年；来自希腊 dekas「十人一组」，是不同但相关的计数词。

entries.definition: A unit built with the prefix deci- 'tenth' plus bel; it measures sound by a logarithmic ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「十分之一」的前缀加 bel 构成的单位，用对数比值衡量声音。

entries.definition: Built on duodecim 'twelve' with decem inside; it describes base twelve, not base ten.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁语中表示「十二」的词构成，里面含 decem；描述十二进制，而非十进制。

entries.definition: One tenth of a metre; the prefix deci- carries the tenth, while decimal describes the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 指十分之一米；前缀只带「十分之一」，而 decimal 描述整个体系。

entries.definition: A learned synonym for base-ten, built on Latin deni 'ten each'; it is rarer than decimal.
entries.definitionCN: 十进制的一个书面同义词，建立在拉丁语中表示「每十个」的词上；比 decimal 更少见。

entries.definition: Describing parts of a unit; it says nothing about whether the parts are counted in tenths.
entries.definitionCN: 描述单位的部分，并不说明这些部分是否按十分位计数。

entries.definition: A written symbol for a number; decimal names a system, while numeral names the mark.
entries.definitionCN: 指表示数的书写符号；前者命名体系，后者命名记号。

entries.definition: A measuring system whose units step by powers of ten; it is decimal in its design but not a synonym for every decimal number.
entries.definitionCN: 指按十的幂进位的度量体系；它在设计上是十进的，但不是所有小数的同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin word for ten, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「十」、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin decem 'ten': every place is worth ten times the one to its right.
normal.cn: 拉丁 decem「十」：每一位都是它右边那一位的十倍。

normal.en: The family runs decimal, decimalize, decimalization, decimally and duodecimal.
normal.cn: 同族词有 decimal、decimalize、decimalization、decimally 与 duodecimal。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: decimal point, decimal place, decimal currency.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：小数点、小数位、十进制货币。

normal.en: The point is a hinge: whole units on the left, tenths on the right.
normal.cn: 小数点是铰链：左边是整数单位，右边是十分位。

normal.en: A decimal fraction is simply a fraction whose denominator is a power of ten.
normal.cn: 十进制分数不过是分母为十的幂的分数。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase with ten steps to every landing, then ten more to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象每十级台阶到一个平台，再十级到下一个平台。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler that keeps halving the gap, but always by ten instead of two.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子不断把间隔细分，只是每次按十而不是按二。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag where the last two digits are the crumbs of a dollar.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签，最后两位数字是一块钱掉下的碎屑。

examples.en: The measurement was recorded to three decimal places.
examples.cn: 这个测量值记录到三位小数。

examples.en: The country changed to decimal currency in the nineteen sixties.
examples.cn: 这个国家在二十世纪六十年代改用十进制货币。

examples.en: Turning the fraction into a decimal made the comparison obvious.
examples.cn: 把分数化成小数后，比较就一目了然了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得西」——「十」的音——按十往下分，一位一位往右走 → 十进制的、小数

root: 拉丁 decem「十」→ decimus「第十」→ 中世纪拉丁 decimalis → 英语 decimal。印欧语「十」的形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all keep the tenth step: a system in tens, a number with a point, a place worth a tenth, a notation, a currency, a repeating tail, a fraction with a power of ten below, a library scheme and a coordinate.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都保留「每十进一」这一步：十进体系、带点的数、值是十分位的数位、记法、货币、循环的尾巴、分母为十的幂的分数、图书分类体系与坐标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler marked in tens, with each gap split again into ten.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把按十标度的尺子，每段间隔再细分成十小格。

branches.en: TEN AS THE UNIT: the base-ten system and the money that divides each unit into a hundred.
branches.cn: 以十为单位：十进体系，以及把每个单位细分成一百的货币。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN SPLIT: a point separates whole units from parts, and digits replace the fraction bar.
branches.cn: 写下来的分割：小点把整数单位与零头分开，数字取代了分数横线。

branches.en: TENTHS BELOW: each place is worth a tenth, and the denominator is a power of ten.
branches.cn: 往下的十分位：每一位值十分之一，分母则是十的幂。

branches.en: THE ENDLESS TAIL: a fraction that never divides evenly repeats its digits forever.
branches.cn: 无尽的尾巴：除不尽十的分数，其数字永远重复。

branches.en: TEN BRANCHES ELSEWHERE: libraries split knowledge into ten classes, and maps split a degree into tenths.
branches.cn: 别处的十个分支：图书馆把知识分成十大类，地图把一度细分成十分位。

intro.en: Decimal is a Latin ordinal turned adjective; its root is the common word for ten, and the endings are still productive.
intro.cn: decimal 是由拉丁序数词转成的形容词；其词根是「十」这个常用词，词尾至今能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin decem and decimus give decimal, decimate, decimeter and duodecimal; the ending -alis, through French -al, forms relational adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 decem 与 decimus 衍生 decimal、decimate、decimeter 与 duodecimal；词尾 -alis 经法语 -al 构成关系形容词。

senses.title: A person who lives somewhere
senses.definition: a person who lives in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: （名词）住在某个地方的人
senses.example: Each dweller of the block has a key to the side gate.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼的每位住户都有一把侧门的钥匙。
senses.why: A wall of brass nameplates in an apartment lobby, one small door behind each name.
senses.whyCN: 公寓门厅里一整墙铜名牌，每个名字后面都有一扇小门。

senses.title: An animal in its habitat
senses.definition: an animal that lives in a particular kind of place
senses.definitionCN: （名词）生活在某类环境中的动物
senses.example: The owl is a forest dweller that hunts along the same edge every night.
senses.exampleCN: 猫头鹰是森林栖息者，每晚沿着同一条林缘捕食。
senses.why: A hollow in an old trunk with a few feathers caught on the bark at its mouth.
senses.whyCN: 老树干上的一个树洞，洞口树皮上挂着几根羽毛。

senses.title: A label for a way of living
senses.definition: a word placed after a place name to describe how someone lives
senses.definitionCN: （名词）放在地点词之后、描述某人如何生活的词
senses.example: The museum card calls them cave dweller and forest dweller.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的卡片把他们称为穴居者与森林栖息者。
senses.why: A museum card reads cave dweller beside a stone tool and forest dweller beside a bark basket.
senses.whyCN: 一张博物馆卡片在石器旁写着穴居者，在树皮篮旁写着森林栖息者。

intro.en: Dweller is dwell plus -er, the ending that names the one who does something; dwell itself began as a verb of delaying and only later settled into the sense of living in a place.
intro.cn: dweller 由 dwell 加 -er 构成，这个后缀指称「做这件事的人」；dwell 本身起初是表示拖延的动词，后来才定为「住在某地」。

items.en: Old English dwellan meant to lead astray or to delay.
items.cn: 古英语 dwellan 意为引入歧途或拖延。

items.en: Old Norse dvelja meant to stay or to tarry, and pushed the verb toward staying.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 dvelja 意为停留、耽搁，把这个动词推向「停留」。

items.en: Middle English dwellen settled on the sense of remaining in one place.
items.cn: 中古英语 dwellen 定于「留在一个地方」这一义。

items.en: The ending -er turns the verb into a noun for the one who does it.
items.cn: 后缀 -er 把动词变成「做这件事的人」的名词。

items.en: Writers on cities used dweller for the people crowded into them.
items.cn: 论述城市的作家用 dweller 指挤在城市里的人。

items.en: Today dweller covers both people and animals in a habitat.
items.cn: 今天 dweller 既指人，也指栖息地里的动物。

note.en: Dweller keeps the agent ending -er, so it looks like seller and teller; its neighbours name the same idea from the side of law, biology or a single room.
note.cn: dweller 保留表「做某事的人」的后缀 -er，所以字形与 seller、teller 相近；它的近义词则分别从法律、生物或单个房间的角度指称同一概念。

dict_mnemonic.text: dweller ＝ dwell（居住）＋ -er（做这件事的人）＝「住在这里的人」。dwell 的古义其实是「拖延、使人迷路」，古诺斯语 dvelja「停留」把它推向了「住下」。同族词 dwelling 指「住所」这个地点，dweller 指「人」，别混。常见搭配是地点词 ＋ dweller：city dweller 城市居民、cave dweller 穴居者、forest dweller 森林栖息者。近义词 resident 偏法律与登记身份，inhabitant 偏生物与地理分布，occupant 偏「此刻在某个房间或车里的人」。

root: 古英语 dwellan（拖延）→ 古诺斯语 dvelja（停留）→ dwell（居住）＋ -er（人）→ dweller（居住者）

sensesIntro.en: Belonging to a place: a brass nameplate with a door behind it, a feather at the mouth of a tree hollow and a museum card naming a way of life.
sensesIntro.cn: 属于某个地方：铜名牌后面的一扇门、树洞口的一根羽毛，以及写着某种生活方式的博物馆卡片。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall of brass nameplates in an apartment lobby with one small door behind each name
core.cn: 核心意象：公寓门厅里一整墙铜名牌，每个名字后面都有一扇小门

branches.en: An animal that lives in a habitat.

branches.en: A label joined to a place word.
branches.cn: 接在地点词之后的标签。

branches.en: Both are the one who stays there.
branches.cn: 两者都是「留在那里的那一个」。

branches.en: The habitat becomes a name for the life.
branches.cn: 栖息地变成了这种生活的名字。

intro.en: Dweller is dwell plus the agent ending -er; in- builds indwell, while Latin habit-, sid- and occup- give the neighbouring words for living somewhere.
intro.cn: dweller 由 dwell 加表人的后缀 -er 组成；in- 造出 indwell，而拉丁语 habit-、sid- 与 occup- 给出指称「住在某地」的近义词。

latinIntro.en: Latin habitare means to dwell, sedere to sit, occupare to seize and domus a house; cavus means hollow.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habitare 意为居住，sedere 意为坐，occupare 意为占据，domus 意为房屋；cavus 意为空的。

definition_zh: 濒危物种；有灭绝危险的物种
definition_en: a species whose numbers have fallen so low that it is in danger of dying out
core_image: 一份名录上排着一行行名字，每一行旁边都空出一个位置，像候诊室里一个个空椅子
scene: 这里指「濒危物种」。 Every endangered species on the list receives a recovery plan.
sceneCN: 这里 endangered species 指「被认定有灭绝危险、因而需要干预的物种」（第 2 个义项：依法列名并附带恢复义务的物种）；句意为名录上的每个濒危物种都配有一份恢复计划。图中可辨识物件：名录纸页、逐行名字、空出的位置、恢复计划表格。

senses.title: A species at risk of dying out
senses.definition: a species whose remaining numbers are too low to be safe in the long run
senses.definitionCN: 剩余数量过低、长期难以存续的物种
senses.example: Every endangered species on the list receives a recovery plan.
senses.exampleCN: 名录上的每个濒危物种都配有一份恢复计划。
senses.why: the phrase simply joins the adjective of risk to the noun for a kind of living thing, and the risk is the whole point.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语只是把表示风险的形容词接到表示生物种类的名词上，而风险正是它的全部要点。

senses.title: A species listed by statute
senses.definition: a species formally placed on a legal list, which brings protection and recovery duties
senses.definitionCN: 被正式列入法律名录的物种，随之附带保护与恢复义务
senses.example: The snail became an endangered species under federal law.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蜗牛依据联邦法律成为濒危物种。
senses.why: law needs a countable, listable unit, and this phrase supplies one, turning a condition into a status.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个可数、可列名的单位，这个短语正好提供，把一种状况变成一种身份。

senses.title: One rung of a ranking
senses.definition: the category between vulnerable and critically endangered in conservation rankings
senses.definitionCN: 保护等级排序中介于易危与极危的一档
senses.example: The cat is officially an endangered species, not yet critically so.
senses.exampleCN: 这种猫正式列为濒危物种，尚未到极危。
senses.why: a ranked scale needs names for each step, and this phrase became the step that sits one above vulnerable.
senses.whyCN: 分级尺度需要为每一档命名，这个短语就成了高于易危的那一档。

senses.title: A species in rapid decline
senses.definition: a species whose population is falling fast even if it is still numerous
senses.definitionCN: 指数量虽仍多但下滑迅速的物种
senses.example: The shark is an endangered species despite large catches still being reported.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管仍报告大量渔获，这种鲨鱼已是濒危物种。
senses.why: what matters is the direction of the curve, not the current height, so a still-numerous species can carry the label.
senses.whyCN: 关键在于曲线的方向而非当下的高度，因此数量仍多的物种也能带这个标签。

senses.title: A flagship on a campaign poster
senses.titleCN: 作为宣传旗舰的濒危物种
senses.definition: a species used in campaigns because its plight attracts attention and money
senses.definitionCN: 因处境引人注意、能带来关注与资金的宣传用物种
senses.example: The panda became the endangered species on every poster.
senses.exampleCN: 熊猫成了每张海报上的濒危物种。
senses.why: campaigns need a face rather than a list, so one species stands in for the category.
senses.whyCN: 宣传活动需要一张脸而非一份清单，因此由某个物种代表整个类别。

senses.title: Protection as policy and budget
senses.titleCN: 作为政策与预算的保护对象
senses.definition: the object of laws, budgets and recovery programmes rather than a single animal
senses.definitionCN: 指法律、预算与恢复计划的对象，而非单个动物
senses.example: Spending on endangered species has risen every year since the act passed.
senses.exampleCN: 自该法通过以来，濒危物种相关支出逐年上升。
senses.why: a category that can be funded becomes a budget line, and the phrase shifts from animals to programmes.
senses.whyCN: 可拨款的类别会变成预算条目，短语便从动物转向计划。

senses.title: A vanishing kind of anything
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：正在消失的一类人或物
senses.definition: a group or type of thing that is becoming rare and may disappear, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指日益稀少、可能消失的一类人或事物
senses.example: The corner bookshop is an endangered species in this city.
senses.exampleCN: 街角书店在这座城市里已是濒危物种。
senses.why: once the phrase is familiar, it can be borrowed for any type that is being pushed out of existence.
senses.whyCN: 短语一旦为人熟悉，就可借用于任何正被挤出存在的类型。

senses.title: The term inside a statute
senses.titleCN: 法律条文内的固定用语
senses.definition: the exact wording used by statutes and treaties to define what counts as protected
senses.definitionCN: 法规与条约用来界定受保护对象的固定措辞
senses.example: The definition of endangered species in the act runs to three pages.
senses.exampleCN: 该法对濒危物种的界定有三页之长。
senses.why: law cannot leave a key term vague, so the everyday phrase is given a precise statutory wording.
senses.whyCN: 法律不能让关键术语含糊，因此给这个日常短语配上了精确的法定措辞。

intro.en: The phrase pairs an English adjective built on danger with Latin species 'kind, appearance'. Species comes from specere 'to look'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把基于 danger 的英语形容词与拉丁 species「种类、外观」并列。species 出自 specere「看」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Species in Latin meant 'a look, an appearance, a kind'; it was a fifth-declension noun and already covered both singular and plural uses.
items.cn: 拉丁 species 意为「外观、样子、种类」，属第五变格法名词，当时已兼有单数与复数用法。

items.en: The noun rests on specere 'to look, to see', the same root that gives spectacle, inspect and specimen.
items.cn: 这个名词基于 specere「看、观察」，同一词根也给出 spectacle、inspect 与 specimen。

items.en: English adopted species in the sixteenth century, and its biological sense was fixed by Linnaeus in the eighteenth.
items.cn: 英语于 16 世纪吸收 species，其生物学义由林奈在 18 世纪固定。

items.en: The fixed phrase emerged in the 1960s; the United States passed an Endangered Species Preservation Act in 1966 and the Endangered Species Act in 1973.
items.cn: 这一固定短语在 1960 年代出现；美国 1966 年通过《濒危物种保存法》，1973 年通过《濒危物种法》。

items.en: The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora, signed in 1973, carried the phrase into international law.
items.cn: 1973 年签署的《濒危野生动植物种国际贸易公约》把这个短语带入国际法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest printed use of the full phrase is not precisely recorded, and the deeper origin of Latin specere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：完整短语的最早印刷记录没有确切定论；拉丁 specere 的更深来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the risk labels that are stacked in a fixed order and constantly swapped; group two holds ways of naming rarity or protection.
note.cn: 第一组是按固定次序叠放、常被替换的风险标签；第二组是命名稀有或受保护的其他说法。

entries.definition: In United States law, a species likely to become endangered in the near future; it is less severe than endangered.
entries.definitionCN: 在美国法律中指很可能在近期变为濒危的物种；严重程度低于 endangered。

entries.definition: A species at risk because of small numbers or narrow range, but not yet in danger of imminent extinction.
entries.definitionCN: 因数量少或分布窄而受威胁、但尚未面临迫近灭绝的物种。

entries.definition: A species facing an extremely high risk of extinction in the wild immediately; it sits above endangered.
entries.definitionCN: 指在野外面临极高、迫近灭绝风险的物种；等级高于 endangered。

entries.definition: A species with no living members; it has passed beyond the endangered stage altogether.
entries.definitionCN: 指已无存活个体的物种；已完全越过濒危阶段。

entries.definition: A species with few individuals or a small range; rarity alone does not make it endangered.
entries.definitionCN: 指个体少或分布窄的物种；仅稀有并不等于濒危。

entries.definition: A species covered by protective law; the protection may exist for reasons other than extinction risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指受保护法覆盖的物种；保护理由未必是灭绝风险。

entries.definition: An informal cover term for any species in trouble, including those not yet formally listed.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何处境不佳的物种，包括尚未正式列名者。

entries.definition: A species picked for campaigns because it draws public support; it need not itself be endangered.
entries.definitionCN: 指为宣传而选出的物种，因其能带来公众支持；本身未必濒危。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: endangered 'in danger' + species 'kind': a kind that is in danger of ending.
normal.cn: endangered「处于危险」+ species「种类」：一种面临终结危险的生物。

normal.en: The family runs endanger, endangered, endangerment, species, speciation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 endanger、endangered、endangerment、species、speciation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the legal sense: endangered species list, endangered species act, trade in endangered species.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律义：濒危物种名录、濒危物种法、濒危物种贸易。

normal.en: Species is both singular and plural, so the phrase never becomes endangered speciess.
normal.cn: species 单复数同形，因此这个短语绝不会写成 endangered speciess。

normal.en: The ladder runs vulnerable, endangered, critically endangered, extinct in the wild, extinct.
normal.cn: 等级阶梯依次为易危、濒危、极危、野外灭绝、灭绝。

abstract.en: Picture a list where each name has an empty chair beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一份名录，每个名字旁边都有一把空椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a poster animal that stands in for a thousand unnamed others.
abstract.cn: 想象一只海报上的动物，替千千万万无名者出场。

abstract.en: Picture a bookshop treated as a kind of animal that may vanish.
abstract.cn: 想象一家书店被当成可能消失的一种动物。

examples.en: Endangered species are often concentrated in a few small habitats.
examples.cn: 濒危物种往往集中在少数狭小的生境里。

examples.en: The act requires a plan for every endangered species it lists.
examples.cn: 该法要求为每一个列名的濒危物种制定计划。

examples.en: Smuggling endangered species is treated as a serious crime.
examples.cn: 走私濒危物种被视为重罪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「endangered（身处危险）+ species（物种）」——面临消失的物种 → 濒危物种

root: endangered（en- + danger + -ed，danger 经古法语 dangier 源自通俗拉丁 dominiarium「领主之权」）+ 拉丁 species「种类、外观」（出自 specere「看」）。英语 endangered species。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one label: a kind of living thing is marked as at risk, and the label is then read as a warning, a legal status, a rank, a trend, a poster, a budget line and finally a metaphor for anything vanishing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个标签展开：某一类生物被标记为有风险，这个标签再被读成警告、法律身份、等级、趋势、海报、预算条目，最后成为任何「正在消失之物」的隐喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a list of names, each with an empty chair beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份名字清单，每个名字旁都有一把空椅子。

branches.en: DECLINE ITSELF: whether already few or still many but falling, the risk is the defining feature.
branches.cn: 下降本身：无论已经很少还是仍多但在下滑，风险都是界定特征。

branches.en: LEGAL STATUS: a condition becomes a listable status with duties attached.
branches.cn: 法律身份：一种状况变成可列名的身份，并附带义务。

branches.en: RANK AND POSTER: the label is both a rung on a ladder and a face on a campaign.
branches.cn: 等级与海报：这个标签既是阶梯上的一档，也是宣传中的一张脸。

branches.en: POLICY OBJECT: money and programmes are attached to the category, not to one animal.
branches.cn: 政策对象：资金与计划附着在这一类别，而非某一只动物。

branches.en: BORROWED METAPHOR: any vanishing type can be called an endangered species.
branches.cn: 借用的隐喻：任何正在消失的类型都可被称为濒危物种。

intro.en: The phrase joins an English adjective of risk to a Latin noun of kind; the two halves come from different language families and keep their own histories.
intro.cn: 这个短语把表示风险的英语形容词接到表示种类的拉丁名词上；两半来自不同语系，各自保留自己的历史。

latinIntro.en: Latin species yields English species, speciation and specimen, while the adjective half comes through French from Latin dominus 'lord'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 species 衍生英语 species、speciation 与 specimen；形容词那一半则经法语来自拉丁 dominus「领主」。

items.example: The prefix makes a verb of putting.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀造出「使进入」的动词。

items.example: The danger was past by dawn.
items.exampleCN: 天亮时危险已过。

items.example: The colony is endangered by warming water.
items.exampleCN: 该群落受水温上升威胁。

items.example: Two species share the lake.
items.exampleCN: 两个物种共享这个湖。

items.meaning: a kind at risk of ending
items.example: Every endangered species on the list has a plan.
items.exampleCN: 名录上的每个濒危物种都有计划。

items.example: Speciation followed the river's change of course.
items.exampleCN: 河流改道之后出现了物种形成。

items.example: The specimen was pressed and labelled.
items.exampleCN: 标本被压平并贴了标签。

items.meaning: the state of being at risk
items.example: Endangerment of the species was documented in 1990.
items.exampleCN: 该物种的濒危状态在 1990 年被记录。

items.example: A specious argument looks sound and is not.
items.exampleCN: 似是而非的论证看起来成立，其实不然。

definition_zh: 人口统计的；人口结构的；特定人群（名词义）
definition_en: relating to the structure and statistics of populations, or a group defined by shared population traits
core_image: 一张人口金字塔图，底层宽、顶层窄，每条横杠代表一个年龄组
scene: 调查表先按年龄和收入把受访者分组： The survey split respondents by demographic group before comparing answers.
