senses.title: Relating to population structure
senses.definition: connected with the size, age and make-up of a population
senses.definitionCN: 与人口的规模、年龄与构成有关
senses.example: Demographic change has left more pensioners than children.
senses.exampleCN: 人口结构变化使领取养老金的人多于儿童。
senses.why: dēmos 'people' plus graphein 'write' gives the study of populations, and the adjective simply describes whatever belongs to that study.
senses.whyCN: dēmos「民众」加 graphein「书写」构成对人口的研究，形容词就描述属于这项研究的一切。

senses.title: Relating to population statistics
senses.definition: connected with the numbers collected about births, deaths, migration and age
senses.definitionCN: 与出生、死亡、迁移与年龄等收集到的数字有关
senses.example: The report opens with a demographic table by region.
senses.exampleCN: 报告开头是一张分地区的人口统计表。
senses.why: the adjective covers both the structure and the figures, so it can sit before data as easily as before change.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词同时涵盖结构与数字，因此既能修饰 change，也能修饰 data。

senses.title: A group with shared traits
senses.titleCN: 由共同特征界定的人群（名词义）
senses.definition: a section of a population defined by age, income, education or similar traits
senses.definitionCN: 按年龄、收入、教育等特征划分出来的一部分人口
senses.example: The survey split respondents by demographic group before comparing answers.
senses.exampleCN: 调查先把受访者按人口特征分组，再比较答案。
senses.why: marketers needed a countable slice of the population, so the adjective became a noun naming that slice.
senses.whyCN: 营销需要人口中可数的一块，于是形容词转为名词，命名那一块。

senses.title: The collected figures
senses.definition: the statistics themselves, usually in the plural demographics
senses.definitionCN: 指统计数字本身，通常用复数 demographics
senses.example: The demographics show a young city growing older.
senses.exampleCN: 统计数据显示，一座年轻的城市正在变老。
senses.why: once the figures are habitually referred to in the plural, demographics becomes a noun in its own right.
senses.whyCN: 当这些数字习惯上用复数指称，demographics 就独立成为名词。

senses.title: The transition model
senses.titleCN: 人口转变模型中的用法
senses.definition: belonging to the model that traces a society from high to low birth and death rates
senses.definitionCN: 属于描述社会由高出生高死亡转向低出生低死亡的模式
senses.example: Demographic transition explains the lag between falling deaths and falling births.
senses.exampleCN: 人口转变解释了死亡下降与出生下降之间的时间差。
senses.why: the model needed a fixed name, and the adjective supplied one that fits every stage of the shift.
senses.whyCN: 模式需要一个固定名称，这个形容词正好提供一个能套住各阶段的名称。

senses.title: A dividend from age structure
senses.titleCN: 人口红利：劳动年龄人口占比高带来的增益
senses.definition: the economic gain a country receives when working-age adults outnumber dependants
senses.definitionCN: 劳动年龄成年人多于受抚养者时，国家获得的经济增益
senses.example: The demographic dividend lasted two decades.
senses.exampleCN: 人口红利持续了二十年。
senses.why: economists priced the age structure, so a bulge of workers became a dividend to be spent.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家给年龄结构定了价，于是劳动力高峰成了一份可以花掉的红利。

senses.title: Ageing and shrinking
senses.definition: belonging to the trend of older populations and fewer births
senses.definitionCN: 属于人口老化、出生减少的趋势
senses.example: Demographic ageing is reshaping the labour market.
senses.exampleCN: 人口老龄化正在重塑劳动力市场。
senses.why: the adjective attaches to any trend defined by the age profile, and ageing is now the dominant one.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可接任何由年龄结构定义的走势，而老龄化如今是主要那一个。

senses.title: A market segment label
senses.definition: used by business to describe the slice of customers a product is aimed at
senses.definitionCN: 商业用来描述产品针对的那一部分顾客
senses.example: The app was built for a younger demographic.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用是为更年轻的人群打造的。
senses.why: segmentation turned the adjective into a targeting word, and the noun became shorthand for the audience itself.
senses.whyCN: 市场细分把这个形容词变成定向用词，名词则成了受众本身的简称。

intro.en: Demographic combines Greek dēmos 'the people' with -graphic from graphein 'to write'. Demography was coined in 1855 by Achille Guillard. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: demographic 把希腊 dēmos「民众」与来自 graphein「书写」的 -graphic 结合。demography 由 Achille Guillard 于 1855 年造出。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dēmos meant 'the people, the common people' and also named a district; it is the root of democracy as well as demography.
items.cn: dēmos 意为「民众、平民」，也指一个行政区；它既是 demography 的词根，也是 democracy 的词根。

items.en: Graphein meant 'to write, to draw'; with -ia it made words for a field of writing or study, as in geography.
items.cn: graphein 意为「书写、刻画」；加 -ia 构成表示某一书写或研究领域的词，如 geography。

items.en: The noun demography is generally credited to Achille Guillard, who used démographie in a work of 1855.
items.cn: 名词 demography 一般归功于 Achille Guillard，他在 1855 年的一部著作中使用了 démographie。

items.en: The adjective demographic followed in the later nineteenth century, and the plural noun demographics spread in the twentieth as market research grew.
items.cn: 形容词 demographic 在 19 世纪后期出现；复数名词 demographics 随 20 世纪市场研究的发展而扩散。

items.en: The twentieth century added fixed phrases such as demographic transition and demographic dividend, turning the word into a policy instrument.
items.cn: 20 世纪又增添了 demographic transition 与 demographic dividend 等固定说法，使这个词成为政策工具。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest English use of the adjective is not precisely recorded, and the exact month of Guillard's coinage is not established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：该形容词在英语中的最早使用没有精确记录；Guillard 造词的确切月份亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words of the same demo- and -graphy stock that are constantly swapped; group two holds terms for describing groups of people.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 demo- 与 -graphy 词干、常被互换的词；第二组是描述人群的其他术语。

entries.definition: The discipline that studies populations; demographic is the adjective belonging to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究人口的学科；demographic 是属于它的形容词。

entries.definition: The plural noun for population statistics or for the groups they describe, as in the demographics of a city.
entries.definitionCN: 复数名词，指人口统计数据或其所描述的群体，如一座城市的人群构成。

entries.definition: A person who studies populations; the word names a profession, not a statistic.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究人口的人；命名一种职业，而非一项统计。

entries.definition: Relating to rule by the people; it shares demo- but concerns government, not population structure.
entries.definitionCN: 与民主有关的；共享 demo-，但关乎政体而非人口结构。

entries.definition: The people counted; demographic describes their structure rather than naming them.
entries.definitionCN: 指被计数的人；demographic 描述其结构，而非命名其人。

entries.definition: Relating to statistics in general; demographic narrows this to population figures.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与统计有关；demographic 把它限定到人口数字。

entries.definition: Combining social and economic position; demographic covers age and household too.
entries.definitionCN: 结合社会与经济地位；demographic 还涵盖年龄与家庭。

entries.definition: The official counting of a population; demographic work uses it but is not identical with it.
entries.definitionCN: 指官方的人口清点；人口统计工作会使用它，但并不等同于它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: demo- 'people' + -graphic 'written': written down about the people.
normal.cn: demo-「民众」+ -graphic「书写」：关于民众的记录。

normal.en: The family runs demography, demographer, demographic, demographics, demographically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 demography、demographer、demographic、demographics、demographically。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the policy sense: demographic transition, demographic dividend, demographic ageing.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出政策义：人口转变、人口红利、人口老龄化。

normal.en: The plural demographics usually means the figures, the singular a segment.
normal.cn: 复数 demographics 多指数据，单数多指某一人群。

normal.en: The same dēmos root appears in democracy and in epidemic's cousin epidemiology.
normal.cn: 同一 dēmos 词根也出现在 democracy 与 epidemiology 中。

abstract.en: Picture a pyramid standing on a wide base and narrowing to a point.
abstract.cn: 想象一座金字塔底宽顶尖。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd sorted into coloured bands by age.
abstract.cn: 想象人群按年龄被分成不同颜色的带。

abstract.en: Picture a shop that knows exactly which age buys its bread.
abstract.cn: 想象一家店清楚哪个年龄层买它的面包。

examples.en: Demographic data show a sharp fall in the number of children.
examples.cn: 人口统计数据表明儿童数量大幅下降。

examples.en: The party's demographic base is older than it was a decade ago.
examples.cn: 该党的人口基础比十年前更老。

examples.en: Advertisers pay more for a young demographic.
examples.cn: 广告商为年轻人群付更高的价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「demo（人民）+ graphic（描绘）」——把人群按年龄收入画出来 → 人口统计的、人群的

root: 希腊 dēmos「民众、平民」+ graphein「书写」（经 -graphic）；demography 由 Achille Guillard 于 1855 年造出。英语 demographic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one view: a population is drawn as a chart, and that view is then read as structure, statistics, a targeted segment, a data set, a transition, a dividend, an ageing trend and a market label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种视角展开：把人口画成图表，这个视角再被读成结构、统计、定向人群、数据集、转变、红利、老化趋势与市场标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a population pyramid, wide at the base and narrow at the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座底宽顶尖的人口金字塔。

branches.en: THE VIEW ITSELF: what belongs to population structure and to its figures.
branches.cn: 视角本身：属于人口结构与统计数字的东西。

branches.en: A SLICE OF PEOPLE: the adjective becomes a countable segment and then a market target.
branches.cn: 人群的一小块：形容词变成可数的人群，再变成市场目标。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: demographics as a plural noun for collected figures.
branches.cn: 数字本身：demographics 作复数名词指收集到的数据。

branches.en: MODEL AND GAIN: the transition describes change, the dividend prices it.
branches.cn: 模型与增益：转变描述变化，红利为其定价。

branches.en: AGEING TREND: older populations and fewer births become a standing phrase.
branches.cn: 老化趋势：人口变老与出生减少成为固定说法。

intro.en: Demographic is built from two Greek elements; demo- is a combining form and -graphic a suffix meaning 'written or described'.
intro.cn: demographic 由两个希腊成分构成；demo- 是组合形式，-graphic 是表示「书写、描绘」的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The elements are Greek rather than Latin: dēmos 'people' and graphein 'to write', the second also giving geography and biography.
latinIntro.cn: 这两个成分属希腊语而非拉丁语：dēmos「民众」与 graphein「书写」，后者还构成 geography 与 biography。

items.structure: Greek dēmos (people) as a combining form
items.example: Democracy and demography share this element.
items.exampleCN: democracy 与 demography 共享这一成分。

items.example: Geography writes the earth, demography writes the people.
items.exampleCN: 地理学书写大地，人口学书写人群。

items.example: Demography tracks births and deaths.
items.exampleCN: 人口学追踪出生与死亡。

items.example: The demographer projected the 2050 population.
items.exampleCN: 人口学家预测了 2050 年的人口。

items.example: Demographic change reshapes the workforce.
items.exampleCN: 人口结构变化重塑劳动力。

items.example: The demographics of the town are shifting.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇的人口构成在变化。

items.example: The two cities differ demographically.
items.exampleCN: 这两座城市在人口结构上不同。

items.example: An epidemic spreads through a population.
items.exampleCN: 流行病在人群中传播。

items.example: The same dēmos root underlies democratic.
items.exampleCN: 同一 dēmos 词根也支撑 democratic。

definition_zh: 艺术史；艺术史学科；（某一时期或地区的）艺术发展史
definition_en: the academic study of the history and development of the visual arts, or the history of art in a particular period or place
core_image: 一排按年代挂起的画，被一条关于风格、赞助与观看方式的线索穿起来
scene: 讲堂的屏幕上，两幅相隔百年的画被并排放置，学生被要求找出构图的变化。 The lecture used two paintings a century apart to show how art history compares styles.
sceneCN: 这里 art history 指「作为学科的艺术史」（第 1 个义项：系统研究艺术发展及其方法的学问）；句意为这堂课用相隔一个世纪的两幅画，说明艺术史如何比较风格。

pos.zh: 艺术史；艺术史学科（通常不可数，特定叙述时可数）

forms.label: 可数用法（少见，指多种叙述）

derivatives.zh: art history + -an（从业者）→ 艺术史学者；从「学科」转到「研究该学科的人」
art history + -al（关系形容词）→ 艺术史的；从「领域」转到「属性」
history + -ic（关系形容词）→ 有历史意义的；从「记录」转到「值得记录」
historic + -ally（副词后缀）→ 在历史上；从「性质」转到「观察角度」
history + -an（人）→ 历史学家；从「叙述」转到「写叙述的人」

senses.title: The academic discipline
senses.definition: the scholarly study of art and its development, with its own methods and questions
senses.definitionCN: 对艺术及其发展进行学术研究，并形成自身方法与问题的学科
senses.example: She studied art history in Florence.
senses.exampleCN: 她在佛罗伦萨学习艺术史。
senses.why: The compound joins a subject (art) to a method of inquiry (history), so the name denotes the discipline that applies historical questions to works of art.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把对象「艺术」与探究方式「历史」连接起来，因此命名的是把历史问题用于艺术作品的学科。

senses.title: A course or programme
senses.definition: a class or programme in this field
senses.definitionCN: 该领域的一门课程或培养项目
senses.example: Art history is a required course for the major.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术史是这个专业的必修课。
senses.why: A discipline taught becomes a course, so the same name can denote the slot in a timetable rather than the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 被教授的一门学科会成为课程，因此同一个名称也能指课表上的一个位置，而不是整个领域。

senses.title: The actual development of art
senses.definition: the history of art as it happened, independent of how it is studied
senses.definitionCN: 艺术实际发生的历史，不依赖人们如何研究它
senses.example: The art history of the period is one of rapid experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 这一时期的艺术史充满快速实验。
senses.why: History can mean the events themselves, not only the study of them; the compound inherits both readings from its second element.
senses.whyCN: history 既可指事件本身，也可指对事件的研究；复合词从第二个成分继承了这两种读法。

senses.title: A particular written account
senses.titleCN: 关于艺术发展的一种叙述
senses.definition: a book or account that narrates the development of art
senses.definitionCN: 叙述艺术发展的一部书或一种说法
senses.example: His book offers a new art history of the interwar years.
senses.exampleCN: 他的书提供了两次大战之间年代的一种新艺术史叙述。
senses.why: Every history is also a telling, so the compound can name one narrative among rivals rather than the objective sequence.
senses.whyCN: 每一种历史也是一种叙述，因此复合词能指与竞争叙述并列的一种讲法，而不是客观序列。

senses.title: Art history of a place or period
senses.titleCN: 某地或某时期的艺术史
senses.definition: the history of art in a specified region, period or tradition
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区、时期或传统中的艺术史
senses.example: The art history of Venice is inseparable from its trade.
senses.exampleCN: 威尼斯的艺术史与它的贸易密不可分。
senses.why: Restricting the compound with of or a place-name turns the whole discipline into a bounded subject: this art history, here.
senses.whyCN: 用 of 或地名限定这个复合词，就把整门学科变成一个有限对象：此地的这一段艺术史。

senses.title: The scholarly literature
senses.definition: the body of published research on a work, artist or question
senses.definitionCN: 关于某件作品、某位艺术家或某个问题的已发表研究总体
senses.example: The art history on this workshop fills three shelves.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这个工坊的艺术史研究文献装满了三层书架。
senses.why: The discipline is also the sum of what has been written; the uncountable use shifts from activity to accumulated text.
senses.whyCN: 学科也是已写成之物总和；不可数用法从「活动」转到「累积的文本」。

senses.title: A method of visual analysis
senses.definition: a method of analysing works through their forms, materials and visual structure
senses.definitionCN: 通过形式、材料与视觉结构分析作品的方法
senses.example: Formal art history begins with a close reading of the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 形式分析的艺术史从对画面的细读开始。
senses.why: Because the discipline developed distinct techniques, its name can stand for the technique itself, especially when contrasted with theory or criticism.
senses.whyCN: 由于这门学科发展出多种技术，其名称也可指技术本身，尤其在与理论或批评对照时。

senses.title: A department or scholarly community
senses.definition: the institutional unit or community of scholars working in the field
senses.definitionCN: 从事该领域工作的院系单位或学者群体
senses.example: The art history department shares a building with the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术史系与博物馆共用一栋楼。
senses.why: Metonymy turns the subject into the people and rooms that teach it: the department is called by the name of its field.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把学科变成教授它的人与房间：院系用其领域的名称来称呼。

intro.en: Art history joins two old words, Latin ars and Greek historia, into a modern compound; the discipline took shape in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: art history 把两个古老的词——拉丁 ars 与希腊 historia——合成一个现代复合词；这门学科在 19 世纪成形。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ars, artis meant practical skill, a craft, or a system of rules; the modern category of fine art grew out of this word.
items.cn: ars、artis 意为实用技艺、手艺或规则体系；现代「美术」这一类别就是从这个词生长出来的。

items.en: Greek historia meant 'inquiry, learning by investigation, a written account'; it came from histōr 'witness, judge'.
items.cn: 希腊 historia 意为「探究、通过调查获得的知识、书面叙述」，来自 histōr「见证者、评判者」。

items.en: Latin borrowed historia as a narrative of events; Old French histoire and Middle English history carried it into English.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 historia，指对事件的叙述；古法语 histoire 与中古英语 history 把它带入英语。

items.en: Art history is a modern English compound: the object plus the inquiry. Similar compounds such as natural history and church history were already established.
items.cn: art history 是现代英语复合词：对象加探究方式。natural history、church history 等类似复合词此前已经确立。

items.en: Universities, museums and printed catalogues turned the study of art's past into a taught discipline with chairs, journals and methods.
items.cn: 大学、博物馆与印刷图录把对艺术过去的研究变成有教席、期刊与方法的可授学科。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): no single first citation for the compound is agreed, and the boundary between antiquarian description and art history is itself debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个复合词没有公认的最早书证，而且古物描述与艺术史之间的界线本身也有争议。

note.en: Group one holds the academic labels most often swapped with art history; group two holds neighbouring ways of studying art that ask different questions.
note.cn: 第一组是最常与 art history 混用的学科名称；第二组是研究艺术但问题不同的邻近路径。

entries.definition: The scholar who works in the field; art history is the field itself.
entries.definitionCN: 在该领域工作的学者；art history 是领域本身。

entries.definition: The evaluation of works, usually present-tense; art history reconstructs their place in time.
entries.definitionCN: 对作品的评价，通常是当下时态；艺术史则重建作品在时间中的位置。

entries.definition: The conceptual framework for understanding art; it need not follow dates or provenance.
entries.definitionCN: 理解艺术的概念框架；不必按年代或来源展开。

entries.definition: General instruction in how to look at and enjoy art, usually without original research.
entries.definitionCN: 教人如何观看与欣赏艺术的通识课程，通常不含原创研究。

entries.definition: The study of all visual media, including advertising and scientific images; art history keeps the fine-art core.
entries.definitionCN: 研究一切视觉媒介，包括广告与科学图像；艺术史保留美术核心。

entries.definition: The study of museums, collecting and display; it uses art history but focuses on institutions.
entries.definitionCN: 研究博物馆、收藏与展示；会使用艺术史，但焦点在机构。

entries.definition: The expert judgement of authorship, date and quality; a handmaid to art history rather than the whole discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 对作者、年代与品质的专家判断；是艺术史的辅助技艺，而非整门学科。

entries.definition: The history of beliefs and practices, of which art may be one source; art history keeps works at the centre.
entries.definitionCN: 信念与实践的历史，艺术只是其中一种材料；艺术史把作品放在中心。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: art + history: the history of art, then the discipline that writes it.
normal.cn: art + history：艺术的历史，然后是书写这段历史的学科。

normal.en: history goes back to Greek historia 'inquiry'; the discipline is an inquiry, not a list of dates.
normal.cn: history 上溯希腊 historia「探究」；这门学科是探究，不是年表。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: art history department, art history survey, a degree in art history.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：艺术史系、艺术史通史课、艺术史学位。

normal.en: The family runs art, history, historian, art historian and art historical.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 art、history、historian、art historian 与 art historical。

normal.en: A museum label often gives the 'art historical' date, while the wall text gives the criticism.
normal.cn: 博物馆标签常给出「艺术史」年代，墙面说明则给出评论。

abstract.en: Picture paintings hung in a row, each one turning to face the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一排挂起的画，每幅都转过来面对下一幅。

abstract.en: Picture a timeline drawn through a gallery rather than along a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一条时间线穿过画廊，而不是画在纸页上。

abstract.en: Picture a question mark placed over a finished masterpiece.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问号落在一件已完成的杰作上。

examples.en: Art history asks not only what a work looks like but who paid for it.
examples.cn: 艺术史不只问作品长什么样，还问是谁出钱做的。

examples.en: The department teaches art history alongside conservation and museum studies.
examples.cn: 该系把艺术史与修复、博物馆研究放在一起教授。

examples.en: Her art history of the region begins with a single church door.
examples.cn: 她写的该地区艺术史从一扇教堂门开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「art（艺术）+ history（历史）」——给艺术写的历史 → 艺术史

root: art 来自拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺」；history 来自希腊 historia「探究、叙述」，经拉丁 historia 与古法语 histoire。二者合成现代英语复合词 art history，19 世纪成为学科。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses separate the discipline from its course, its actual past, its narratives, its literature, its method and its institutional home.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把学科与课程、实际过去、叙述、文献、方法及机构归属分开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of paintings is threaded by one line about style, patronage and the way viewers looked.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排画被一条关于风格、赞助与观看方式的线索穿起来。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND ITS HOME: the discipline as knowledge, then the department that teaches it.
branches.cn: 学科及其归属：先作为知识的学科，再是教授它的院系。

branches.en: THE COURSE: the discipline cut down to a timetable slot.
branches.cn: 课程：学科被切成课表上的一个位置。

branches.en: WHAT HAPPENED: the events themselves, before any account is written.
branches.cn: 实际发生：在任何叙述写成之前的事件本身。

branches.en: ACCOUNTS, LITERATURE AND METHOD: one telling, the accumulated shelf of tellings, and the trained way of reading form.
branches.cn: 叙述、文献与方法：一种讲法，累积成架的各种讲法，以及阅读形式的训练有素的方法。

branches.en: A BOUNDED SUBJECT: the whole discipline restricted to one place or period.
branches.cn: 有限对象：整门学科被限定到一地或一时。

intro.en: The phrase is a transparent compound of a Latin-derived noun and a Greek-derived noun, so both halves can be read with their own histories.
intro.cn: 这个短语是拉丁来源名词与希腊来源名词的透明复合词，两半都能连同自身历史一起读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies ars for the first half and historia, borrowed from Greek, for the second; historia itself comes from Greek histōr 'witness'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语为前半提供 ars，为后半提供借自希腊语的 historia；historia 本身来自希腊 histōr「见证者」。

items.example: Art names the object studied.
items.exampleCN: art 命名被研究的对象。

items.structure: Greek historia (inquiry, account), through Latin and Old French
items.meaning: an inquiry into the past; a narrative
items.example: History names the method.
items.exampleCN: history 命名方法。

items.example: Art history began to be taught in universities.
items.exampleCN: 艺术史开始在大学里被教授。

items.meaning: a person connected with a field
items.example: Historian uses the same ending.
items.exampleCN: historian 用的是同一个词尾。

items.example: The art historian dated the panel by its frame.
items.exampleCN: 这位艺术史学者通过画框为木板画定年。

items.example: The question is art historical, not chemical.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题属于艺术史，而不是化学。

items.meaning: a writer or researcher of history
items.example: The historian checked the inventory.
items.exampleCN: 历史学家核对了清单。

items.meaningCN: 历史上有重要意义的；有记载的
items.example: The sale was a historic event for the museum.
items.exampleCN: 这次收购对博物馆是历史性事件。

items.meaning: relating to the past as recorded
items.meaningCN: 与有记载的过去有关的
items.example: The building has historical value.
items.exampleCN: 这座建筑有历史价值。

latinEntries.meaning: inquiry; a written account of events
latinEntries.meaningCN: 探究；对事件的书面叙述

latinEntries.meaning: a craftsman; a maker by skill

definition_zh: 出生的；本地的；原产的；天生的；（计算机）原生的；本地居民；原住民
definition_en: born in or belonging naturally to a particular place, and hence original or inborn
core_image: 一株只长在这面山坡的野花，根须抓住本地的碎石，移栽到别处便枯死
scene: 这面山坡上只长这一种野花，移栽到别处总活不成。 The plant is native to this slope and nowhere else.
sceneCN: 这里 native 指原产于某地的（第 2 个义项：天然属于某地）；句意为这种植物原产于这面山坡，别处没有。

pos.zh: 出生的；本地的（指生于某地或天然属于某地）
天生的；固有的（指与生俱来的性质）
（计算机）原生的（为某平台原生开发）
本地人；原住民（可数）

derivatives.zh: 原生地；天生地（由基础形容词加表方式的副词后缀而来，由性质转指方式）
出生；诞生（由拉丁词干加表抽象属性的名词后缀而来，由「出生的」转指「出生」这一事件）
本地出生的（由基础形容词与表出生的成分复合而成，由「出生」转指「生于本地」的身份）
本族性；母语程度（由基础形容词加表抽象状态的名词后缀而来，由性质转指抽象状态）
民族；国家（由拉丁同一词干加表过程或结果的名词后缀而来，同一「出生」词根，由「出生的人群」转指「民族」）

senses.title: Born in a place
senses.definition: having been born in a particular place or country
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地方或国家出生的
senses.example: She is a native of the coastal town and knows every lane.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这座海滨小镇本地出生的人，认得每一条小巷。
senses.why: The Latin root is birth itself; the adjective begins as a plain statement about where someone was born.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根本身就是「出生」；这个形容词起初只是关于出生地的平实陈述。

senses.title: Belonging to a place naturally
senses.definition: growing or living naturally in a region and not introduced from elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 在某地区自然生长或生活，而非从别处引入的
senses.example: The plant is native to this slope and nowhere else.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物原产于这面山坡，别处没有。
senses.why: The same birth relation applies to species: a plant is 'born' in its range and does not need a person to place it there.
senses.whyCN: 同样的出生关系也适用于物种：植物在其分布区内「出生」，不需要人把它放到那里。

senses.title: Indigenous person
senses.definition: a member of the peoples who lived in a territory before later settlers
senses.definitionCN: 在后来定居者之前就生活于某片土地的民族的成员
senses.example: The treaty was signed with the native inhabitants, not with the settlers.
senses.exampleCN: 条约是与原住居民签订的，而不是与定居者。
senses.why: The noun turns the birth relation into a political identity, and modern usage often prefers indigenous for this sense.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式把出生关系变成政治身份；现代用法在这一义项上更常用「原住民族」这一说法。

senses.title: Inborn quality
senses.definition: present from birth rather than learned or acquired
senses.definitionCN: 出生时就有、而非习得或获得的
senses.example: He has a native talent for hearing pitch.
senses.exampleCN: 他有分辨音高的天赋。
senses.why: If native means born with a place, it can also mean born with a quality; the metaphor moves from location to nature.
senses.whyCN: 如果这个词指「生在某地」，它也能指「生来带有某种性质」；这个比喻从地点移到了天性。

senses.title: Unmixed material
senses.definition: found in a pure form in nature, as of metals
senses.definitionCN: 在自然界以纯净形态存在，如某些金属
senses.example: The riverbed holds native copper, not ore.
senses.exampleCN: 河床里有天然铜，而不是矿石。
senses.why: A metal 'native to the earth' is one that nature left uncombined; the sense narrows to chemical purity.
senses.whyCN: 「生在大地之中」的金属，就是自然留下、未经化合的那种；词义收窄到化学纯度。

senses.title: Built for a platform
senses.definition: designed to run directly on a particular operating system or device
senses.definitionCN: 为某一操作系统或设备直接运行而设计的
senses.example: The native app opens faster than the web version.
senses.exampleCN: 原生应用比网页版打开得更快。
senses.why: Computing borrows the word for belonging: software native to a system needs no translator layer.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用了「属于」这一含义：属于某系统的软件不需要转译层。

senses.title: First-learned language
senses.definition: the language a person acquired in childhood, often called the mother tongue
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在童年习得的语言，常称为母语
senses.example: Her native language is not the one she writes in now.
senses.exampleCN: 她的母语并不是她现在写作所用的语言。
senses.why: Language is acquired at birth-time, so the adjective marks the earliest layer of speech rather than national origin.
senses.whyCN: 语言在出生时期被习得，因此这个形容词标记言语的最早层次，而非国籍。

senses.title: A local resident
senses.definition: a person who lives in a place by birth rather than by recent arrival
senses.definitionCN: 因出生而居住在某地、而非近期到来的人
senses.example: The shopkeeper is a native but the cook arrived last year.
senses.exampleCN: 店主是本地人，厨师则是去年才来的。
senses.why: In everyday use the noun simply contrasts old residents with newcomers, with no legal weight.
senses.whyCN: 在日常用法中，这个名词只是把老居民与新来者对照，没有法律分量。

senses.title: The colonial label
senses.definition: the dated and often demeaning use of the noun for colonised peoples
senses.definitionCN: 殖民时代用来指被殖民人群的过时且常含贬抑的名词用法
senses.example: Colonial reports used the noun in a way that modern editors avoid.
senses.exampleCN: 殖民报告使用这个名词的方式，现代编辑会回避。
senses.why: A neutral birth word can be turned into a category of rule; this sense names that history rather than endorsing it.
senses.whyCN: 一个中性的出生词可以被变成统治的类别；这个义项命名那段历史，而非认可它。

intro.en: Native comes from Latin nativus 'innate, born', from nasci 'to be born', whose older form gnasci belongs to the gen- root seen in genus and generate. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: native 来自拉丁 nativus「天生的、出生的」，源自动词 nasci「出生」，其更早形式 gnasci 属于 gen- 词根，该词根也见于 genus 与 generate。年代均为约数。

items.en: Nasci 'to be born, to arise' is a deponent verb; its older form gnasci shows the initial g that survives in cognate words.
items.cn: nasci「出生、产生」是异态动词；其更早形式 gnasci 显示出词首的 g，这个 g 在同族词中保留下来。

items.en: Nativus meant 'innate, natural, born with one', and also 'of birth'. It could describe a person born in a place and a quality present from birth.
items.cn: nativus 意为「天生的、自然的、生来带有的」，也指「出生的」。它既能描述生于某地的人，也能描述与生俱来的性质。

items.en: The gen- root 'to be born, beget' is reconstructed; it also underlies genus, genius, generate and nation. The reconstruction is standard but the exact ablaut grades are reconstructed forms.
items.cn: 表示「出生、生育」的 gen- 词根属重构；它也是 genus、genius、generate 与 nation 的基础。这一重构是通行的，但具体的元音交替形式均属重构。

items.en: Old French natif carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of inborn and later of local birth.
items.cn: 古法语 natif 在十四世纪把该词带入英语，先表示「天生的」，后表示「本地出生的」。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the noun was used by settlers for the peoples they colonised, a usage now recognised as demeaning and largely replaced.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个名词被定居者用来指他们所殖民的人群；这一用法如今被认定为贬抑性的，且多被取代。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact pre-Latin shape of the birth root is a reconstruction, and the date at which the computing sense appeared is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个「出生」词根在拉丁语之前的确切形状属重构形式；计算机义项出现的年代也没有精确固定。

note.en: Group one separates near neighbours from the same birth root; group two holds words for original belonging.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一「出生」词根的近邻词；第二组表示原初归属。

entries.definition: A people or state, from the same birth root; it names a collectivity, while native names a relation.
entries.definitionCN: 民族或国家，同出「出生」词根；它命名一个集合，而 native 命名一种关系。

entries.definition: Relating to birth, as in natal care; it is medical and temporal, with no sense of belonging to a place.
entries.definitionCN: 与出生有关的，如产后护理；它属医学与时间用法，不含「属于某地」之意。

entries.definition: A birth, especially the Nativity; it names the event rather than a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 出生，尤指耶稣诞生；它命名事件，而非性质。

entries.definition: Lacking experience; it comes from French naive, from Latin nativus 'natural', but developed the sense of unworldly.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏经验的；来自法语 naive，再上溯拉丁 nativus「自然的」，但发展出「不通世故」之义。

entries.definition: Native to a territory before settlers; it is the preferred term in law and advocacy.
entries.definitionCN: 先于定居者而原产于某地；它是法律与倡议中更受青睐的说法。

entries.definition: Of a nearby place; it says nothing about birth or priority.
entries.definitionCN: 属于附近地方的；不涉及出生或时间在先。

entries.definition: Present from birth as a quality; it covers only the innate sense of native.
entries.definitionCN: 作为性质与生俱来的；只覆盖 native 的天生义。

entries.definition: Found only in one region, often of species or disease; it stresses restriction rather than birth.
entries.definitionCN: 仅见于某一地区，常用于物种或疾病；强调局限，而非出生。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real birth root, its real relatives and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「出生」词根、其真实同族词与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Native means born: the same root gives nation, natal and nativity.
normal.cn: native 意为「出生的」：同一词根给出 nation、natal、nativity。

normal.en: A plant native to a slope is 'born' there; a native speaker was 'born into' the language.
normal.cn: 原产山坡的植物是在那里「出生」的；母语者是被「生进」那门语言的。

normal.en: Native copper is metal nature left unmixed, the chemical version of 'belonging to the earth'.
normal.cn: 天然铜是自然留下、未经混合的金属，即「属于大地」的化学版本。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: native speaker, native species, native to, a native of.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出范围：母语者、本地物种、原产于、本地出生的人。

normal.en: The plural natives is neutral only for local residents; for peoples, indigenous is safer.
normal.cn: 复数 natives 只在指本地居民时中性；指民族时，用 indigenous 更稳妥。

abstract.en: Picture a root system that refuses to hold in foreign gravel.
abstract.cn: 想象一套根须，在陌生的碎石里怎么也抓不住。

abstract.en: Picture a word learned at a kitchen table before any classroom.
abstract.cn: 想象一个在饭桌旁、任何教室之前就学会的词。

abstract.en: Picture software that speaks the machine's own language without an interpreter.
abstract.cn: 想象一种软件，不用翻译就说着机器自己的语言。

examples.en: The eucalyptus is native to Australia but grows all over the world now.
examples.cn: 桉树原产于澳大利亚，如今却长遍世界。

examples.en: A native speaker may still not know why a sentence is grammatical.
examples.cn: 母语者仍可能不知道一个句子为何合乎语法。

examples.en: The app was rebuilt as a native version for each platform.
examples.cn: 这个应用被重做成各平台的原生版本。

dict_mnemonic.text: nasci（出生）+ ive（……的）＝ 生来就在这里的；记「根不肯离开这面坡」。

root: 源自拉丁 nativus「天生的、出生的」，来自动词 nasci「出生」，其更早形式为 gnasci；其词根 gen- 属原始印欧语重构形式，也见于 genus、generate 与 nation。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow birth from a place to species, peoples, innate qualities, pure metals, software platforms, first languages, local residency and the colonial label.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着「出生」展开：从出生地，到物种、民族、天生性质、纯净金属、软件平台、母语、本地居民，以及殖民时代的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a root that holds only in its own gravel.
core.cn: 核心意象：一套只在本乡碎石里才抓得住的根。

branches.en: BIRTH AT TWO SCALES: born in a place, and born into a language.
branches.cn: 两种尺度的出生：生于某地，以及生入一门语言。

branches.en: NATURE AND HISTORY: a species belongs to its range, and a people belongs before settlers.
branches.cn: 自然与历史：物种属于其分布区，民族则先于定居者而属于那里。

branches.en: INWARD AND PURE: a quality present at birth, and a metal left unmixed.
branches.cn: 向内与纯净：出生时就在的性质，以及未经混合的金属。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: software native to a system needs no translator.
branches.cn: 机器：属于某系统的软件不需要转译。

branches.en: RESIDENT AND LABEL: the neutral local, and the colonial noun that modern usage rejects.
branches.cn: 居民与标签：中性的本地人，以及现代用法拒斥的殖民名词。

intro.en: Native is a Latin adjective of birth; its stem also builds a family of English words about origins.
intro.cn: native 是表示「出生」的拉丁形容词；其词干还构成一批关于来源的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nasci and nativus supply the base; the same gen- root reaches English in genus, generate, nation and natal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nasci 与 nativus 提供基础；同一 gen- 词根经 genus、generate、nation 与 natal 进入英语。

items.example: The format is natively supported.
items.exampleCN: 这种格式被原生支持。

items.example: Tests cannot measure nativeness directly.
items.exampleCN: 测试无法直接测量母语程度。

items.example: The church celebrates the Nativity in December.
items.exampleCN: 教堂在十二月庆祝耶稣诞生。

items.example: Native-born citizens and immigrants share the district.
items.exampleCN: 本地出生公民与移民共居这个区。

items.example: The nation was built from many regions.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家由许多地区构建而成。

items.example: The question became a national debate.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题成了全国性的辩论。

items.example: Natal care reduced infant mortality.
items.exampleCN: 围产期护理降低了婴儿死亡率。

items.example: Some abilities are innate rather than taught.
items.exampleCN: 有些能力是天生的，而非教出来的。

definition_zh: 暂定的；试探性的；初步的；迟疑不决的
definition_en: not yet final and open to change, or done cautiously as a first test
core_image: 谈判桌上摆着一份还没定稿的备忘录，签字旁边留着一行小字：待双方董事会批准
scene: 谈判结束时，双方在一份仍可修改的备忘录上签了名，各自都留了一步退路。 They reached a tentative agreement that still needed approval from both boards.
sceneCN: 这里指尚未最终确定、仍可更改（第 1 个义项：暂定的）；句意为双方达成了一份仍待两家董事会批准的初步协议。图中可辨识物件：备忘录、签名栏、一行待批准的小字、会议桌。

pos.zh: 暂定的；试探性的；初步的
（少用）试探性的尝试

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「试探性地；暂定地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「试探性；迟疑」
由同一拉丁动词经法语构成，义为「尝试」，属同源而非直接派生
由同一拉丁动词的另一形态经法语构成，义为「引诱；试探」，属同源而非直接派生

senses.title: Not final
senses.definition: agreed or set for now but still open to change
senses.definitionCN: 暂时确定、但仍可更改的
senses.example: The schedule is tentative and will be confirmed on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 日程是暂定的，周五才会确认。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to try, and what is tried is not yet settled.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「尝试」，试过的东西自然还没有定下来。

senses.title: An initial agreement
senses.definition: an arrangement accepted in outline, pending formal approval
senses.definitionCN: 在要点上接受、等待正式批准的安排
senses.example: The two sides signed a tentative agreement and left the details to their lawyers.
senses.exampleCN: 双方签了一份初步协议，细节留给各自的律师。
senses.why: An agreement is tentative while the signatures still wait for approval upstairs.
senses.whyCN: 协议在签名还等着上级批准时，就是初步的。

senses.title: A testing first step
senses.definition: a cautious action taken to see how others react
senses.definitionCN: 为看看对方反应而谨慎采取的行动
senses.example: She took a tentative step into the new market before committing a full budget.
senses.exampleCN: 她先在新市场试探性地迈出一步，之后才投入全部预算。
senses.why: A step that tests the ground keeps the meaning of trying in the body.
senses.whyCN: 试探地面的一步，把「尝试」的含义落到了步子上。

senses.title: A cautious smile
senses.definition: a slight smile that asks whether it is welcome
senses.definitionCN: 轻微地笑一下，试探对方是否接受
senses.example: The new student gave a tentative smile and waited for an answer.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的学生试探性地笑了笑，等着对方回应。
senses.why: Here the uncertainty is social rather than factual, but the same caution shows.
senses.whyCN: 这里的不确定是社会性的而非事实性的，但同样的谨慎仍然可见。

senses.title: A provisional conclusion
senses.definition: a conclusion offered while evidence is still incomplete
senses.definitionCN: 在证据仍不完整时给出的结论
senses.example: Our tentative conclusion is that the effect is small, though more trials are needed.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的初步结论是效应不大，但仍需更多试验。
senses.why: A conclusion offered while data are still arriving is held provisionally by design.
senses.whyCN: 在数据仍陆续到来时给出的结论，按设计就是暂且持有的。

senses.title: A date that may move
senses.definition: a fixed date that everyone knows may be changed
senses.definitionCN: 大家都明白可能会改的已定日期
senses.example: We have a tentative date in June, subject to the permit.
senses.exampleCN: 我们暂定六月，还要看许可证。
senses.why: Setting a date provisionally is a way of planning without promising.
senses.whyCN: 把日期暂定下来，是一种「做计划但不作承诺」的办法。

senses.title: A hesitant tone
senses.definition: speaking in a way that shows one is unsure of the welcome
senses.definitionCN: 说话时显出不确定对方是否欢迎的样子
senses.example: He answered in a tentative voice, as if expecting to be corrected.
senses.exampleCN: 他迟疑地回答，好像随时准备被纠正。
senses.why: Caution moves from the plan to the voice, and the word now describes how someone speaks.
senses.whyCN: 谨慎从计划移到声音上，词于是描述一个人怎么说话。

senses.title: Exploratory in method
senses.definition: trying a small move in an unfamiliar situation before going further
senses.definitionCN: 在陌生情境里先小幅行动、再决定是否继续
senses.example: The first meetings were tentative, designed to test whether the teams could work together.
senses.exampleCN: 最初的几次会面是试探性的，用来检验两队是否能合作。
senses.why: A method is tentative when its first purpose is to find out whether it works at all.
senses.whyCN: 当一种方法的首要目的是弄清它究竟行不行，它就是试探性的。

intro.en: Tentative comes from Latin tentativus, trying or testing, from tentare, to try, a frequentative form of tendere, to stretch. English took it in the sixteenth century for statements and steps held only provisionally, and the idea of a trial has stayed at its centre.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 tentativus「尝试的、试探的」，出自动词 tentare「试」，而 tentare 是 tendere「伸展」的反复形式。十六世纪进入英语，用来指只是暂时拿出的说法与步骤，「试一试」的意思始终在核心。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch or aim, and its repeated form described trying something again and again.
items.cn: 这个词意为「伸展、指向」，其反复形式表示一次又一次地试。

items.en: Tentare meant to try, to test, and also to attack or probe.
items.cn: 这个词意为「试、试探」，也有「进攻、探察」之意。

items.en: The adjective described what was done by way of trial rather than as a settled act.
items.cn: 该形容词形容出于尝试而非定论所做的。

items.en: French used the adjective for experiments and provisional arrangements.
items.cn: 法语用它指实验与暂定的安排。

items.en: English applied it to opinions, plans and the first movements of a cautious person.
items.cn: 英语把它用于意见、计划以及谨慎者的最初动作。

items.en: Negotiation gave the word its common phrase, tentative agreement; the phrase's first recorded year is uncertain.
items.cn: 谈判给出它最常见的搭配「初步协议」；该搭配首见的年份不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the trying root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of provisional things. The note also separates tentative from tenable, which looks similar but comes from a different verb.
note.cn: 第一组共享「尝试」词根或形近；第二组指其他「暂时性」的说法。这里也把「暂定的」与形近但异源的「站得住脚的」分开。

entries.definition: In a cautious or provisional way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以试探或暂定的方式。

entries.definition: The quality of being provisional or hesitant.
entries.definitionCN: 指暂定或迟疑的性质。

entries.definition: To try to do something; the same Latin verb reached English through French.
entries.definitionCN: 指尝试做某事；同一拉丁动词经法语进入英语。

entries.definition: To lure or test someone; a different form of the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指引诱或试探某人；同一拉丁动词的另一形式。

entries.definition: Able to be defended; it comes from the verb meaning to hold, not to try.
entries.definitionCN: 指站得住脚、可辩护的；出自表示「握住」的动词，与「尝试」无关。

entries.definition: A principle held as true; from the same holding verb as tenable.
entries.definitionCN: 指被奉为真的原则；与「站得住脚」同出「握住」动词。

entries.definition: Arranged for present needs and expected to be replaced.
entries.definitionCN: 指为当前需要而设、预期会被替换的。

entries.definition: Coming before the main event as preparation.
entries.definitionCN: 指在正式活动之前、作为准备的。

entries.definition: Serving only for the time between two settled states.
entries.definitionCN: 指只在两个稳定状态之间暂时顶替的。

entries.definition: Done in order to find out rather than to settle.
entries.definitionCN: 指为了了解情况而非下定论所做的。

entries.definition: Slow to act because of uncertainty; it describes the person rather than the arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指因不确定而行动迟缓，描述的是人而不是安排。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the unsigned contract, the first small step, the careful smile and the June date pencilled in.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用未定稿的备忘录、试探的一小步、谨慎的微笑与用铅笔写下的六月。

normal.en: A tentative deal is written in pencil, not in ink.
normal.cn: 初步协议用铅笔写，不用墨水。

normal.en: A tentative step is a foot testing the ice before the body follows.
normal.cn: 试探性的一步，是脚先试试冰面，身体再跟上。

normal.en: A tentative smile asks a question without words.
normal.cn: 试探性的微笑，是在不用言语地问一句。

normal.en: If the date is tentative, the invitation says so and nobody is blamed.
normal.cn: 日期若为暂定，请柬上会写明，事后也没人该被责怪。

normal.en: Tentative and tenable look alike, but one means tried and the other means holdable.
normal.cn: 「暂定的」与「站得住脚的」形近，一个意为「试过」，一个意为「握得住」。

abstract.en: Provisional things are honest about their own fragility, which is why they are trusted for a while.
abstract.cn: 暂定之物坦白自己的脆弱，所以反而能被信任一阵。

abstract.en: Every firm decision began as a tentative one that someone dared to repeat.
abstract.cn: 每个确定的决定，起初都是一个有人敢重复的暂定决定。

abstract.en: To try is to leave a door open; to settle is to close it, and both have their season.
abstract.cn: 尝试是留一扇门，确定是把门关上，两者各有其时。

examples.en: The committee adopted a tentative plan and asked for cost estimates.
examples.cn: 委员会采纳了一项暂定计划，并要求提供成本估算。

examples.en: He gave a tentative nod, then asked to see the contract again.
examples.cn: 他试探性地点了点头，随后要求再看一遍合同。

examples.en: The tentative date is 12 June, subject to the venue.
examples.cn: 暂定日期是六月十二日，还要看场地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「坦特提夫」：先「试」一下再说话，语气留半分，结论也留半分

root: 源于拉丁语中表示「伸展、指向」的动词，其反复形式义为「试、试探」，再加形容词尾，经法语进入英语。表示「尝试」「引诱」的英语词与之同源，但不是由它直接派生。十六世纪进入英语；「初步协议」这一搭配首见年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one caution: a provisional arrangement, an initial deal, a testing step, a cautious smile, a provisional conclusion, a movable date, a hesitant voice, and an exploratory method.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一种谨慎：暂定安排、初步协议、试探的一步、谨慎的微笑、初步结论、可改的日期、迟疑的语气与试探性的做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signature goes on a memorandum that still carries a line asking for later approval.
core.cn: 核心意象：名字签在一份备忘录上，旁边还留着一行「待批准」。

branches.en: THE OPEN ARRANGEMENT: a plan or date that everyone knows may move.
branches.cn: 敞开的安排：人人都知道可能会变的计划或日期。

branches.en: THE FIRST VERSION: an initial deal or conclusion, subject to approval.
branches.cn: 最初版本：初步协议或结论，仍待批准。

branches.en: THE FIRST PROBE: a small action taken to read another person's reaction.
branches.cn: 探路的一步：先做一个动作，看看对方如何反应。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL HESITATION: a careful smile and a careful voice.
branches.cn: 社交上的迟疑：谨慎的微笑与谨慎的语气。

branches.en: EXPLORATORY BY METHOD: start small in an unfamiliar setting, then decide whether to continue.
branches.cn: 方法上的试探：在陌生情境里先做小步，再决定是否继续。

intro.en: Tentative is a Latin trying verb with two endings; its family covers trying, testing and the caution that goes with both.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「试」动词加词尾；词族覆盖尝试、试探以及随之而来的谨慎。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere, tentare and tentativus trace the path from stretching to trying to provisional.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「伸展」「试」「尝试的」三词，勾出从拉伸到尝试再到暂定的路径。

items.example: The deeper root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这是词族更深的根。

items.example: The repeated form that carries the trying sense.
items.exampleCN: 承载「尝试」义的反复形式。

items.example: It gives the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: It marks the word as describing a manner.
items.exampleCN: 它标明该词描述一种方式。

items.example: It forms tentatively.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「试探性地」。

items.example: It forms tentativeness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「试探性」。

items.example: A same-root word, not a derivative of tentative.
items.exampleCN: 同源词，不是由本词派生。

items.example: Another same-root word through French.
items.exampleCN: 另一个经法语而来的同源词。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「试探性地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「试探性」
同一拉丁动词经法语构成，义为「尝试」，属同源词
同一拉丁动词另一形态经法语构成，义为「引诱」，属同源词

definition_zh: 自治的；自主的；有自主权的；自行运转的；（车辆、机器）无人驾驶的、自主运行的
definition_en: governing itself or acting on its own, without control from outside, including machines that operate without a driver
core_image: 一辆没有驾驶座的车在田垄间自己转弯，方向盘转得比人手还稳
scene: 拖拉机沿着垄沟自己走，遇到地头的石堆就减速绕开，驾驶室里空着。 An autonomous tractor steers itself across the field and slows for the stones at the edge.
sceneCN: 这里指机器无人驾驶、自行作业（第 4 个义项：无人驾驶的、自主运行的）；句意为这台无人驾驶的拖拉机自己穿过田地，遇到地边的石堆就减速。场景图取象：一辆没有驾驶座的车在田垄间自己转弯。

pos.zh: 自治的；自主的（地区、机构）
自主行动的；不受外部支配的（人、决定）
（车辆、机器）无人驾驶的；自主运行的
（哲学、伦理）自律的；自我立法的

derivatives.zh: 自治；自主权（把希腊语「自己的」与「法、规矩」合在一起，字面即「自己的法」）
自主地；自行地（加副词词尾，指不受外部操控地运行）
自主神经的；自动调节的（同源形容词，现代医学多用来指不受意识支配的神经系统）
自治主义（加表示「学说、倾向」的后缀）
使自治；使自主（加表示「使成为」的动词词尾）
自治主义者；主张自主者（加表示「从事者、主张者」的名词后缀）

senses.title: Self-governing in law
senses.definition: of a region, institution or community, having the right to govern its own affairs
senses.definitionCN: 指地区、机构或群体有权管理自身事务
senses.example: The autonomous region sets its own school curriculum.
senses.exampleCN: 这个自治区自行制定学校课程。
senses.why: The Greek word literally means living under one's own law, so self-rule is its oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词字面就是按自己的法生活，因此自治是最古老的义项。

senses.title: Acting independently
senses.definition: able to act or decide without direction from another person or body
senses.definitionCN: 无需他人或他机构指示即可行动或决定
senses.example: The research unit is autonomous in how it spends its grant.
senses.exampleCN: 这个研究单位在如何使用经费上自主。
senses.why: From self-rule in law the word moved to self-direction in ordinary institutions.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法律上的自治，转到一般机构里的自行其是。

senses.title: Self-directed as a person
senses.definition: of a person, able to think and choose for oneself rather than being led
senses.definitionCN: 指人能独立思考和选择，而非被人牵着走
senses.example: An autonomous learner asks the next question without being told.
senses.exampleCN: 自主的学习者不用别人吩咐就会问下一个问题。
senses.why: Education and ethics both prize the person who can set a rule for himself.
senses.whyCN: 教育与伦理都看重那个能替自己立规矩的人。

senses.title: Driverless in the physical world
senses.definition: of a vehicle or machine, able to move and operate without a human driver
senses.definitionCN: 指车辆或机器无需人驾驶即可移动与作业
senses.example: An autonomous tractor steers itself across the field and slows for the stones at the edge.
senses.exampleCN: 这台无人驾驶的拖拉机自己穿过田地，遇到地边的石堆就减速。
senses.why: A machine that needs no hand on the wheel is self-governing in the most literal way.
senses.whyCN: 不需要手扶方向盘的机器，是最字面意义上的自治者。

senses.title: A self-running system
senses.definition: of software or a system, able to monitor its own state and act without a human in the loop
senses.definitionCN: 指软件或系统能监测自身状态并在无人介入时行动
senses.example: The autonomous system rerouted traffic when the sensor failed.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器失效时，这套自主系统重新规划了车流。
senses.why: Computing took the word for loops that close on themselves, a small republic of code.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域用这个词指自我闭合的循环，是一小块代码的自治体。

senses.title: Moral self-legislation
senses.definition: in philosophy, the capacity of a rational being to give itself its own moral law
senses.definitionCN: 在哲学中，指理性存在者替自己立下道德法则的能力
senses.example: Kant placed autonomy at the centre of moral worth.
senses.exampleCN: 康德把自律置于道德价值的中心。
senses.why: The Greek image of giving oneself a law became, in ethics, the ground of dignity.
senses.whyCN: 为自己立法的希腊意象，在伦理学里成了尊严的根据。

senses.title: A self-governing agent
senses.definition: in artificial intelligence, an agent that pursues goals without continuous instruction
senses.definitionCN: 在人工智能中，指无需持续指令即可追求目标的智能体
senses.example: The autonomous agent books the tickets and confirms them itself.
senses.exampleCN: 这个自主代理自己订票并自己确认。
senses.why: Software agents were named after political self-rule, a joke that became a technical term.
senses.whyCN: 软件代理借用了政治上的自治，这个玩笑后来成了技术术语。

senses.title: Weapons that choose
senses.definition: of a weapon system, able to select and engage targets without human decision
senses.definitionCN: 指武器系统能不经人决定就选择并攻击目标
senses.example: Talks on autonomous weapons stalled over the question of accountability.
senses.exampleCN: 关于自主武器的谈判卡在责任归属问题上。
senses.why: When the machine picks the target, the word stops being neutral and becomes a warning.
senses.whyCN: 当机器自己挑目标，这个词就不再中性，而成了警告。

senses.title: Not the same as automatic
senses.definition: governed by its own rules rather than merely following a fixed mechanical sequence
senses.definitionCN: 按自身规则行事，而不只是执行固定的机械序列
senses.example: A thermostat is automatic; a system that rewrites its own rules is autonomous.
senses.exampleCN: 恒温器是自动的；能改写自身规则的系统才是自主的。
senses.why: Automatic comes from a Greek word for acting of itself, but only autonomy implies law of one's own.
senses.whyCN: 「自动」出自希腊语「自行动作」，但只有「自主」才含有自己的法之意。

intro.en: Autonomous comes from Greek autonomos, 'living under one's own laws', from autos 'self' and nomos 'law or custom'. The formation is clear; the exact date of its English entry is uncertain.
intro.cn: autonomous 出自希腊语 autonomos「按自己的法生活」，由 autos「自己」与 nomos「法、习俗」构成。构词清楚，进入英语的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Autos meant self or the same, and it is the source of auto- in automatic, autobiography and automobile.
items.cn: autos 意为自身、同一，是 automatic、autobiography 与 automobile 中 auto- 的来源。

items.en: Nomos meant law, custom or usage, and it also stands behind economy, astronomy and taxonomy.
items.cn: nomos 意为法、习俗、惯例，economy、astronomy 与 taxonomy 也由它而来。

items.en: The compound described a city or people living under its own laws rather than under an outside ruler.
items.cn: 这个复合词描述按自己的法而非按外来统治者之法治生活的城邦或民族。

items.en: Greek politics made autonomy a claim of cities, and the word entered political argument before philosophy used it.
items.cn: 希腊政治使自治成为城邦的主张，这个词先进入政治论辩，后被哲学使用。

items.en: Kant gave autonomy a moral sense, the rational will legislating for itself, which is still the philosophical anchor.
items.cn: 康德赋予自律道德含义，即理性意志替自己立法，这仍是哲学上的锚点。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word was applied to vehicles and software, extending self-rule from cities to machines.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个词被用于车辆与软件，把自治从城邦扩展到机器。

note.en: The first group shares the self or law root or looks close; the second group holds the related words that are routinely confused with autonomous.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「自己」或「法」的词根，或字形相近；第二组是常与 autonomous 混淆的相关词。

entries.definition: The noun: the right or condition of self-government.
entries.definitionCN: 名词：自治的权利或状态。

entries.definition: The adverb for acting without outside control.
entries.definitionCN: 副词：不受外部控制地行动。

entries.definition: Of the nervous system that regulates the body without conscious control.
entries.definitionCN: 指不受意识支配、自行调节身体的神经系统。

entries.definition: Working by itself mechanically; it shares autos but its second half means acting of itself, not law.
entries.definitionCN: 机械地自行工作；共享「自己」，后半却意为自行动作而非法。

entries.definition: Nameless; it looks close but comes from a word meaning name.
entries.definitionCN: 无名的；字形相近，却出自意为「名字」的词。

entries.definition: Not controlled by another, the everyday word for the same idea.
entries.definitionCN: 不受他人控制，是同一意思的日常说法。

entries.definition: Ruling itself, the plain English equivalent of the political sense.
entries.definitionCN: 自我治理，是政治义项最朴素的英语对应。

entries.definition: Without a human driver, the narrow transport sense.
entries.definitionCN: 无人类驾驶，是交通领域的窄义。

entries.definition: Holding supreme authority, stronger and more legal than autonomous.
entries.definitionCN: 握有最高权力，比 autonomous 更强、更法律化。

entries.definition: Setting one's own course, the personal sense without the legal weight.
entries.definitionCN: 自己定方向，是个人层面的意思，没有法律分量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real self and law roots, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「自己」与「法」词根、真实词族与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Autos is self and nomos is law, so autonomous means living under one's own law.
normal.cn: 前者是自己，后者是法，合起来就是按自己的法生活。

normal.en: The family runs autonomy, autonomous, autonomously, autonomic and autonomism.
normal.cn: 同族词有 autonomy、autonomous、autonomously、autonomic 与 autonomism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: autonomous region, autonomous vehicle, autonomous system, autonomous learning.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：自治区、无人驾驶车辆、自主系统、自主学习。

normal.en: The word has three lines: a region governs itself, a person directs himself, a machine drives itself.
normal.cn: 这个词有三条线：地区自治、个人自主、机器自驾。

normal.en: Keep it apart from automatic, which only means working by itself.
normal.cn: 要与「自动」分开，后者只是自行工作。

abstract.en: Autonomy is not the absence of rules but the presence of one's own.
abstract.cn: 自主不是没有规则，而是有一套自己的规则。

abstract.en: A machine that governs itself raises the oldest political question in a new body.
abstract.cn: 自行治理的机器，把最古老的政治问题装进了一具新的身体。

abstract.en: Self-rule is a burden before it is a freedom.
abstract.cn: 自治先是负担，然后才是自由。

examples.en: The province became autonomous after the treaty.
examples.cn: 条约签订后，这个省取得自治。

examples.en: Autonomous vehicles still struggle with unmapped roads.
examples.cn: 无人驾驶车辆在未测绘的道路上仍吃力。

examples.en: She encouraged autonomous work rather than close supervision.
examples.cn: 她鼓励自主工作，而不是紧盯着管。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥托诺默斯」——自己给自己定规矩，自己走自己的路：自治的、自主的

root: 希腊语 autonomos「按自己的法生活」← autos「自己」＋ nomos「法、习俗」；nomos 另见于 economy、astronomy、taxonomy。政治义先出，康德赋予道德自律义，二十世纪扩展到无人驾驶车辆与自主软件系统。进入英语确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one self-made law: a self-governing region, an independent institution, a self-directed person, a driverless machine, a self-running system, moral self-legislation, a software agent, a weapon that chooses, and the contrast with merely automatic.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着同一部自订的法：自治地区、独立机构、自主的个人、无人驾驶的机器、自行运转的系统、道德的自我立法、软件智能体、自行选择的武器，以及与「自动」的区别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tractor with an empty cab turning a corner by itself, steadier than a human hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：空着驾驶室的拖拉机自己转过弯来，比人手还稳。

branches.en: THE GOVERNING BODY: a region or institution that sets its own rules and spends its own budget.
branches.cn: 治理的主体：自订规则、自支预算的地区或机构。

branches.en: THE SELF-LEGISLATING PERSON: a learner who asks the next question, and a will that gives itself a moral law.
branches.cn: 自我立法的个人：自己问出下一个问题的学习者，以及替自己立道德法的意志。

branches.en: THE MACHINE THAT RUNS ITSELF: a driverless tractor, and software that acts with no hand in the loop.
branches.cn: 自行运转的机器：无人驾驶的拖拉机，以及无人介入即行动的软件。

branches.en: THE AGENT AND THE WEAPON: a program pursuing a goal, and a system that picks its own target.
branches.cn: 智能体与武器：追求目标的程序，以及自己挑选目标的系统。

branches.en: THE DISTINCTION: automatic follows a fixed sequence; autonomous follows a law of its own.
branches.cn: 那条区别：自动执行固定序列，自主遵循自己的法。

intro.en: Autonomous is a Greek compound of self and law, with a family that runs from politics through philosophy into robotics.
intro.cn: autonomous 是「自己」与「法」的希腊复合词，其词族从政治经哲学一直延伸到机器人技术。

latinIntro.en: The source is Greek rather than Latin: autos and nomos, with the adjective ending -os becoming -ous in English.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是希腊语而非拉丁语：autos 与 nomos，形容词词尾 -os 在英语中变成 -ous。

items.exampleCN: 它构成自治的、著名的与危险的等词。

items.example: It builds autonomously, meaning without outside control.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 autonomously，意为不受外部控制。

items.example: It builds autonomic, the medical adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 autonomic，即医学形容词。

items.example: It builds autonomism, a political stance.

items.example: It builds autonomize, to make self-governing.

latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 autonomos 意为按自己的法生活。

latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 autos 意为自己，并给出英语的 auto-。

senses.title: An animal that eats plants
senses.titleCN: 植食动物：以植物为主要食物
senses.definition: an animal whose diet consists mainly of plant material such as grass, leaves, fruit or seeds
senses.definitionCN: 指以草、叶、果实或种子等植物材料为主要食物的动物
senses.example: The savanna supports herds of large herbivores during the wet season.
senses.exampleCN: 雨季时，稀树草原养活了成群的巨型植食动物。
senses.why: The word names a dietary class by its food source, so the definition is about what enters the mouth, not about teeth or hooves.
senses.whyCN: 这个词按食物来源命名食性类别，定义关注的是吃进嘴里的东西，而不是牙齿或蹄子。

senses.title: Grazers and browsers
senses.titleCN: 放牧型与啃食型：两种取食方式
senses.definition: a herbivore classified by feeding style, either cropping grass low to the ground or stripping leaves and twigs from shrubs and trees
senses.definitionCN: 指按取食方式分类的植食动物：或贴地啃食草类，或摘取灌木与树木的枝叶
senses.example: Grazing herbivores keep the grassland short, while browsing herbivores reach into the canopy.
senses.exampleCN: 放牧型植食动物把草地压短，啃食型则伸进树冠取食。
senses.why: Ecology splits the class by height of feeding, because grass and browse regrow differently under the same animal pressure.
senses.whyCN: 生态学按取食高度细分这一类，因为草与枝叶在同样取食压力下再生方式不同。

senses.title: Gut and fermentation
senses.titleCN: 消化道与发酵：靠微生物分解纤维素
senses.definition: a herbivore defined by its digestive arrangement, such as a rumen or a hindgut, where microbes break down cellulose
senses.definitionCN: 指按消化结构界定的植食动物，如具有瘤胃或后肠，由微生物分解纤维素
senses.example: As a ruminant herbivore, the cow relies on rumen microbes to digest grass.
senses.exampleCN: 作为反刍型植食动物，牛依靠瘤胃微生物消化草料。
senses.why: Plants are tough, so herbivores are defined as much by the microbial partnership in their gut as by their food.
senses.whyCN: 植物很坚韧，因此植食动物既由食物界定，也同样由肠道中的微生物伙伴界定。

senses.title: Obligate versus facultative
senses.titleCN: 专性与兼性：能否靠植物独活
senses.definition: a herbivore that must eat plants to survive, as opposed to one that eats plants only when other food is scarce
senses.definitionCN: 指必须吃植物才能存活的植食动物，与仅在其他食物稀缺时才吃植物的兼性者相对
senses.example: The koala is an obligate herbivore restricted to a few eucalypt species.
senses.exampleCN: 考拉是专性植食动物，只吃少数几种桉树。
senses.why: The distinction separates a fixed diet from an opportunistic one, which matters when habitats change.
senses.whyCN: 这一区分把固定食性与机会性食性分开，在生境变化时尤为重要。

senses.title: Herbivore as ecosystem engineer
senses.titleCN: 生态系统工程师：植食动物塑造植被
senses.definition: a herbivore whose feeding and trampling reshape plant communities and therefore the habitats of other species
senses.definitionCN: 指其取食与踩踏重塑植物群落、进而改变其他物种生境的植食动物
senses.example: The elephant is a herbivore that engineers the savanna by pushing over trees.
senses.exampleCN: 大象是一种植食动物，它推倒树木，从而改造稀树草原。
senses.why: The label stops describing a diet and starts describing a force: what the animal eats determines what everyone else can eat.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签不再只描述食性，而开始描述一种力量：它吃什么决定了别人能吃什么。

senses.title: Plant defence against herbivores
senses.titleCN: 植物的防御：针对植食动物的化学与物理屏障
senses.definition: the role of a herbivore as the pressure that selects for thorns, toxins and tough tissues in plants
senses.definitionCN: 指植食动物作为选择压力，促使植物演化出刺、毒素与坚韧组织的角色
senses.example: Thorns and bitter alkaloids are defences aimed at herbivores.
senses.exampleCN: 刺与苦味生物碱是针对植食动物的防御。
senses.why: The word appears on the attacking side of a coevolutionary arms race, which is why plant defences are named after it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出现在共同演化军备竞赛的进攻一方，因此植物的防御以它为名。

senses.title: Marine herbivores
senses.titleCN: 海洋植食者：海草与藻类的取食者
senses.definition: an aquatic animal that feeds on seagrass, algae or other marine plants
senses.definitionCN: 指以海草、藻类或其他海洋植物为食的水生动物
senses.example: Sea turtles and some reef fish are marine herbivores that keep algae short.
senses.exampleCN: 海龟与部分礁鱼是海洋植食者，它们把藻类压短。
senses.why: The class crosses the shoreline: wherever there is plant tissue, there is a herbivore adapted to eat it.
senses.whyCN: 这一类跨越海岸线：凡有植物组织的地方，就有适应取食它的植食动物。

senses.title: Herbivore in casual speech
senses.titleCN: 口语用法：素食者或食性比喻
senses.definition: an informal or humorous use for a person who eats a plant-based diet, or for a mild, non-aggressive party
senses.definitionCN: 口语或戏谑用法，指以植物性饮食为主的人，或指温和不具攻击性的一方
senses.example: He calls himself a herbivore, though he still eats eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 他自称植食者，不过仍然吃蛋。
senses.why: The zoological word has drifted into diet talk, where it is friendlier and less doctrinal than vegetarian.
senses.whyCN: 这个动物学词汇漂移到饮食话题，在那里比「素食者」这一说法更轻松、更少教条色彩。

intro.en: Herbivore is a modern scientific compound from Latin herba 'grass, herb' and vorare 'to devour', literally 'plant devourer'.
intro.cn: herbivore 是近代科学复合词，由拉丁语 herba「草、草本」与 vorare「吞食」构成，字面即「吞食植物者」。

items.en: Herba meant grass, green plants or an herb, and it also underlies herb, herbage and herbaceous in English.
items.cn: herba 指草、绿色植物或香草，也是英语 herb、herbage、herbaceous 的来源。

items.en: Vorare meant to devour or swallow whole. It is the second half of carnivore, omnivore, insectivore and voracious.
items.cn: vorare 意为吞食、整口吞下，它是 carnivore、omnivore、insectivore 与 voracious 的后半部分。

items.en: The compound was formed in modern scientific Latin, and French zoologist Georges Cuvier is usually credited with popularising the dietary classification in the early nineteenth century. The exact coining is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个复合词在近代科学拉丁语中形成；一般认为法国动物学家居维叶在 19 世纪早期推广了这套食性分类，但确切的造词者存疑。

items.en: Zoology standardised the triad herbivore, carnivore and omnivore, turning a descriptive compound into a classification system.
items.cn: 动物学把 herbivore、carnivore、omnivore 确立为三分法，把一个描述性复合词变成分类体系。

items.en: The pattern later produced insectivore, frugivore, folivore and nectarivore, each naming a specific plant or animal food.
items.cn: 这一模式后来派生出 insectivore、frugivore、folivore、nectarivore，各自命名特定的植物或动物食物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vore ending and must be told apart by the first element; the near-meaning group separates diet class from feeding style.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -vore 结尾，须靠前半部分区分；近义组区分食性类别与取食方式。

entries.definition: An animal that eats mainly animal flesh. The first element is Latin caro 'flesh', so the two words differ at the stem, not the ending.
entries.definitionCN: 指以动物肉为主食的动物。前半是拉丁语 caro「肉」，因此两词区别在词干而非词尾。

entries.definition: An animal that eats both plant and animal food. The first element omni- 'all' marks the broader diet.
entries.definitionCN: 指既吃植物也吃动物的动物。前半 omni-「全部」标出更宽的食性。

entries.definition: The adjective form meaning plant-eating. Herbivore is the noun for the animal, so the two cannot swap places.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，意为植食的。herbivore 是动物的名词，两者不能互换位置。

entries.definition: A herbivore that crops grass and low vegetation. It is a subset of herbivore, defined by feeding height rather than diet alone.
entries.definitionCN: 指啃食草类与低矮植被的植食动物。它是植食动物的子集，按取食高度而非仅按食性界定。

entries.definition: A herbivore that strips leaves and twigs from shrubs and trees. Do not confuse it with the web browser.
entries.definitionCN: 指摘食灌木与树木枝叶的植食动物。注意不要与网络浏览器混淆。

entries.definition: A herbivore specialising in leaves. It is narrower than herbivore, which also covers grass, fruit and seed eaters.
entries.definitionCN: 指专食树叶的植食动物，比 herbivore 更窄，后者还包括吃草、果实与种子者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: herba 'grass' + vorare 'devour': the plant devourer.
normal.cn: herba「草」+ vorare「吞食」：吞食植物者。

normal.en: Read -vore as 'eater' and the first half names the food: herbi-, carni-, omni-, insecti-.
normal.cn: 把 -vore 读作「吃……者」，前半部分就是食物：herbi-、carni-、omni-、insecti-。

normal.en: The family runs herb, herbaceous, herbage, herbicide, herbivorous and herbivory.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 herb、herbaceous、herbage、herbicide、herbivorous、herbivory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: grazing herbivore, browsing herbivore, obligate herbivore, herbivore population.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：放牧型植食动物、啃食型植食动物、专性植食动物、植食动物种群。

normal.en: Cuvier is usually credited with the dietary triad in the early 1800s, though the coining is uncertain.
normal.cn: 一般认为居维叶在 1800 年代初提出这套食性三分法，但造词者存疑。

abstract.en: Picture a cow tearing grass with a sideways sweep of its head.
abstract.cn: 想象一头牛把头一甩，撕下一把草。

abstract.en: Picture a deer standing on hind legs to reach leaves above the browse line.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鹿立起后腿，够取啃食线以上的树叶。

abstract.en: Picture an elephant pushing a tree over so the whole herd can feed.
abstract.cn: 想象大象推倒一棵树，让整群都能取食。

examples.en: Large herbivores keep the savanna open by eating young trees.
examples.cn: 大型植食动物吃掉落树幼苗，使稀树草原保持开阔。

examples.en: The koala is an obligate herbivore with a narrow diet.
examples.cn: 考拉是食性很窄的专性植食动物。

examples.en: Plant toxins evolved as defences against herbivores.
examples.cn: 植物毒素是作为抵御植食动物的防御演化出来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: herb（草本）+ vore（吃……者）→ 吃草的东西 → herbivore 食草动物

root: 拉丁 herba「草、草本」+ vorare「吞食」→ 近代科学拉丁语 herbivorus／herbivore「吞食植物者」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the plain diet label and then add feeding height, gut design, obligation, ecosystem effects, plant defence, marine life and casual speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从最朴素的食性标签开始，再依次加入取食高度、消化道设计、专性程度、生态效应、植物防御、海洋生活与口语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cow sweeping grass into its mouth, leaving curved bite marks.
core.cn: 核心意象：牛把草扫进嘴里，留下弧形咬痕。

branches.en: DIET: the base sense names an animal by what it eats.
branches.cn: 食性：基本义按吃什么来命名动物。

branches.en: STYLE: grazer and browser split the class by feeding height.
branches.cn: 方式：放牧型与啃食型按取食高度细分这一类。

branches.en: PHYSIOLOGY AND NECESSITY: gut microbes and obligation decide whether plants can be the only food.
branches.cn: 生理与必要性：肠道微生物与专性程度决定植物能否成为唯一食物。

branches.en: FORCE: the herbivore shapes plant communities, and plants evolve defences against it.
branches.cn: 力量：植食动物塑造植物群落，植物则演化出针对它的防御。

branches.en: RANGE: the label crosses into the sea and into casual talk about diets.
branches.cn: 范围：这个标签跨入海洋，也跨入口语中的饮食话题。

intro.en: Herbivore is a two-part scientific compound, and the same -vore ending builds a whole family of diet words.
intro.cn: herbivore 是两部分构成的科学复合词，同一个 -vore 结尾还能造出一整族食性词汇。

latinIntro.en: Herba supplies the food, vorare supplies the eating, and the compound was fixed in modern scientific Latin before entering English.
latinIntro.cn: herba 提供食物，vorare 提供吃，这个复合词在近代科学拉丁语中定型后才进入英语。

items.example: The meadow supports several herbivores.
items.exampleCN: 这片草甸养活着好几种植食动物。

items.example: Herbivorous insects stripped the leaves.
items.exampleCN: 植食性昆虫把叶子吃光了。

items.meaning: the act or process of plant eating

items.exampleCN: 这只食肉动物黄昏时狩猎。

items.meaning: animal eating both plants and flesh
items.meaningCN: 既吃植物也吃肉的动物
items.example: The omnivore switches between berries and insects.
items.exampleCN: 这种杂食动物在浆果与昆虫之间切换。

items.example: The caterpillars are voracious feeders.
items.exampleCN: 这些毛虫是贪食的取食者。

sceneCN: 这里是「堆；一堆」（第 1 个义项：叠在一起的物品）；句意为书摞成高高的一堆立在门口。画面里就是一摞顶到下巴的书。

堆放；堆叠；（pile) （非正式）涌进涌出

pile 与 up 的复合形容词，义为「堆积的」
与 pile 同源的姊妹词形，义为「塔架；桥塔」

senses.title: A mass of things lying one on another
senses.definition: objects stacked loosely on top of each other
senses.definitionCN: 松散地叠在一起的物品
senses.example: A pile of letters waited on his desk.
senses.exampleCN: 一堆信件堆在他的桌上等处理。
senses.why: Latin pila meant a pier or column, and the stone sense became the picture for things resting on each other.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pila 指桥墩或柱，石头意象变成了东西彼此叠压的画面。

senses.title: A large quantity
senses.definition: a very large amount of something, especially money
senses.definitionCN: 很大数量，尤指金钱
senses.example: She made a pile selling handmade jewellery online.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠网上卖手工首饰赚了一大笔。
senses.why: A stack grows until it becomes abundance: the picture of many objects turns into the idea of much.
senses.whyCN: 一堆东西越堆越多，直到变成「丰盛」：从许多件东西的画面转出「大量」的概念。

senses.title: A heavy column driven into the ground
senses.definition: a long heavy beam of wood, steel or concrete driven into the ground to support a building
senses.definitionCN: 打入地下的木、钢或混凝土长柱，用于支撑建筑
senses.example: Workers drove a concrete pile into the riverbed.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把一根混凝土桩打进河床。
senses.why: This sense keeps the original Latin image of a pier standing on stone: a column holding weight.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留了拉丁语原意中「石上立柱」的形象：一根承重的柱。

senses.title: To put things in a heap
senses.definition: to put things on top of each other in a loose mass
senses.definitionCN: 把东西松散地叠放在一起
senses.example: He piled the dirty dishes beside the sink.
senses.exampleCN: 他把脏盘子堆在水槽边。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb by conversion: to make a pile out of things.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接转类成动词：把东西弄成一堆。

senses.title: To move quickly in a crowd
senses.titleCN: 涌进涌出（pile into / out of）
senses.definition: to move quickly and in large numbers into or out of a place
senses.definitionCN: 大量的人快速涌进或涌出某处
senses.example: The team piled out of the bus and onto the field.
senses.exampleCN: 全队从车上涌出来跑向球场。
senses.why: People pressed together like objects in a heap, so the heap picture covers movement too.
senses.whyCN: 人们挤在一起，就像堆里的东西，堆的画面也覆盖了移动。

senses.title: To accumulate over time
senses.definition: to increase gradually until there are too many
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐增加直到多到应付不过来
senses.example: Unpaid bills piled up during her illness.
senses.exampleCN: 她生病期间未付的账单越积越多。
senses.why: One object on another, day after day, until the heap can no longer be managed.
senses.whyCN: 一件压一件，日复一日，直到那堆东西再也无法应付。

senses.title: To add pressure or blame
senses.definition: to add more criticism, work or pressure to what already exists
senses.definitionCN: 在已有基础上追加批评、工作或压力
senses.example: The tabloids piled on after the scandal broke.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻曝光后小报们火上浇油。
senses.why: Adding one more thing to a heap is exactly what a critic does to a reputation.
senses.whyCN: 往堆上再添一件东西，正是批评者对名声做的事。

intro.en: Pile comes through Old French from Latin pila, a pier or column of stone; the heap meaning grew from the column picture, and modern building took the column back as a technical sense.
intro.cn: pile 经古法语来自拉丁语 pila（石桥墩或柱）；「堆」义从柱子的形象长出来，而现代建筑又把「柱」收回去当专业义项。

items.en: Pila meant a stone pillar or a mole built into the sea.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pila 指石柱或伸入海中的堤。

items.en: Pile kept the column meaning as it passed into French.
items.cn: 进入法语后 pile 保留了柱子的意思。

items.en: English took pile for both the column and, by image, the heap of things stacked like stones.
items.cn: 英语借入 pile，既指柱子，也借其形象指像石头一样叠起来的堆。

items.en: Engineering revived the column as a beam driven into soil to carry weight.
items.cn: 工程学把柱义复活为打入土中承重的桩。

items.en: Informal English made a pile for making a fortune and pile up for bills and debts accumulating.
items.cn: 非正式英语用 make a pile 指发大财，用 pile up 指账单债务的累积。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the Latin column family and a false friend; the near-meaning group holds words for heaps and stacking.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁「柱」词族和一个假朋友；近义组收指堆与叠放的词。

entries.definition: A tall upright column supporting a building or a person's role.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑建筑或承担角色的立柱。

entries.definition: A tower carrying cables or marking a road, from the same Latin stone image.
entries.definitionCN: 承载线缆或标示道路的塔架，源于同一拉丁石柱意象。

entries.definition: A structure from shore into water; spelling looks close but the source differs.
entries.definitionCN: 从岸边伸入水中的结构；拼写相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: A disorderly mass of things thrown together.
entries.definitionCN: 乱扔在一起的杂乱一堆。

entries.definition: A neatly arranged pile, often of the same items.
entries.definitionCN: 码放整齐的一叠，通常是同类物品。

entries.definition: A rounded heap of earth or small objects.
entries.definitionCN: 土或小物件的圆堆。

normalIntro.en: The word hides two pictures — a stack of things and a column of stone — and both help memory.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词藏着两幅画面——一堆东西和一根石柱——都有助于记忆。

normal.en: Latin pila, stone pillar; picture a pillar of books standing on the desk.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pila 是石柱；想象桌上一摞立起来的书柱。

normal.en: Pile up works for laundry, bills and snow: anything that grows one layer at a time.
normal.cn: pile up 可用于脏衣、账单和积雪：任何一层层长起来的东西。

normal.en: Pile into the car keeps the heap picture: bodies squeezed like luggage.
normal.cn: pile into the car 保留堆的画面：人像行李一样挤在一起。

normal.en: Make a pile is British money slang — a pile of banknotes, not of stones.
normal.cn: make a pile 是英式金钱俚语——指的是一叠钞票，不是石头。

normal.en: A foundation pile goes down, a laundry pile goes up — one word, two directions.
normal.cn: 地基桩往下打，脏衣堆往上摞——一个词，两个方向。

abstract.en: Gravity does the stacking: things fall onto things, and a pile is born.
abstract.cn: 重力完成堆叠：东西落在东西上，一堆就诞生了。

abstract.en: A debt grows invisibly, but a pile grows visibly — the word forces you to see the burden.
abstract.cn: 债务无形地生长，堆却看得见——这个词逼你看见负担。

abstract.en: From stone pier to paper stack, pile measures everything that holds something up by mass.
abstract.cn: 从石墩到纸堆，pile 丈量一切靠体量托住东西的东西。

examples.en: She sorted the washing into three piles.
examples.cn: 她把要洗的衣服分成三堆。

examples.en: Work kept piling up before the holidays.
examples.cn: 假期之前工作越积越多。

examples.en: The bridge rests on concrete piles sunk deep in mud.
examples.cn: 大桥坐落在深插泥中的混凝土桩上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派哦」——快递员派件派哦，门口堆成小山；pile 就是一堆。

root: 拉丁语 pila（石柱、堤）经古法语 pile 进入中古英语；「堆」义由石柱叠石的形象引申，工程义「桩」则保留柱的本义。

sensesIntro.en: A single stone image forks into two lines: the vertical column that carries a building, and the loose heap that anything falling makes.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个石头的意象分出两条线：承载建筑的竖直柱，和任何东西落下时形成的那堆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: things resting one on another, whether stacked by hands or sunk by machines.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件压着一件，无论是人手摞的还是机器打的。

branches.en: letters lying on a desk in layers
branches.cn: 一层层躺在桌上的信件

branches.en: banknotes counted in thick stacks
branches.cn: 厚厚一叠一叠数着的钞票

branches.en: a beam disappearing into river mud
branches.cn: 一根没入河泥的桩柱

branches.en: players squeezing through one door
branches.cn: 球员们从一扇门里挤出来

branches.en: the same heap, made in a minute or a year
branches.cn: 同一堆东西，一分钟或一年堆成

intro.en: Pile itself is unanalysable, but English builds freely on it with particles and compounds.
intro.cn: pile 本身不可再分析，但英语用小词和复合词在它上面自由构词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root pila left few direct relatives in English; most of the family was built inside English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 pila 在英语里留下的直接同源词不多；词族大部分在英语内部构成。
