definition_zh: 减轻；缓解；缓和；使缓和
definition_en: to make pain, difficulty or a bad feeling less severe without removing its cause
core_image: 压在人肩上的石袋被一只只手卸下一半，肩线慢慢回正
scene: 换药时最疼，护士引导病人慢慢呼吸，疼痛就退了一些。 The clinic uses guided breathing to alleviate pain during dressing changes.
sceneCN: 这里指让疼痛变轻（第 1 个义项：减轻疼痛或症状）；句意为诊所靠引导呼吸来缓解换药时的疼痛。图中可辨识物件：病床、绷带、被卸下一半的石袋。

pos.zh: 减轻；缓解；缓和

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「减轻；缓解」
由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「缓解性的」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「缓解的；缓和剂」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「缓解者；缓解手段」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「已减轻的」

senses.title: To ease pain
senses.definition: to reduce the intensity of physical pain without curing its cause
senses.definitionCN: 降低身体疼痛的强度，但不消除病因
senses.example: The drug alleviates pain but does not repair the joint.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药能减轻疼痛，却修不好关节。
senses.why: Alleviate comes from a word for light, and pain is treated as a weight that can be made lighter.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自「轻」义，疼痛被当作一份可以变轻的重量。

senses.title: To ease pressure or strain
senses.definition: to reduce the level of stress, workload or tension that people or systems carry
senses.definitionCN: 降低人或系统所承受的压力、工作量或紧张程度
senses.example: Extra staff alleviated the pressure on the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 增加人手缓解了夜班的压力。
senses.why: Pressure is a load, so making it lighter is the same physical move applied to work.
senses.whyCN: 压力是负荷，让它变轻就是把同一物理动作用到工作上。

senses.title: To reduce poverty or hardship
senses.definition: to lessen the severity of material hardship, usually by policy rather than by cure
senses.definitionCN: 减轻物质困苦的严重程度，通常靠政策而非根治
senses.example: The subsidy alleviated hardship among the poorest households.
senses.exampleCN: 这项补贴缓解了最贫困家庭的困苦。
senses.why: Social policy speaks of lightening a burden that cannot yet be removed.
senses.whyCN: 社会政策谈的是先把卸不掉的负担弄轻。

senses.title: To relieve congestion
senses.definition: to make traffic, queues or demand less dense
senses.definitionCN: 使交通、排队或需求不再那么密集
senses.example: A second entrance alleviated congestion at the main gate.
senses.exampleCN: 增加第二个入口缓解了正门的拥堵。
senses.why: Congestion is pressure concentrated at one point, and the verb spreads or lowers it.
senses.whyCN: 拥堵是集中在一处的压力，这个动词把它摊开或降低。

senses.title: To soothe anxiety
senses.definition: to make fear or worry less intense, often temporarily
senses.definitionCN: 使恐惧或担忧不那么强烈，常常只是暂时
senses.example: A clear explanation alleviated her anxiety about the results.
senses.exampleCN: 清楚的解释缓解了她对结果的焦虑。
senses.why: Emotional weight is lightened much as physical weight is, which is why the same verb serves both.
senses.whyCN: 情绪的重量与身体的重量一样可以被减轻，所以同一个动词两者都管。

senses.title: To soften an impact
senses.definition: to reduce how hard an event, change or policy hits those affected
senses.definitionCN: 降低某个事件、变化或政策对受影响者的打击力度
senses.example: The fund alleviated the impact of the sudden price rise.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔基金缓和了价格骤涨带来的冲击。
senses.why: An impact lands as force, and lightening it is to take part of the blow away.
senses.whyCN: 冲击以力量的形式落下，减轻它就是卸掉一部分打击。

senses.title: To provide relief measures
senses.definition: to supply practical help that makes a difficult situation easier to bear
senses.definitionCN: 提供实际帮助，使困难处境更容易承受
senses.example: The city alleviated the water shortage with temporary deliveries.
senses.exampleCN: 市里用临时送水缓解了缺水。
senses.why: Here the verb shifts from the feeling to the measure that produces the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词从「感受」转向「产生该感受的措施」。

senses.title: To treat symptoms only
senses.definition: to give symptomatic relief while leaving the underlying condition untreated
senses.definitionCN: 只提供症状层面的缓解，不处理根本病因
senses.example: Hospice care alleviated her symptoms without treating the disease itself.
senses.exampleCN: 临终照护缓解了她的症状，却没有治疗疾病本身。
senses.why: Medicine distinguishes cure from relief, and alleviate belongs firmly to the second.
senses.whyCN: 医学区分「治愈」与「缓解」，这个词稳稳属于后者。

intro.en: Alleviate comes from Latin alleviare, to lighten, from ad, toward, and levare, to raise or lighten, from levis, light in weight. It is not related to the Latin verb for raising or nourishing.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 alleviare「使轻」，由 ad「向」与 levare「举起、减轻」构成，而 levare 出自 levis「轻」；它与拉丁语中表示「举起、养育」的另一个动词无关。

items.en: Levis meant light in weight, and the same root gives levity, elevate and relief through related verbs.
items.cn: 这个词指重量轻；同一词根经相关动词还给出「轻快」「举起」与「缓解」等词。

items.en: Levare meant to lighten or to raise, and the two readings share the picture of something becoming easier to lift.
items.cn: 这个词意为使轻或举起，两种读法共享「东西变得容易举起」的画面。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant toward, and it marks the direction in which the lightening is applied.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「向」，标出减轻作用的方向。

items.en: Alleviare meant to lighten, relieve or comfort, and it was used of pain, grief and burdens.
items.cn: 这个词意为使轻、缓解、安慰，用于疼痛、悲伤与负担。

items.en: It is often confused with allevare, to raise or feed, but the two verbs differ in root and meaning.
items.cn: 它常与表示「举起、喂养」的 allevare 混淆，但两者词根与词义都不同。

items.en: English took the verb directly from Latin in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪直接从拉丁语引入这个动词，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the light root or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of relief and reduction.
note.cn: 第一组与「alleviate」共享「轻」的词根或只是形近；第二组是与「缓解、减少」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of making something less severe.
entries.definitionCN: 指减轻、缓解这一行为的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for something that relieves.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指起缓解作用的。

entries.definition: To raise something, from the same light root through a different prefix path.
entries.definitionCN: 指举起、抬高；同出「轻」词根，经不同前缀路径。

entries.definition: Lightness of mood, literally lightness of weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指情绪轻快，字面就是「重量轻」。

entries.definition: The noun for easing a burden, from a related Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指负担的减轻，出自相关的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To take a burden or pain away, often more completely than alleviate.
entries.definitionCN: 指卸去负担或疼痛，程度常比 alleviate 更彻底。

entries.definition: To make something less painful or difficult, in plain everyday language.
entries.definitionCN: 指使不那么痛苦或困难，是日常说法。

entries.definition: To make something bad less severe, especially damage or risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指使坏事不那么严重，尤指损害或风险。

entries.definition: To calm a feeling or a surface, with a comforting tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指安抚情绪或舒缓表面，带安慰色彩。

entries.definition: To make or become smaller in amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指在数量上减少。

entries.definition: To bring down a size, amount or level, the broad neutral verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指降低大小、数量或水平，是宽泛中性的说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the light root, the false twin allevare, and the medical phrases that keep the word in use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「轻」的词根、容易混淆的近形动词 allevare，以及让这个词保持活力的医学搭配。

normal.en: Levis is light, so alleviate is to put something on a scale and watch the reading drop.
normal.cn: levis 是「轻」，所以这个词就是把东西放上秤，看读数往下走。

normal.en: Elevate and alleviate look alike and are related, but one raises and the other lightens.
normal.cn: elevate 与 alleviate 形近且同源，但一个往上举，一个往轻里减。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with allevare, which meant to raise or feed.
normal.cn: 不要与 allevare 混淆，那个词是「举起、喂养」。

normal.en: Clinics alleviate pain, cities alleviate congestion, and policy alleviates poverty.
normal.cn: 诊所缓解疼痛，城市缓解拥堵，政策缓解贫困。

normal.en: Alleviate treats the symptom; cure treats the cause.
normal.cn: 这个词处理症状，「治愈」处理病因。

abstract.en: To alleviate is to admit you cannot remove the weight, and still take some of it off.
abstract.cn: 减轻，就是承认重量卸不掉，却仍然拿走一部分。

abstract.en: Relief is not cure: the stone is lighter, but it is still on the shoulder.
abstract.cn: 缓解不是治愈：石头变轻了，可还在肩上。

abstract.en: Every soothing act is a small redistribution of weight from the weak to the strong.
abstract.cn: 每一次安抚，都是把重量从弱者身上往强者身上挪一点。

examples.en: Cool compresses alleviate the itching for about an hour.
examples.cn: 冷敷能缓解瘙痒大约一小时。

examples.en: The new lane alleviated congestion on the western approach.
examples.cn: 新车道缓解了西侧入口的拥堵。

examples.en: Cash transfers alleviated hardship but did not end it.
examples.cn: 现金补助缓解了困苦，却没有终结它。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿利维特」——肩上的石袋被卸下一半：减轻、缓解

root: 拉丁语 levis「轻」→ levare「使轻、举起」→ alleviare「使轻、缓解」（ad-「向」）；英语十六世纪直接引入。与表示「举起、养育」的 allevare 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all lighten something: pain, pressure, poverty, congestion, anxiety, impact, shortage and symptoms.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在给某物减重：疼痛、压力、贫困、拥堵、焦虑、冲击、短缺与症状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: half the stones are lifted off a shoulder, and the shoulder slowly straightens.
core.cn: 核心意象：肩上的石袋被卸下一半，肩线慢慢回正。

branches.en: THE BODY IS LIGHTENED: pain or a symptom loses intensity, though the cause may remain.
branches.cn: 身体变轻：疼痛或症状减弱，病因却可能还在。

branches.en: THE LOAD IS SHARED: stress and workload are lowered for those carrying them.

intro.en: Alleviate is a Latin verb built from a light root, and the same root runs through elevate, levity and relief.
intro.cn: 这是一个由「轻」词根构成的拉丁动词，同一词根贯穿 elevate、levity 与 relief。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies levis, levare and alleviare; the deeper origin of the root is reconstructed rather than recorded.

definition_zh: 贫穷；贫困；缺乏钱财与基本生活资源的状态；也指某种东西的匮乏或贫瘠
definition_en: the state of being extremely poor, lacking the money and resources needed for basic living; also a general scarcity or barrenness
core_image: 一只空碗放在缺了角的桌上，窗外的田里只长着稀疏的草，屋里屋外都显出「不够」

sceneCN: 此处指「缺乏钱财与基本生活资源的状态」（第 1 个义项：缺钱维持基本生活）；句意为这家慈善机构致力于减轻河谷家庭的贫困。图中可辨识物件：空碗、破桌、稀疏的田草、救济登记表；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Lack of money for basic needs
senses.definition: the condition of not having enough money to pay for food, shelter, clothing and health care
senses.definitionCN: 没有足够的钱支付食物、住房、衣着与医疗
senses.example: Half the village lives in poverty and often skips meals.
senses.exampleCN: 村里一半人生活在贫困中，常常省掉饭食。
senses.why: The word names a shortage of the means of living, so its core sense is money that does not stretch to necessities.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是维生手段的短缺，因此核心义就是钱不足以覆盖基本需要。

senses.title: The state of being poor
senses.definition: the ongoing social condition of being poor, with its insecurity and limited choices
senses.definitionCN: 长期处于贫穷的社会状态，伴随不安全与选择受限
senses.example: Poverty traps families in unsafe housing and unstable work.
senses.exampleCN: 贫困把家庭困在不安全的住房与不稳定的工作里。
senses.why: Poverty is not only a moment of shortage but a condition that persists and shapes a life.
senses.whyCN: 贫困不只是一时的短缺，而是一种持续并塑造生活的状态。

senses.title: Officially measured deprivation
senses.definition: the level of deprivation defined by income falling below a government or research threshold
senses.definitionCN: 以收入低于政府或研究机构设定的门槛来界定的匮乏程度
senses.example: The census reports poverty by counting households below the threshold.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查通过统计低于门槛的家庭来报告贫困。
senses.why: Modern states turned an old condition into a number by drawing a line and counting who falls under it.
senses.whyCN: 现代国家画一条线、数清线下人数，把古老的处境变成了数字。

senses.title: Scarcity of a resource
senses.definition: a serious shortage of something needed, such as water, soil nutrients or energy
senses.definitionCN: 水、土壤养分或能源等必需品严重不足
senses.example: Poverty of rainfall kept the fields bare for months.
senses.exampleCN: 降雨稀少让田地空了好几个月。
senses.why: The idea of having too little extends from money to any resource, which gives the word its scarcity sense.
senses.whyCN: 「拥有的太少」这一想法从钱扩展到任何资源，于是有了短缺义。

senses.title: Barrenness or poor quality
senses.definition: the state of land or material being thin, worn out or lacking richness
senses.definitionCN: 土地或材料稀薄、耗竭、缺乏肥力的状态
senses.example: The poverty of the soil forced farmers to move every few years.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤贫瘠迫使农民每隔几年就迁移。
senses.why: Land that yields little looks poor in the same way a person with little money does, so the word describes thinness of quality.
senses.whyCN: 产出很少的土地，看起来就像缺钱的人一样「穷」，于是这个词也描述质地的贫薄。

senses.title: Lack of ideas or imagination
senses.definition: the quality of being unoriginal, thin or lacking intellectual substance
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏创意、内容单薄、思想贫乏的性质
senses.example: Critics attacked the poverty of the plan's imagination.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抨击这份计划想象力的贫乏。
senses.why: If a field can be poor, so can an argument, and the metaphor of thinness carries over to thought.
senses.whyCN: 田地可以贫瘠，论证也可以，贫薄这个比喻就延伸到思想上。

senses.title: Voluntary humility in religious writing
senses.titleCN: 宗教写作中自愿的谦卑
senses.definition: the deliberate giving up of worldly wealth or self-importance, especially in religious tradition
senses.definitionCN: 尤其在宗教传统中，主动放弃世俗财富或自我重要感
senses.example: Monks took a vow of poverty and owned nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 修士立下守贫之愿，不拥有任何财物。
senses.why: Religious tradition reframed lack as a virtue when it is chosen, so poverty gained a voluntary, spiritual sense.
senses.whyCN: 宗教传统把自愿的缺乏重新解释为美德，于是贫困获得了自愿的、精神性的义项。

senses.title: Destitution and dependence on charity
senses.definition: the extreme end of poverty in which a person depends on begging or public relief to survive
senses.definitionCN: 贫困的极端一端，人靠乞讨或公共救济才能活下去
senses.example: The old poorhouse sheltered people reduced to poverty.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的济贫院收容陷入赤贫的人。
senses.why: At its worst the condition leaves a person with nothing to sell but labour or appeal, and this is the destitution sense.
senses.whyCN: 到最严重时，人除了劳力或求助已无物可售，这就是赤贫义。

intro.en: Poverty comes from Latin paupertas, the abstract noun of pauper 'poor', through Old French. The deeper origin of pauper is not established. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词经古法语来自拉丁语 paupertas，即 pauper「贫穷」的抽象名词。pauper 的更早来源未查明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pauper meant 'poor, needy'. Its deeper origin is not established; the old link to a root meaning 'produce little' is a hypothesis.
items.cn: pauper 意为「贫穷、匮乏」。其更深来源无定论；把它与表示「产出很少」的词根相联系的旧说只是假说。

items.en: Paupertas 'poverty, want' was the abstract noun, and it passed into Old French as poverte.
items.cn: paupertas「贫穷、匮乏」是对应的抽象名词，后来变成古法语的 poverte。

items.en: Old French poverte entered English in the thirteenth century, naming both the condition and the lack of goods.
items.cn: 古法语 poverte 于十三世纪进入英语，既指贫穷状态，也指物品的匮乏。

items.en: Religious writing used poverty of spirit for voluntary humility, a sense that survives in set phrases.
items.cn: 宗教文献用「精神上的贫穷」指自愿的谦卑，这一义项保留在固定说法里。

items.en: From the nineteenth century poverty became an object of social measurement, defined by income against a line.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，贫穷成为社会测量对象，以收入是否低于某条线来界定。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin of pauper): no agreed Indo-European etymology exists, and the date of the abstract noun is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（pauper 的拉丁语之前来源）：没有公认的印欧语词源，抽象名词的年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close but come from other roots; group two holds words for hardship and shortage.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近却另有词源的词；第二组是表示困苦与短缺的词。

entries.definition: Property comes from Latin proprietas 'ownership', built on proprius 'one's own'; it has nothing to do with pauper.
entries.definitionCN: 财产来自拉丁 proprietas「所有权」，出自 proprius「自己的」，与 pauper 毫无关系。

entries.definition: Propriety also goes back to proprius and means correctness of behaviour, not lack of money.
entries.definitionCN: 礼节同样出自 proprius，指行为得体，与缺钱无关。

entries.definition: Paucity means a small number or amount and comes from Latin paucus 'few'; it is a near neighbour in meaning but not in root.
entries.definitionCN: 少量来自拉丁 paucus「少」，意思相近，词根却不同。

entries.definition: Poor is the everyday adjective related to poverty, but it comes through Old French povre from the same Latin pauper.
entries.definitionCN: poor 是与贫穷相关的日常形容词，经古法语 povre 来自同一个拉丁 pauper。

entries.definition: Destitution is poverty so severe that a person lacks food, shelter and any means of recovery.
entries.definitionCN: 赤贫是严重到缺乏食物、住所与任何恢复手段的贫困。

entries.definition: Deprivation stresses the absence of specific necessities such as heating, food or schooling.
entries.definitionCN: 匮乏强调取暖、食物或教育等具体必需品的缺失。

entries.definition: Hardship is suffering caused by difficult conditions, which may occur without absolute poverty.
entries.definitionCN: 困苦是艰难处境带来的痛苦，未必达到绝对贫困。

entries.definition: Scarcity is a short supply of a particular resource and is the general form of the resource sense.
entries.definitionCN: 稀缺指某种资源供应不足，是资源义的一般化形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin base, real relatives and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: The Latin base means poor, and the abstract ending turns it into the state of being poor.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根意为贫穷，抽象后缀把它变成「贫穷的状态」。

normal.en: The everyday adjective and the formal noun belong to the same family.
normal.cn: 日常形容词与正式名词属于同一词族。

normal.en: Fixed phrases carry the measured sense: poverty line, relative poverty, extreme poverty.
normal.cn: 固定说法承载测量义：贫困线、相对贫困、极端贫困。

normal.en: The same word can describe thin soil or a thin argument, because both are forms of not having enough.
normal.cn: 同一个词既能形容贫瘠的土壤，也能形容单薄的论证，因为两者都是「不够」。

normal.en: Religious tradition added the voluntary sense: a vow of poverty is a choice, not a misfortune.
normal.cn: 宗教传统加上自愿义：守贫之愿是选择，而非不幸。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl that is always half empty, however often it is filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗，无论添多少次，总有一半是空的。

abstract.en: Picture a field that grows grass but never grain.
abstract.cn: 想象一块地只长草，从不结粮。

abstract.en: Picture a room full of furniture and still somehow bare.
abstract.cn: 想象一间堆满家具却仍显得空荡的屋子。

examples.en: The programme cut poverty among older people by raising the basic pension.
examples.cn: 该项目通过提高基本养老金减少了老年人的贫困。

examples.en: Poverty of data made the report's conclusions uncertain.
examples.cn: 数据的匮乏让报告的结论难以确定。

examples.en: She took a vow of poverty and gave away her inheritance.
examples.cn: 她立下守贫之愿，把继承的财产捐了出去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破屋」——屋顶漏风、米缸见底，就是贫穷；记住「破」与「贫」的连带感

root: 拉丁 pauper「贫穷」经古法语进入英语，加上抽象名词后缀构成 paupertas「贫穷、匮乏」，再演变为今天的贫穷一词；pauper 的拉丁语之前来源不确定，相关词根联系多为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shortage: money is missing, then the condition persists, is counted, is extended to resources, to soil, to thought, to chosen humility and finally to total destitution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种「短缺」展开：先是缺钱，继而状态持续、被计数，再扩展到资源、土壤、思想、自愿的谦卑，最后到一无所有。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty bowl on a broken table, with thin grass outside and an empty coal sack by the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：缺角桌上的空碗，窗外稀疏的草，门边空着的煤袋。

branches.en: THE SHORTAGE ITSELF: money is missing, and the lack settles into a lasting condition.
branches.cn: 短缺本身：钱不够，而且这种缺乏沉淀为持久状态。

branches.en: THE COUNT: a line is drawn and the condition becomes an official number.
branches.cn: 计数：画一条线，处境就变成官方数字。

branches.en: FROM MONEY TO MATERIAL: the same thinness describes a scarce resource and barren soil.
branches.cn: 从钱到物：同一种「薄」也能形容短缺的资源与贫瘠的土壤。

branches.en: THIN THOUGHT: an argument can be as poor as a field.
branches.cn: 单薄的思想：论证可以像田地一样贫瘠。

branches.en: CHOSEN AND TOTAL LACK: lack becomes a vow at one end and destitution at the other.
branches.cn: 自愿的与彻底的缺乏：一端是守贫之愿，另一端是赤贫。

intro.en: Poverty is a Latin abstract noun that grew a wide metaphorical reach in English, from money to soil to ideas.
intro.cn: 贫穷是一个拉丁抽象名词，在英语里长出了很宽的比喻范围，从金钱到土壤再到思想。

latinIntro.en: Pauper and paupertas supply the core; English added the adjective, the verb and several compounds.
latinIntro.cn: pauper 与 paupertas 提供核心，英语再加形容词、动词与若干复合词。

items.exampleCN: 贫穷让这家人挤在一个房间。

items.exampleCN: 最贫困的家庭缺少取暖。

items.example: Debt impoverished the whole district.
items.exampleCN: 债务使整个城区陷入贫困。

items.example: The soil was impoverished by years of planting.
items.exampleCN: 连年种植使土壤贫瘠。

items.example: Impoverishment followed the closure of the mine.
items.exampleCN: 矿井关闭后出现了贫困化。

items.example: Aid reached the poverty-stricken villages late.
items.exampleCN: 援助很晚才到达饱受贫困之苦的村庄。

items.example: A paucity of evidence weakened the case.
items.exampleCN: 证据不足削弱了论点。

definition_zh: 艺术作品；（书刊、广告中的）插图与图稿；美术品
definition_en: a work of art, especially a painting, drawing or sculpture, or the illustrations and graphic material prepared for publication
core_image: 一块被反复修改的表面，最后以固定的形状离开工作室，进入别人的眼睛
scene: 印刷厂里，编辑把封面图的文件放大，逐条检查线条。 The editor enlarged the artwork to check every line before the press run.
sceneCN: 这里 artwork 指「交给印刷厂的成稿图稿」（第 4 个义项：可供制版复制的图形材料）；句意为编辑把封面图稿放大，在开印前逐条检查线条。

pos.zh: 艺术作品（可数）；插图、图稿（不可数或可数）；美术品

collocations.zh: 封面图稿；封面艺术设计

derivatives.zh: artwork + -ed（分词形容词）→ 经过图稿加工的；从「成品」转到「加工状态」
artwork + -er（人）→ 图稿制作员；从「成品」转到「制作成品的人」
artwork + -ing（动作）→ 图稿制作；从「物件」转到「工序」

senses.title: A single work of art
senses.definition: a painting, drawing, sculpture or similar piece made as art
senses.definitionCN: 作为艺术品创作的绘画、素描、雕塑或类似作品
senses.example: The museum bought the artwork at auction.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆在拍卖会上买下了这件艺术作品。
senses.why: Artwork is simply art plus work, so the compound names a made thing belonging to the category of art: one countable object.
senses.whyCN: artwork 就是 art 加 work，复合词命名一件属于艺术类别的制成品：一个可数的物件。

senses.title: An artist's output as a whole
senses.titleCN: 某位艺术家的全部作品
senses.definition: the collected pieces made by one artist, treated as a body of work
senses.definitionCN: 某位艺术家创作的全部作品，作为一个整体来看
senses.example: The retrospective gathered artwork from forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这场回顾展汇集了四十年的作品。
senses.why: The uncountable use drops the count and keeps the material: the same word now names the whole body rather than one piece.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法取消了计数，只保留「作品实体」：同一个词现在指整个作品群，而不是单件。

senses.title: Illustrations in a publication
senses.definition: the pictures and drawings prepared to accompany printed text
senses.definitionCN: 为配合印刷文字而准备的图画与插图
senses.example: The novel's artwork was drawn by a single illustrator.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的插图全部由一位插画师绘制。
senses.why: Publishing borrowed the word because illustrations are art made to work inside a page: the aesthetic object becomes part of a printed job.
senses.whyCN: 出版业借用这个词，因为插图是「在页面里工作的艺术」：审美对象成了印刷品的一部分。

senses.title: Print-ready graphic material
senses.definition: the finished graphic material supplied to a printer for reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 交给印刷厂用于复制的完成图形材料
senses.example: The editor enlarged the artwork to check every line before the press run.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把封面图稿放大，在开印前逐条检查线条。
senses.why: In the print trade the word narrows to what the press needs: not the idea but the camera-ready surface from which copies are made.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷业中，这个词收窄为印刷机所需之物：不是构思，而是用来复制的那块可制版表面。

senses.title: A digital image or file
senses.definition: an image or layered file made and stored on a computer
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机上制作并保存的图像或分层文件
senses.example: Keep the layered artwork so the type can be changed later.
senses.exampleCN: 保留分层图稿，以便日后修改文字。
senses.why: When production moved to screens, artwork named the editable file rather than the physical surface; the material changed, the function did not.
senses.whyCN: 当制作转移到屏幕上，artwork 指的可编辑文件而非实体表面；材料变了，功能没变。

senses.title: Decoration on a product or package
senses.titleCN: 产品与包装上的装饰图案
senses.definition: the designed pictures or patterns printed on an object or its packaging
senses.definitionCN: 印在物件或其包装上的设计图案
senses.example: The biscuit tin's artwork copies a Victorian print.
senses.exampleCN: 饼干盒上的图案模仿了一幅维多利亚时期的版画。
senses.why: Commercial design applies the print sense to packaging: the image still exists to be reproduced, but now it sells the object beneath it.
senses.whyCN: 商业设计把印刷义用到包装上：图像仍为复制而存在，只是现在用来推销它下面的商品。

senses.title: Visual design for a screen work
senses.titleCN: 影视、游戏等作品的视觉设计
senses.definition: the visual design of a film, game or performance, including concept pieces
senses.definitionCN: 电影、游戏或演出中的视觉设计，包括概念图
senses.example: The game's artwork borrows from woodblock prints.
senses.exampleCN: 这款游戏的视觉设计借鉴了木版画。
senses.why: The word follows images into new media: concept drawings and textures are artworks made to serve a larger screened work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词跟着图像进入新媒介：概念图与贴图都是为更大的屏幕作品服务的图稿。

senses.title: The original object, not a copy
senses.definition: the physical piece made by the artist, as opposed to a reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家亲手制作的实体作品，区别于复制品
senses.example: Collectors pay for the artwork itself, not the poster.
senses.exampleCN: 收藏者付钱买的是原作本身，而不是海报。
senses.why: Because artwork names the made object, museums and dealers use it to insist on the original surface rather than its image.
senses.whyCN: 因为 artwork 命名的是被制作出来的物件，博物馆与画商便用它强调原初表面，而非其图像复制。

intro.en: Artwork is an English compound of art and work, recorded from 1847 and possibly modelled on German Kunstwerk; both parts are old, but the compound is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: artwork 是 art 与 work 的英语复合词，1847 年有记录，可能以德语 Kunstwerk 为模板；两部分都很古老，复合词却是现代产物。年代均为约数。

items.en: Art goes back through Old French to Latin ars, artis 'skill, craft', whose deeper root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: art 经古法语上溯拉丁 ars、artis「技艺、手艺」，其更早词根属重构。

items.en: Work descends from Old English weorc 'deed, something made', from Proto-Germanic *werka- and the root *werg- 'to do'.
items.cn: work 来自古英语 weorc「行为、制成之物」，上溯原始日耳曼语 *werka- 与词根 *werg-「做」。

items.en: German Kunstwerk 'work of art' joins Kunst 'art' and Werk 'work'; the English compound may have followed this model, though the model is not certain.
items.cn: 德语 Kunstwerk「艺术作品」由 Kunst「艺术」与 Werk「作品」合成；英语复合词可能沿此模板，但模板本身并不确定。

items.en: Art-work is recorded in 1847 in the sense 'artistic work; paintings, drawings and similar pieces'.
items.cn: art-work 于 1847 年有记录，意为「艺术性的作品；绘画、素描一类」。

items.en: In twentieth-century printing, artwork narrowed to the finished graphic material from which copies are reproduced.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪的印刷业，artwork 收窄为可供复制成品的图形材料。

items.en: From the late twentieth century the word also names editable image files, extending the old print sense to screens.
items.cn: 从 20 世纪后期起，这个词也指可编辑的图像文件，把旧的印刷义延伸到屏幕。

note.en: Group one separates artwork from art- words that look close but name very different things; group two separates it from words for pictures and designs in other trades.
note.cn: 第一组把 artwork 与看似接近、实则所指完全不同的 art- 词分开；第二组把它与其他行当中表示图画与设计的词分开。

entries.definition: The two-word spelling usually means 'work done in or for art', a task or labour, not a countable piece.
entries.definitionCN: 分写形式通常指「为艺术所做的工作」，是一种劳动或事务，而非可数作品。

entries.definition: An object made by human hands, especially one of archaeological interest; its value lies in evidence, not beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 人手制作的物件，尤指有考古意义的器物；其价值在于证据性，而非美。

entries.definition: A clever made device or a cunning trick; it shares the art- stem but carries deception, not display.
entries.definitionCN: 精巧的装置或狡黠的计谋；同出 art- 词干，却带欺骗而非展示之意。

entries.definition: Skilful in a calculating way; it describes a manner, while artwork names a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 以算计的方式机巧；描述一种方式，而 artwork 命名一个物件。

entries.definition: A picture made to explain or decorate a text; it is a functional category, while artwork can stand alone.
entries.definitionCN: 为解释或装饰文字而作的图画；是功能类别，而 artwork 可以独立存在。

entries.definition: A visual element in design or printing, often commercial; artwork is the broader term that may include fine pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 设计或印刷中的视觉元素，常指商业图形；artwork 更广，可包含纯艺术作品。

entries.definition: A casual word for one work in a gallery or studio; artwork is the explicit term used in catalogues and contracts.
entries.definitionCN: 画廊或工作室中对单件作品的随口说法；artwork 是图录与合同中的明确用语。

entries.definition: The arrangement or plan behind an object; artwork stresses the finished visual surface rather than the planning.
entries.definitionCN: 物件背后的安排或方案；artwork 强调完成的视觉表面，而非计划过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: art + work: a made thing in the category of art.
normal.cn: art + work：艺术类别中的一件制成品。

normal.en: The compound is recorded from 1847 and may follow German Kunstwerk, literally 'art-work'.
normal.cn: 这个复合词 1847 年有记录，可能仿照德语 Kunstwerk，字面就是「艺术-作品」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: original artwork, cover artwork, send artwork to the printer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：原作、封面图稿、把图稿交给印刷厂。

normal.en: The family runs art, work, artwork, artworks and the trade verb artworking.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 art、work、artwork、artworks 以及行业动词 artworking。

normal.en: A printer asks for 'the artwork' when it needs the file, not the framed picture.
normal.cn: 印刷厂要「the artwork」时，要的是文件，不是装框的画。

abstract.en: Picture a surface that keeps the marks of every decision made on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块保留着每一次修改痕迹的表面。

abstract.en: Picture an object that leaves the studio and begins a life in other people's eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一件物品离开工作室，开始在别人的目光里过日子。

abstract.en: Picture a file and a framed canvas answering to the same name.
abstract.cn: 想象一个文件与一幅装框画布回应着同一个名字。

examples.en: The auction catalogue lists every artwork with its provenance.
examples.cn: 拍卖图录列出每件作品及其来源。

examples.en: The magazine's artwork was finished two weeks before the issue closed.
examples.cn: 杂志的图稿在截稿前两周就完成了。

examples.en: She keeps the original artwork in a flat file, away from light.
examples.cn: 她把原作平放在抽屉柜里，避开光线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「art（艺术）+ work（作品）」——艺术做出来的活儿 → 艺术作品

root: art 来自拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺」；work 来自古英语 weorc「所做之事、制成品」，上溯原始日耳曼语 *werka-。二者在 1847 年合为 artwork，可能仿德语 Kunstwerk。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the object from the gallery wall to the printed page, the packaging and the screen, and finally back to the original surface that copies cannot replace.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让这件物品从画廊墙面走到印刷页、包装与屏幕，最后回到复制品无法替代的原作表面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface is revised again and again until it leaves the studio as a fixed shape and enters other people's eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块表面被反复修改，直到以固定形状离开工作室，进入别人的眼睛。

branches.en: THE OBJECT AND THE ORIGINAL: one countable piece, and the insistence that it is not a copy.
branches.cn: 物件与原作：一件可数作品，以及对「它不是复制品」的坚持。

branches.en: THE OEUVRE: the same word without a count gathers a whole life's making.
branches.cn: 作品群：去掉计数后，同一个词收拢一生的创作。

branches.en: THE PRINTED PAGE: illustration first, then the material handed to the press.
branches.cn: 印刷页：先是插图，再是交给印刷机的材料。

branches.en: THE FILE: the editable image inherits the print function on a screen.
branches.cn: 文件：可编辑图像在屏幕上继承了印刷功能。

branches.en: COMMERCIAL SURFACES: packaging and screen works put the image to work.
branches.cn: 商业表面：包装与屏幕作品让图像去干活。

intro.en: Artwork is a transparent English compound, so both halves can be read separately, and each half has its own family.
intro.cn: artwork 是一个透明的英语复合词，两半都能单独读，而且各自都有自己的词族。

latinIntro.en: Only the first half has a Latin ancestor, ars; the second half is native Germanic, and the compound itself is modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前半有拉丁祖先 ars；后半是日耳曼本族词，复合词本身则是现代英语的产物。

items.example: Art supplies the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: art 提供这个复合词的前半。

items.example: Work supplies the second half.
items.exampleCN: work 提供后半。

items.example: The gallery hung the artwork badly.
items.exampleCN: 画廊把这件作品挂得很糟。

items.example: The crate held six artworks.
items.exampleCN: 箱子里装了六件作品。

items.example: The artworker fixed the spacing before printing.
items.exampleCN: 图稿制作员在印刷前调整了字距。

items.example: Artworking took longer than the design.
items.exampleCN: 图稿制作比设计本身更耗时。

items.example: The phrase is older than the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语比复合词更古老。

items.example: The dig catalogued every artefact.
items.exampleCN: 发掘记录了每一件器物。

items.example: The artisan signed the table.
items.exampleCN: 工匠在桌上签了名。

definition_zh: 衰老；老化；（细胞的）衰老状态；老年期
definition_en: the process or state of growing old, especially the biological decline of cells and organisms
core_image: 一片由绿转黄的银杏叶，叶脉清晰，叶柄旁放着一枚放大镜
scene: 公园的银杏林里，叶子由绿转黄，管理员蹲下捡起一片开始褪色的叶子夹进标本册。 Autumn senescence turns the whole grove gold before the leaves drop.
sceneCN: 这里指植物与叶片的衰老（第 4 个义项：叶片在脱落前发生的有序衰退）；句意为秋天的衰老过程让整片林子转黄，之后叶子才落下。图中可辨识物件：银杏叶、叶脉、标本册、放大镜。

pos.zh: 名词：不可数，指衰老的过程或状态；生物学中特指细胞停止分裂的状态

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示「正在……的」词尾构成，义为「衰老的；老化的」
去掉名词词尾得到的动词，义为「变老；开始衰老」
同一词根经另一形容词路径形成的名词，义为「衰老；老态」
同一词根的形容词，义为「年老的；老年性的」
由表示「免疫」的成分加本词构成，义为「免疫衰老」
由本词加表示「溶解、清除」的成分构成，指清除衰老细胞的药物

senses.title: Cellular senescence
senses.definition: a stable state in which a cell stops dividing but remains alive and secretes signalling molecules
senses.definitionCN: 细胞停止分裂却仍然存活、并分泌信号分子的稳定状态
senses.example: Cellular senescence is marked by a permanent exit from the cell cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞衰老的标志是永久退出细胞周期。
senses.why: The word names a controlled programme, not passive wear, which is why biology adopted it for cells that refuse to divide.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一套受控程序而非被动磨损，因此生物学用它指拒绝分裂的细胞。

senses.title: Organismal ageing
senses.definition: the gradual loss of function that living things undergo as they grow older
senses.definitionCN: 生物随年龄增长而逐渐丧失功能的过程
senses.example: Senescence in the whole organism brings a steady loss of reserve capacity.
senses.exampleCN: 整个机体的衰老带来储备能力的逐步丧失。
senses.why: At the level of the body the word covers every system at once, from skin to kidney.
senses.whyCN: 在身体层面，这个词同时涵盖从皮肤到肾脏的每一个系统。

senses.title: Replicative senescence
senses.definition: the permanent arrest that cells enter after a fixed number of divisions, known as the Hayflick limit
senses.definitionCN: 细胞在完成固定次数分裂后进入的永久停滞，即海弗利克极限
senses.example: Replicative senescence was shown by growing fibroblasts until they stopped dividing.
senses.exampleCN: 复制性衰老是通过培养成纤维细胞直到其停止分裂而得到证明的。
senses.why: Counting divisions gave ageing a measurable clock, and the word became the name of that clock's end.
senses.whyCN: 计数分裂次数为衰老提供了可测量的钟表，这个词就成了那只钟走到尽头的名称。

senses.title: Plant and leaf senescence
senses.definition: the ordered breakdown of a leaf or whole plant before it sheds parts or dies back
senses.definitionCN: 叶片或整株植物在脱落或枯死之前发生的有序分解
senses.example: Autumn senescence turns the whole grove gold before the leaves drop.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天的衰老过程让整片林子转黄，随后叶子才落下。
senses.why: In plants the process is scheduled and nutrient-recycling, so the word carries no sense of failure.
senses.whyCN: 在植物身上这一过程是有计划的养分回收，因此这个词不含「衰败」的贬义。

senses.title: Demographic senescence
senses.definition: the rising share of elderly people within a population
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中老年人所占比例不断上升
senses.example: Demographic senescence has reshaped the country's labour market.
senses.exampleCN: 人口老龄化重塑了该国的劳动力市场。
senses.why: Demography borrowed the biological noun to describe what happens when a whole population grows older.
senses.whyCN: 人口学借用这个生物学名词，描述整个人口变老时发生的事。

senses.title: Senescence in disease
senses.definition: the accumulation of senescent cells that drive inflammation and chronic disease
senses.definitionCN: 衰老细胞的堆积推动炎症与慢性疾病
senses.example: Senescence in the tissue is now treated as a target for new drugs.
senses.exampleCN: 组织中的衰老现象如今被视为新药的靶点。
senses.why: Once senescent cells were linked to illness, the word moved from description to a medical target.
senses.whyCN: 当衰老细胞与疾病建立联系后，这个词便从描述变成了医学靶点。

senses.title: Old age as a stage
senses.definition: the later part of life, described in formal or literary writing
senses.definitionCN: 人生的后期阶段，多用于正式或文学性表达
senses.example: The essay describes senescence as a season rather than a single hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把老年期描述成一个季节，而不是一个时辰。
senses.why: Before biology claimed the word, it simply meant the state of being old, and that literary sense survives.
senses.whyCN: 在生物学占用这个词之前，它只表示年老的状态，这一文学义至今仍在。

senses.title: Institutional senescence
senses.definition: the loss of adaptability in an organisation that has stopped renewing itself
senses.definitionCN: 组织停止自我更新后失去适应能力
senses.example: Institutional senescence set in once the same committee approved everything.
senses.exampleCN: 自从同一个委员会审批所有事项，机构的老化就开始了。
senses.why: Organisations age in a recognisable way, so the biological noun is applied to them by analogy.
senses.whyCN: 组织会以可辨识的方式变老，因此人们用类比把这个生物学名词用到了它们身上。

senses.title: Immunosenescence
senses.definition: the age-related decline in the immune system's ability to respond to new threats
senses.definitionCN: 免疫系统随年龄增长而对新威胁反应减弱
senses.example: Immunosenescence explains why older patients respond less well to some vaccines.
senses.exampleCN: 免疫衰老解释了为何年长患者对某些疫苗反应较弱。
senses.why: A single branch of the immune system ages on its own schedule, and the compound names it precisely.
senses.whyCN: 免疫系统中有一个分支按自己的时间表衰老，这个复合词精确地命名了它。

intro.en: The word comes from Latin senescere, to begin to grow old, built on senex, an old man. The Latin source is clear; the exact year the English noun entered use is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语中表示「开始变老」的动词，其根是表示「老人」的名词。拉丁来源清楚，英语名词进入使用的确切年份为约数。

items.en: Senex meant an old man and stands behind senior and senate as well.
items.cn: 这个词指老年男子，也是「年长的」与「元老院」等词的根源。

items.en: The verb added an inceptive ending to mean to begin to grow old, stressing the start of the process.
items.cn: 这个动词加上表示「开始」的词尾，意为「开始变老」，强调过程的起点。

items.en: The abstract noun named the process itself rather than the person who undergoes it.
items.cn: 这个抽象名词命名的是过程本身，而非经历过程的人。

items.en: English adopted the noun in the seventeenth century for the state of being old.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，用来表示年老的状态。

items.en: Twentieth-century biology narrowed the word to a programmed process with measurable steps.
items.cn: 二十世纪的生物学把词义收窄为有可测步骤的程序性过程。

items.en: When cells were found to stop dividing for good, the same noun was attached to that arrest.
items.cn: 当人们发现细胞会永久停止分裂，同一个名词便被用到了这种停滞上。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root senex; the second group names ageing and decline in plainer words.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「老人」的拉丁词根；第二组是用更朴素的词表示衰老与衰退。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning growing old or having stopped dividing.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「正在变老」或「已停止分裂」的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to begin to grow old.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「开始变老」的动词。

entries.definition: The state of being old, often with weakened mental powers.
entries.definitionCN: 年老的状态，常含心智衰退之意。

entries.definition: Old and showing the effects of age.
entries.definitionCN: 年老的并显出衰老影响。

entries.definition: Older or higher in rank.
entries.definitionCN: 年长的或级别较高的。

entries.definition: The process of growing older.
entries.definitionCN: 变老的过程。

entries.definition: A gradual loss of strength or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 力量或质量的逐渐下降。

entries.definition: The process of becoming worse.
entries.definitionCN: 变得更差的过程。

entries.definition: The later part of a person's life.
entries.definitionCN: 人生的后期。

entries.definition: Shrinking and drying up, as a plant does.
entries.definitionCN: 像植物那样萎缩干枯。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the leaf, the cell and the population; abstract ones treat senescence as a scheduled programme rather than a breakdown.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着叶片、细胞与人群展开；抽象联想把衰老看作被安排好的程序而非崩坏。

normal.en: A leaf yellows on schedule, and that schedule is senescence.
normal.cn: 叶子按时变黄，这个时间表就是衰老。

normal.en: A cell that stops dividing but stays alive is senescent.
normal.cn: 停止分裂却仍活着的细胞就是衰老细胞。

normal.en: The Hayflick limit is the cell's built-in countdown.
normal.cn: 海弗利克极限就是细胞自带的倒计时。

normal.en: An ageing population is senescence written at the scale of a country.
normal.cn: 人口老龄化就是把衰老写到一个国家的尺度上。

normal.en: The immune system ages too, and the compound is immunosenescence.
normal.cn: 免疫系统也会衰老，这个复合词就是免疫衰老。

abstract.en: Senescence is not damage; it is a programme that damage can accelerate.
abstract.cn: 衰老不是损伤本身，而是一套可被损伤加速的程序。

abstract.en: Every system that renews itself must also decide when to stop.
abstract.cn: 每个能自我更新的系统都必须决定何时停止。

abstract.en: Ageing is the price of having a schedule at all.
abstract.cn: 变老，是拥有时间表所付出的代价。

examples.en: Senescence is now studied as an active programme rather than simple wear.
examples.cn: 衰老如今被当作主动程序而非单纯磨损来研究。

examples.en: The forest showed clear signs of senescence after the dry decade.
examples.cn: 干旱十年之后，这片森林显出明显的衰老迹象。

examples.en: Researchers now treat senescence as a target rather than an inevitable fate.
examples.cn: 研究人员如今把衰老当作可干预的目标，而非不可改变的归宿。

dict_mnemonic.text: sen（老）+ escence（开始成为）——开始变老：衰老

root: 来自拉丁语 senescere「开始变老」，其根为 senex「老人」，与 senior、senate 同源。拉丁来源清楚，英语名词约在十七世纪进入使用，确切年份不确定；二十世纪后词义收窄为生物学的程序性衰老。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses carry one root meaning of growing old across cells, bodies, leaves, populations, institutions and the immune system.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项把「变老」这一词根含义贯穿细胞、身体、叶片、人群、机构与免疫系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a yellowing leaf with a visible vein map and a lens beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片正在变黄的叶子，叶脉清晰，旁边放着放大镜。

branches.en: THE CELLULAR CORE: a permanent exit from division, reached after a counted number of cycles.
branches.cn: 细胞内核：永久退出分裂，且发生在计数过的若干循环之后。

branches.en: THE WHOLE BODY: every organ losing reserve at once.
branches.cn: 整个身体：每个器官同时失去储备。

branches.en: THE PLANT VERSION: an ordered breakdown that recycles nutrients before shedding.
branches.cn: 植物版本：脱落前发生的有序分解并回收养分。

branches.en: THE HUMAN ARC: a population growing older and a single life reaching its late stage.
branches.cn: 人类弧线：人口整体变老，以及单条生命进入晚期。

branches.en: THE TARGETS: senescent cells in disease, institutions losing adaptability, and an ageing immune system.
branches.cn: 靶点层面：疾病中的衰老细胞、失去适应力的机构，以及衰老的免疫系统。

intro.en: One Latin root, senex, yields a verb of growing old, an abstract noun and a family of adjectives.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁词根「老人」衍生出表示变老的动词、抽象名词以及一组形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the noun of age, the inceptive verb and the adjective of old age; English adds the abstract ending and later compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示年老的名称、表示开始变老的动词与老年形容词；英语加上抽象名词词尾，后来又构成复合词。

items.example: The root also stands behind words for elders and councils of elders.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也藏在表示长者与长者议事会的词背后。

items.example: The inceptive ending stresses the start of ageing.
items.exampleCN: 表示「开始」的词尾强调衰老的起点。

items.example: The abstract noun passed into English as senescence.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词以「衰老」的形式进入英语。

items.example: It supplies the English adjectives for senile conditions.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了英语中表示老年性状态的形容词。

items.example: It marks a process that has started but not finished.
items.exampleCN: 它标记已经开始但尚未完成的过程。

items.example: It turns the participle into the name of a state.
items.exampleCN: 它把分词变成状态名称。

items.example: The adjective keeps the inceptive sense of starting to age.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词保留了「开始变老」的起始含义。

items.example: The verb is a back formation from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是从名词逆构出来的。

items.example: A modern compound joins immunity to the old noun.
items.exampleCN: 一个现代复合词把免疫与这个古老名词连在一起。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示「正在……的」词尾构成，义为「衰老的；老化的」
去掉名词词尾得到的动词，义为「变老；开始衰老」
同一词根经另一形容词路径形成的名词，义为「衰老；老态」
同一词根的形容词，义为「年老的；老年性的」
由表示「免疫」的成分加本词构成，义为「免疫衰老」
由本词加表示「溶解、清除」的成分构成，指清除衰老细胞的药物

definition_zh: 与……一致；与……相符；符合；与……相合；与……相称
definition_en: to agree with or match something such as evidence, a rule, a style or a forecast, so that no contradiction arises
core_image: 两张坐标纸叠在一起，一条曲线来自仪器记录，另一条来自推算，笔尖停在两线完全重合的位置
scene: 实验室的灯一直亮着，值班的人把温度记录纸与模拟输出并排铺在桌上，发现两条曲线的起伏几乎一模一样。 Every reading in the log must be consistent with the simulation before the report is signed.
sceneCN: 这里指观测数据与模拟结果相合（第 1 个义项：与实测证据相符）；句意为在报告签字之前，日志里的每一次读数都必须与模拟结果相符。图中可辨识物件：温度记录纸、模拟曲线、签字笔、封存袋。

pos.zh: 与……一致；符合（系表结构，时态由系动词承担，后接名词、代词或名词性从句）
与……相称（后接风格、身份、惯例等抽象名词）

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「一致性；前后一贯」
去掉系动词后的形容词原形，义为「一致的；相符的」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「一贯地；始终如一地」
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「不一致的；自相矛盾的」
由否定前缀加名词尾构成，义为「不一致之处」

senses.title: Matching the evidence
senses.definition: to agree with the observed data or the recorded facts
senses.definitionCN: 与观测到的数据或已记录的事实相合
senses.example: Any explanation of the anomaly must be consistent with every measurement taken that night.
senses.exampleCN: 对这一异常的任何解释，都必须与当晚取到的每一次测量相符。
senses.why: The core verb meant to stand together; a claim that stands together with the data is a claim the data will not knock down.
senses.whyCN: 核心动词本义是「站在一起」；一个能与数据站在一起的说法，就是数据推不倒的说法。

senses.title: Following the same rule
senses.definition: to comply with an established rule, code or standard
senses.definitionCN: 遵守既定的规则、规范或标准
senses.example: All new buildings should be consistent with the city's safety code.
senses.exampleCN: 所有新建房屋都应与该市的安全规范相符。
senses.why: Rules are written to hold across many cases, so a single case that fits them can stand beside every other case.
senses.whyCN: 规则要能覆盖许多情形，因此与规则相合的单个情形，可以和其余情形并排站住。

senses.title: Not contradicting itself
senses.definition: to be internally coherent, with no part denying another
senses.definitionCN: 内部自洽，没有任何一部分否定另一部分
senses.example: A sound argument must be consistent with its own premises from the first line to the last.
senses.exampleCN: 一个可靠的论证必须从第一行到最后一行都与自身的前提保持一致。
senses.why: Standing together also means standing together with oneself: the parts of a statement must not pull apart.
senses.whyCN: 「站在一起」也包括与自己站在一起：一个说法的各部分不能各自扯开。

senses.title: Compatible with another theory
senses.definition: to be able to coexist with another account without contradiction
senses.definitionCN: 能与另一种解释共存而不产生矛盾
senses.example: The two models can be consistent with each other only if the second assumption is dropped.
senses.exampleCN: 只有放弃第二个假设，这两个模型才可能与彼此相容。
senses.why: Two accounts are compatible when both can stand on the same ground; where they cannot, one must give way.
senses.whyCN: 两种解释能站在同一块地面上才叫相容；站不住的时候，必须有一方让位。

senses.title: In keeping with a style or character
senses.definition: to match the tone, manner or character of something
senses.definitionCN: 与某物的格调、做法或气质相配
senses.example: The plain wooden benches should be consistent with the meeting house's austere style.
senses.exampleCN: 那些素木长凳应当与聚会所的简朴风格相称。
senses.why: Style is a kind of standing together too: each detail must stand beside the others without looking borrowed.
senses.whyCN: 风格也是一种站在一起：每个细节都要与其余细节并排而不显得是借来的。

senses.title: In line with past practice
senses.definition: to follow the custom or precedent set by earlier decisions
senses.definitionCN: 沿用早先决定所立下的惯例或先例
senses.example: The committee's ruling will be consistent with its decisions over the past decade.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会的裁决将与其过去十年的决定保持一致。
senses.why: Custom is continuity over time: a new decision stands together with the old ones, or the record looks broken.
senses.whyCN: 惯例是时间上的连续：新决定要与旧决定站在一起，否则记录就显得断裂。

senses.title: Within the allowed tolerance
senses.definition: to fall inside the permitted range of variation for a measurement
senses.definitionCN: 测量值处在允许的变动范围之内
senses.example: A shaft that is slightly oval may still be consistent with the tolerance band.
senses.exampleCN: 略微呈椭圆的轴，仍可能落在允许的误差带之内。
senses.why: In manufacture, agreement is numeric: the part stands within a band rather than exactly on a line.
senses.whyCN: 在制造中，一致是数值上的：零件只要站进误差带，而不必正好压线。

senses.title: Matching a legal precedent
senses.definition: to be compatible with a constitution, statute or earlier court ruling
senses.definitionCN: 与宪法、成文法或早先判决相兼容
senses.example: The new statute must be consistent with the constitution as interpreted by earlier courts.
senses.exampleCN: 新法规必须与早先法院所解释的宪法条文相符。
senses.why: Law settles disputes by asking whether a new rule can stand beside the old ones without rewriting them.
senses.whyCN: 法律判断争议的方式，是看新规则能否与旧规则并排站住而不必改写旧规则。

senses.title: Matching what was predicted
senses.definition: to agree with a forecast or a calculated expectation
senses.definitionCN: 与预报或推算出的预期相合
senses.example: The cooling curve should be consistent with the model's prediction if the insulation is intact.
senses.exampleCN: 如果保温层完好，冷却曲线就应与模型的预测相符。
senses.why: A prediction is a claim about a curve not yet drawn; agreement means the drawn curve stands where the claim said it would.
senses.whyCN: 预测是对尚未画出的曲线所作的断言；相符意味着画出的曲线站到了断言所说的位置。

intro.en: The phrase is a grammatical frame around the Latin adjective consistent, which descended from the verb meaning to stand together. The frame itself is an English construction, and its first recorded use in academic prose is dated only approximately.
intro.cn: 这个短语是围绕一个拉丁形容词搭起的语法框架，那个形容词出自表示「一起站立」的动词。框架本身是英语的构造，它在学术文章里最早出现的年代只能给约数。

items.en: Sistere meant to stand, to place or to hold one's ground, and it supplied the standing image behind the whole family.
items.cn: 这个词意为「站立、安放、站住脚」，整个词族的「站」的意象都由它提供。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus sistere produced consistere, to stand together, to hold firm, to remain in one place.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的前缀加「站立」，构成「站在一起、立稳、留在原处」的动词。

items.en: The noun named the state of standing firm, and the participle described something that holds its ground.
items.cn: 相应的名词指「立稳的状态」，分词则形容「站得住的东西」。

items.en: English took the adjective by way of French in the sixteenth century, first for things that hold together, then for statements that do not contradict each other.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪经法语引入这个形容词，先指「结实地连在一起的东西」，后指「不自相矛盾的说法」。

items.en: The frame be plus the adjective plus with became the standard way to say that a finding, a rule or a style agrees with something else. The exact first citation of the frame is uncertain.
items.cn: 由系动词、形容词与介词构成的这个框架，成为表示「结论、规则或风格与某物相合」的标准说法。该框架最早的书证年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the same Latin standing root but splits into two unlike meanings; the second group holds ordinary ways of saying that two things agree.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一个拉丁「站立」词根，却分成两个完全不同的意思；第二组是表示「两物相合」的普通说法。

entries.definition: Built on the same verb, it means to be made up of parts, not to agree with something. A report can consist of five chapters and still not be consistent with the evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一个动词构成，意思却是「由部分组成」，并非「与某物一致」。一份报告可以由五章构成，却仍与证据不符。

entries.definition: The bare adjective describes a thing or a set of results that holds together; the phrase adds the second party that it agrees with.
entries.definitionCN: 单独的形容词形容某物或某组结果自身站得住；短语则补出它所相合的那一方。

entries.definition: The noun names the quality of agreement, as in the consistency of the results; it cannot take the whole phrase's object directly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指「一致」这一性质，如结果的一致性；它不能像短语那样直接带出所相合的对象。

entries.definition: The negative adjective says that two things cannot stand together, which is exactly what the phrase denies.
entries.definitionCN: 否定形容词表示两物无法并立，正是这个短语所肯定的反面。

entries.definition: A formal verb phrase for agreeing with facts or principles; it is close in meaning but far less common in quantitative writing.
entries.definitionCN: 正式地表示与事实或原则相合，意思接近，但在定量写作中远不如本短语常用。

entries.definition: Literally to bring into one line; used for plans and interests that point the same way, with less stress on factual proof.
entries.definitionCN: 字面是「排成一条线」，多用于方向、利益一致，对事实证据的强调较弱。

entries.definition: To follow a rule or pattern exactly; it stresses obedience to a standard rather than agreement among findings.
entries.definitionCN: 指严格遵照规则或范式，强调对标准的服从，而不是结论之间的一致。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for two things fitting each other; it is neutral in tone and lacks the phrase's academic register.
entries.definitionCN: 日常表示两物相配的动词，语气中性，没有这个短语的学术语域。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two overlapping curves, the code book, the committee record and the tolerance band.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两条重合的曲线、规范手册、委员会记录与误差带四个场景。

normal.en: Two curves laid on one sheet: where they overlap, the reading agrees with the model.
normal.cn: 两张曲线铺在同一张纸上：重叠之处，读数就与模型相符。

normal.en: A new building checked against the code book, clause by clause.
normal.cn: 新楼对着规范手册，一条一条核对。

normal.en: A statement read twice: the second half must not deny the first.
normal.cn: 一句话读两遍：后半句不能否定前半句。

normal.en: A committee ruling placed beside ten years of earlier rulings.
normal.cn: 把委员会的新裁决，摆到过去十年的旧裁决旁边。

normal.en: A shaft measured against the tolerance band, not against a perfect line.
normal.cn: 量轴时对着误差带，而不是对着一条完美的线。

abstract.en: Agreement is not sameness: two things can differ in shape and still stand together.
abstract.cn: 一致不是相同：两样东西形状不同，仍可以站在一起。

abstract.en: Every field draws a line and then asks which results may stand on it.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都先画一条线，再问哪些结果可以站到线上。

abstract.en: A claim that agrees with everything agrees with nothing in particular.
abstract.cn: 与一切都相符的说法，其实不与任何具体事物相符。

examples.en: The isotope ratio must be consistent with the age assigned to the layer.
examples.cn: 同位素比值必须与该层位所定的年代相符。

examples.en: Her account of the meeting should be consistent with the minutes kept by the secretary.
examples.cn: 她对那次会议的叙述，应与秘书所作的记录一致。

examples.en: A policy can be consistent with the law and still be unpopular.
examples.cn: 一项政策可以合乎法律，却依然不得人心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 肯西斯滕特 威兹」：把「站在一起」记成两条线站到同一条线上——站得齐，才叫一致

root: 核心动词出自拉丁语「一起站立」，由表示「共同」的前缀加表示「站立」的词根构成，本义是「立稳、站得住」，引申为「前后相合」。该短语是英语学术写作的固定框架，由系动词、形容词与介词三层组成，时态由系动词承担。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from proof to propriety: agreement with data, with a rule, with itself, with another theory, with a style, with past practice, with a tolerance band, with precedent, and with a forecast.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从证据走到得体：与数据相符、与规则相符、与自身自洽、与另一理论相容、与风格相称、与旧例一致、落在误差带内、合于判例、与预测相符。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two curves drawn on one sheet, one from an instrument and one from a calculation, meeting along the same line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条曲线画在同一张纸上，一条来自仪器，一条来自推算，沿着同一条线重合。

branches.en: THE DRAWN LINE: a reading or a forecast must land where the claim said it would.
branches.cn: 画出的线：读数或预测必须落在断言所说的位置。

branches.en: THE STANDING RULE: a case fits the written code, or fits the unwritten custom of earlier cases.
branches.cn: 站得住的规则：或合于成文规范，或合于旧例的不成文惯例。

branches.en: THE SELF AND THE OTHER: a statement must not deny its own parts, and two accounts must not deny each other.
branches.cn: 自身与对方：一个说法不能否定自己的各部分，两种解释也不能互相否定。

branches.en: THE SETTING: style and character are agreement of tone rather than of fact.
branches.cn: 场合：风格与身份的一致，是语气上的一致，而非事实上的相符。

branches.en: THE BAND AND THE BENCH: a part sits inside a tolerance band, a statute sits beside earlier rulings.
branches.cn: 误差带与判席：零件站进误差带，法规站到旧判决旁边。

intro.en: This phrase is a Latin standing word inside an English frame; its family covers the verb, the adjective, the noun and their negatives.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语的「站立」之词装进英语框架；词族覆盖动词、形容词、名词及各自的否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin consistere and its noun consistentia supplied the adjective, and English added its own endings around them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「一起站立」动词及其名词提供了形容词的底子，英语又在其外围加上自己的词尾。

items.example: It binds the parts into one standing whole.
items.exampleCN: 它把各部分绑成一个站立的整体。

items.meaning: to stand, to hold one's ground
items.example: The standing image at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这是整个词族中心的「站立」意象。

items.example: The source of the English verb and adjective.
items.exampleCN: 英语动词与形容词的共同来源。

items.example: The stem that English took as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 英语取作形容词的那个词干。

items.example: It turns the stem into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 它把词干变成描述性的词。

items.example: It names the state of standing firm.
items.exampleCN: 它给「立稳的状态」命名。

items.meaningCN: 状态；性质（另一种词尾形式）
items.example: It produces the modern noun of agreement.
items.exampleCN: 它构成现代表示「一致」的名词。

items.example: It reverses the adjective into its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词翻成反义。

items.example: It produces the adverb of manner.
items.exampleCN: 它构成方式副词。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词尾构成，义为「一致性」
形容词原形，义为「一致的」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「一贯地」
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「不一致的」
由否定前缀加名词尾构成，义为「不一致之处」

definition_zh: 突破；重大进展；突破性成果；（军事）突破防线
definition_en: a sudden important advance that gets past a barrier, especially in science, medicine, technology, or the military
core_image: 一堵墙上被撞开的第一道缺口，后面的人由此穿过去
scene: 实验室熬夜三个月后，第一块样品终于通过了测试。 On the lab screen the long-unsolved structure finally resolved, and the team leader said, This is the breakthrough we needed.
sceneCN: 这里 breakthrough 是「重大突破、突破性进展」（第 2 个义项：科研上越过长期障碍）；句意：实验室屏幕上多年无解的结构终于显出清晰轮廓，团队负责人说，这就是他们需要的突破。场景要点：屏幕上的结构图、实验台、团队、记录板。

pos.zh: 突破；重大进展；突破性成果；军事突破

derivatives.zh: 突破；穿透；强行穿过
爆发痛（慢性疼痛治疗中突然发作的剧痛）
突破性感染（接种或服药后仍发生的感染）
突破性技术（名词作定语）

senses.title: Military: a hole forced in a defensive line
senses.titleCN: 军事：在防线中强行打开缺口
senses.definition: a successful advance through an enemy's defensive line, opening a gap for the rest of the force
senses.definitionCN: 成功穿过敌方防线，为其余部队打开缺口
senses.example: The armoured division made a breakthrough at dawn and pushed into open ground.
senses.exampleCN: 装甲师在黎明时突破防线，向开阔地推进。
senses.why: Breakthrough began as a noun from the phrase break through: a line is broken and the force passes through the hole. The earliest recorded modern noun use is military, from the trench warfare of the late 1910s.
senses.whyCN: breakthrough 最初是短语 break through 名词化的结果：防线被打破，部队从缺口穿过去。最早有记录的现代名词用法是军事义，来自 1910 年代后期的堑壕战。

senses.title: Science and technology: an advance past a long barrier
senses.titleCN: 科研与技术：越过长期障碍的进展
senses.definition: a sudden, important advance that solves a problem or removes an obstacle that had blocked work for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 突然而重要的进展，解决了一个问题或清除了长期阻碍工作的障碍
senses.example: The team's breakthrough came when they could finally image the protein's active site.
senses.exampleCN: 当团队终于能成像该蛋白的活性位点时，他们的突破到来了。
senses.why: The military gap becomes an intellectual gap. Something long closed is suddenly open, and work that was stuck can move forward; this transfer is recorded from the 1930s, on the notion of a successful attack.
senses.whyCN: 军事上的缺口变成了知识上的缺口。长期封闭的东西突然打开，卡住的工作得以推进；这一转移自 1930 年代有记录，依托的是“进攻成功”的意象。

senses.title: Medicine: a treatment that changes the outcome
senses.definition: a new drug, test, or procedure that greatly improves the treatment of a disease
senses.definitionCN: 极大改善某种疾病治疗的新药、检测或疗法
senses.example: The drug was hailed as a breakthrough for patients who had run out of options.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药被赞为那些已无其他选择的患者的突破。
senses.why: The barrier here is disease or a failed treatment, and the advance passes through it. Medical writing adopts the word because it captures both the obstacle and the sudden release, keeping the battlefield shape intact.
senses.whyCN: 这里的障碍是疾病或失效的疗法，而进展穿过了它。医学写作采用这个词，因为它同时抓住障碍与突然的解除，并保持战场的形状不变。

senses.title: Personal: breaking a deadlock or limit
senses.definition: a moment when a person gets past a mental block, a deadlock, or a limit that had held them back
senses.definitionCN: 一个人越过心理障碍、僵局或长期限制自己的极限的时刻
senses.example: Learning to speak in public was a personal breakthrough for him.
senses.exampleCN: 学会公开演讲对他而言是一次个人突破。
senses.why: The wall is now inside the person: fear, habit, or a fixed limit. The same shape holds — a barrier is met and passed — which is why the word feels natural outside science and warfare.
senses.whyCN: 墙现在在人的内心：恐惧、习惯或固定极限。形状不变——遇到障碍并越过去——因此这个词用在科学与战争之外也很自然。

senses.title: Business and market: opening a closed door
senses.titleCN: 商业与市场：打开一扇关着的门
senses.definition: a product, deal, or strategy that lets a company enter a new market or reach a new level
senses.definitionCN: 让公司进入新市场或达到新水平的产品、交易或策略
senses.example: The low-cost model was the company's breakthrough into emerging markets.
senses.exampleCN: 低成本模式是这家公司进入新兴市场的突破。
senses.why: A closed market is treated as a wall, and a successful entry as the hole through it. Business English borrows the military image and keeps its force, so entering a market becomes a passage through a barrier.
senses.whyCN: 封闭的市场被当作一堵墙，成功进入就是墙上打开的洞。商业英语借用了军事意象并保留其力度，于是进入市场变成了穿过障碍。

senses.title: Attributive use: breakthrough drug, technology, year
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：突破性药物、技术、年份
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark the thing as the one that produced the advance, as in breakthrough technology
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，标记该事物就是产生突破的那一个，如 breakthrough technology
senses.example: The breakthrough technology cut the cost of sequencing by half.
senses.exampleCN: 这项突破性技术把测序成本降低了一半。
senses.why: The noun is placed before another noun without a suffix, a zero-derived modifier. It names not a general quality but the specific advance that opened the way, so the modifier keeps the concrete event.
senses.whyCN: 名词不加后缀直接放在另一个名词前，构成零派生修饰语。它命名的不是一般性质，而是打开道路的那次具体突破，因此修饰语保留具体事件。

senses.title: Usage boundary: breakthrough versus discovery
senses.definition: a discovery is something found; a breakthrough is a discovery or advance that passes a barrier and changes what can be done next
senses.definitionCN: discovery 是被发现的东西；breakthrough 是越过障碍、改变接下来能做之事的新发现或进展
senses.example: The discovery of the fossil was interesting, but the dating method was the breakthrough.
senses.exampleCN: 发现化石本身很有意思，但真正突破的是测年方法。
senses.why: Discovery names the find; breakthrough adds the wall and the passage. A discovery can be small and still be a discovery, but a breakthrough must change the situation, because the break is part of its meaning.
senses.whyCN: discovery 命名“找到的东西”；breakthrough 额外包含“墙”与“穿过”。发现可以很小仍是发现，而突破必须改变局面，因为“打破”是它意义的一部分。

senses.title: Usage boundary: breakthrough versus advance and progress
senses.definition: advance and progress can be gradual; breakthrough implies a sudden, decisive jump past an obstacle
senses.definitionCN: advance 与 progress 可以是渐进的；breakthrough 暗示突然而决定性地越过障碍
senses.example: Years of steady progress led to one breakthrough.
senses.exampleCN: 多年稳步进展最终带来一次突破。
senses.why: The compound contains break, a sudden verb, so it cannot describe slow improvement. This is why journalists reserve it for the moment the wall gives way, while progress can continue for years.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组含有 break 这个表示突然动作的动词，因此不能描述缓慢改善。这也是记者只把它留给墙崩塌那一刻的原因，而 progress 可以持续多年。

senses.title: Specialized: breakthrough infection and breakthrough pain
senses.titleCN: 专业用法：突破性感染与爆发痛
senses.definition: in medical compounds, breakthrough describes something that gets past a defence, such as a vaccine or a painkiller
senses.definitionCN: 在医学复合词中，breakthrough 描述越过某种防御的东西，如疫苗或止痛药
senses.example: A breakthrough infection occurred in a few vaccinated patients.
senses.exampleCN: 少数已接种患者发生了突破性感染。
senses.why: These compounds use the oldest literal sense: the pathogen or the pain breaks through the defence that was supposed to hold it. The barrier is medical, but the image is unchanged, so the noun keeps its military geometry.
senses.whyCN: 这些复合词用的是最古老的字面义：病原体或疼痛突破了本应拦住它的防线。障碍是医学的，但意象没有变，因此名词保留了军事几何。

intro.en: Breakthrough is not a Latin derivative. It is the English phrase break through turned into a noun: two native Old English words, a verb of breaking and a word of passing through, welded into one compound. Etymonline dates the noun to 1918 in a military sense; the exact first occurrence is uncertain.
intro.cn: breakthrough 不是拉丁派生词。它是英语短语 break through 名词化的结果：两个本土古英语词——表示“打破”的动词与表示“穿过”的词——焊合为一个复合词。etymonline 把名词的军事义定在 1918 年；确切的最早出现存疑。

items.en: Break goes back to Old English brecan 'to divide solid matter violently, to burst, to break', from Proto-Germanic *brekanan and PIE root *bhreg- 'to break'. Through goes back to Old English þurh, from Proto-Germanic *thurx and PIE *tere- 'to cross over, pass through, overcome'. Neither word is Latin or Greek.
items.cn: break 上溯古英语 brecan“猛烈分开固体、爆裂、打破”，来自原始日耳曼语 *brekanan 与原始印欧语词根 *bhreg-“打破”。through 上溯古英语 þurh，来自原始日耳曼语 *thurx 与原始印欧语 *tere-“越过、穿过、克服”。两者都不是拉丁语或希腊语。

items.en: The verbal phrase break through is attested from about 1400 in the sense 'overcome or penetrate a barrier'. The verb keeps its sudden force, and the later noun inherits that suddenness.
items.cn: 短语动词 break through 约自 1400 年起有记录，意为“克服或穿透障碍”。动词保留突然的力度，后来的名词继承了这种突然性。

items.en: Etymonline records the noun breakthrough (also written break-through) from 1918, meaning a 'significant or sudden advance', in a military sense. The date fits the trench warfare of the First World War, but the exact first written occurrence is uncertain and may be slightly earlier.
items.cn: etymonline 记录名词 breakthrough（也写作 break-through）自 1918 年起表示军事上的“重大或突然的推进”。这个年代与第一次世界大战的堑壕战相符，但确切的最早书面出现存疑，可能略早。

items.en: The meaning 'abrupt solution or progress' is recorded from the 1930s, on the notion of a successful attack. The wall becomes a research problem, a disease, or a personal limit, and the passage through it becomes a decisive advance.
items.cn: “突然的解决或进展”义自 1930 年代有记录，依托的是“进攻成功”的意象。墙变成研究难题、疾病或个人极限，而穿过墙的通道变成决定性的进展。

items.en: Medicine applied the word to drugs and procedures that change outcomes, and business to products that open new markets. The attributive use, as in breakthrough technology, is a zero-derived modifier with no suffix.
items.cn: 医学把这个词用于改变结局的药物与疗法，商业把它用于打开新市场的产品。breakthrough technology 这类定语用法是零派生修饰语，不加后缀。

items.en: Journalism has inflated the word, so it is often used for any good news. Technical compounds such as breakthrough infection and breakthrough pain keep the strict literal sense of something passing a defence. The noun remains a native English compound, not a borrowed root.
items.cn: 新闻写作把这个词用滥了，常用来指任何好消息。breakthrough infection、breakthrough pain 等技术复合词则保留“某物越过防御”的严格字面义。这个名词始终是本土英语复合词，而不是借来的词根。

note.en: The first group is the same break + particle pattern with different particles and different results; the second separates a breakthrough from a find, a gradual gain, a jump, and a new method.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个 break + 小品词的构词模式，但小品词与结果不同；第二组把突破与发现、渐进增益、跃升及新方法区分开。

entries.definition: The end of a relationship or the splitting of a group. Up here means apart, so the compound is about separation, not passage.
entries.definitionCN: 关系结束或团体分裂。这里的 up 表示“分开”，因此复合词说的是分离，而不是穿过。

entries.definition: An escape from a place or a sudden success that escapes a limited category. Out stresses leaving a container, not crossing a line.
entries.definitionCN: 从某处逃出，或突然脱离某一局限类别的成功。out 强调离开容器，而不是越过一条线。

entries.definition: A failure of a machine, system, or person, or an analysis into parts. Down marks collapse or division, the opposite direction from through.
entries.definitionCN: 机器、系统或人的崩溃，或分解为部分。down 标记崩塌或分解，与 through 的方向相反。

entries.definition: A separation or departure from a group, as in a breakaway faction. Away marks distance from the source, not a passage to the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 从群体中分离或脱离，如 breakaway faction。away 标记远离源头，而不是穿到另一边。

entries.definition: The act of finding something that was already there but unknown. It names the find, while breakthrough names the barrier passed.
entries.definitionCN: 发现原本存在却未知之物的行为。它命名“找到”，而 breakthrough 命名“越过的障碍”。

entries.definition: A forward movement or improvement, often gradual. It lacks the sudden break that breakthrough requires.
entries.definitionCN: 向前的移动或改善，常为渐进。它没有 breakthrough 所要求的突然断裂。

entries.definition: A very large and sudden change, as in a leap in technology. It stresses distance jumped rather than a wall broken.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大而突然的变化，如技术上的 leap。它强调跳过的距离，而不是打破一堵墙。

entries.definition: A new idea, method, or product actually put into use. It stresses novelty and application, not the overcoming of an obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 被实际采用的新想法、方法或产品。它强调新颖与应用，而不是克服障碍。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: break + through, the military gap, and real medical compounds such as breakthrough infection.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：break + through 的构词、军事缺口，以及 breakthrough infection 等真实医学复合词。

normal.en: break + through: first a wall is broken, then people pass through the hole. The noun keeps both halves of that action.
normal.cn: break + through：先打破一堵墙，再有人从洞里穿过去。名词同时保留这一动作的两半。

normal.en: The word grew in the trenches: a breakthrough was a hole in the enemy line, not a clever idea.
normal.cn: 这个词在堑壕里长大：breakthrough 是敌军防线上的一个缺口，而不是一个聪明点子。

normal.en: When a lab says breakthrough, it borrows the trench image: the problem was a wall, and now there is a way through.
normal.cn: 实验室说 breakthrough 时借用了堑壕的意象：问题是一堵墙，现在有路可过了。

normal.en: breakthrough technology is the technology that made the hole; the modifier names the specific advance, not a general quality.
normal.cn: breakthrough technology 就是打出缺口的那个技术；修饰语命名的是具体那次突破，不是一般性质。

normal.en: breakthrough infection is literal: the germ breaks through the vaccine's defence. The old image survives in the clinic.
normal.cn: breakthrough infection 是字面义：病原体突破了疫苗的防线。旧意象在诊室里活了下来。

abstract.en: A wall is not removed; a hole is made. A breakthrough does not erase the obstacle, it creates a passage through it.
abstract.cn: 墙没有被移走，只是被打开一个洞。突破并不消除障碍，而是在障碍上开出一条通路。

abstract.en: Before the break, every step is blocked; after it, the same energy moves freely. The word marks the single instant when the direction changes.
abstract.cn: 在断裂之前，每一步都被挡住；之后，同样的力气自由流动。这个词标记方向改变的那一瞬。

abstract.en: A breakthrough is a door that was not there yesterday: the room behind it was always there, but no one could enter.
abstract.cn: 突破是昨天还不存在的一扇门：门后的房间一直都在，只是没人进得去。

examples.en: The vaccine was the first real breakthrough in the fight against the disease.
examples.cn: 这种疫苗是对抗该疾病的第一项真正突破。

examples.en: Years of failed experiments made the final breakthrough feel sudden.
examples.cn: 多年失败的实验让最后的突破显得很突然。

examples.en: The company's breakthrough into the Japanese market came through a local partner.
examples.cn: 这家公司借本地伙伴实现了进入日本市场的突破。

dict_mnemonic.text: “布雷克思如”——先把墙 break（打破），再 through（穿过去）→ breakthrough 突破

root: 英语本土短语 break through 的名词化；break 来自古英语 brecan“打破”，through 来自古英语 þurh“穿过”。不是拉丁派生，而是“动词 + 方位小品词”的复合。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of breakthrough share one shape: a barrier is broken and something passes through it. The barrier may be a trench line, a research problem, a disease, a personal limit, a closed market, or a vaccine defence.
sensesIntro.cn: breakthrough 的九个义项形状相同：障碍被打破，某物穿过去。障碍可以是战壕防线、研究难题、疾病、个人极限、封闭市场，或疫苗防线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall is broken at one point, and what was blocked can now pass through.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙在某一点被打破，原本被挡住的东西现在可以通过。

branches.en: BATTLE: the literal gap in a defensive line, the historical seed of the word.
branches.cn: 战场：防线上字面的缺口，这个词的历史种子。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE AND CURE: a research problem or a disease becomes the wall that is passed.
branches.cn: 知识与治疗：研究难题或疾病变成被越过的墙。

branches.en: SELF: the barrier moves inside a person, as fear or a fixed limit.
branches.cn: 自我：障碍移到人的内心，成为恐惧或固定极限。

branches.en: MARKET AND MODIFIER: a closed market is a wall, and the breakthrough product is the thing that made the hole.
branches.cn: 市场与定语：封闭市场是一堵墙，而突破性产品就是打出缺口的那个东西。

branches.en: BOUNDARIES: discovery names the find, advance names a gradual step, and medical compounds keep the literal defence.
branches.cn: 边界：discovery 命名发现，advance 命名渐进一步，医学复合词则保留字面的防御义。

intro.en: Breakthrough has no affixes at all. It is a compound of break and through, both native English words; the noun is a zero-derivation from the phrasal verb, with no suffix added.
intro.cn: breakthrough 没有任何词缀。它是 break 与 through 两个本土英语词的复合；名词由短语动词零派生而来，没有添加后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin layer here. The word is native English, so the Latin entries below are not ancestors but Latin-derived counterparts that English already had for a forward step or a find.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语层次。这个词是本土英语，因此下面的拉丁条目不是祖先，而是英语中原本就有的、表示“向前一步”或“发现”的拉丁来源对应词。

items.structure: break (to break) + through (from one side to the other)
items.meaning: to force a way through an obstacle; the source phrase, later compressed into a noun
items.meaningCN: 强行穿过障碍；这是源短语，后来压缩成名词
items.example: The water broke through the dam at midnight.
items.exampleCN: 水在午夜冲破了堤坝。

items.meaning: the gap and the passage through it; no suffix marks the change of word class
items.meaningCN: 缺口以及穿过缺口的通道；词性变化不靠后缀标记
items.example: The breakthrough came after ten years of work.
items.exampleCN: 这项突破在十年工作之后到来。

items.meaning: sudden pain that breaks through painkillers; the old literal sense applied to medicine
items.meaningCN: 突破止痛药控制的突发疼痛；旧字面义用于医学
items.example: She described the breakthrough pain as sharp and brief.
items.exampleCN: 她描述那种爆发痛尖锐而短暂。

items.meaning: an infection that gets past a vaccine or drug defence
items.meaningCN: 越过疫苗或药物防线的感染
items.example: Breakthrough infections are expected when a virus changes.
items.exampleCN: 病毒变异时，出现突破性感染是意料之中的。

items.meaning: the technology that produced the decisive advance
items.meaningCN: 产生决定性进展的技术
items.example: The breakthrough technology halved the cost of sequencing.
items.exampleCN: 这项突破性技术把测序成本降低了一半。

items.meaning: an escape or a sudden success beyond a former limit
items.meaningCN: 逃脱；突破原有局限的突然成功
items.example: The band had a breakout year after the album.
items.exampleCN: 这张专辑之后，乐队迎来了突破性的一年。

items.meaning: a collapse or a division into parts
items.example: The breakdown of the talks surprised both sides.
items.exampleCN: 谈判破裂让双方都感到意外。

items.meaning: the ending of a relationship or the splitting of a group
items.example: The breakup of the partnership left both firms weaker.
items.exampleCN: 合作关系解体后，两家公司都变弱了。

items.meaning: a separation or departure from a larger group
items.meaningCN: 从较大群体中分离或脱离
items.example: A breakaway faction formed a new party.
items.exampleCN: 一个脱离出来的派系组成了新政党。

latinEntries.meaning: a forward step; a Latin-derived counterpart, not the source of breakthrough
latinEntries.meaningCN: 前进一步；拉丁来源的对应词，并非 breakthrough 的来源

latinEntries.structure: Old French avancer, ultimately from Latin abante 'from before'
latinEntries.meaning: to move forward; again a counterpart rather than an ancestor
latinEntries.meaningCN: 向前移动；同样是对应词而非祖先

latinEntries.meaning: the introduction of something new; it stresses novelty, not a broken barrier
latinEntries.meaningCN: 引入新事物；强调新颖，而不是被打破的障碍

latinEntries.meaning: an uncovering, hence a find; it names the thing found, not the passage through a wall
latinEntries.meaningCN: 揭开覆盖，故为发现；它命名被找到之物，而不是穿墙而过
