senses.title: More people in a place
senses.definition: a rise in the number of people living in a place
senses.definitionCN: 某地居住人数的上升
senses.example: Rapid population growth outpaced the city's water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 人口的快速增长超出了城市供水能力。
senses.why: population names the people counted together, and growth names increase, so the phrase states a simplest fact: the count is going up.
senses.whyCN: population 指被一起计数的人，growth 指增加，因此这个短语陈述一件最简单的事：数目在上升。

senses.title: The rate of increase
senses.titleCN: 增长率：单位时间增加多少
senses.definition: the percentage or number by which a population rises in a given period
senses.definitionCN: 一定时期内人口上升的百分比或数量
senses.example: The population growth rate fell from three percent to one.
senses.exampleCN: 人口增长率从百分之三降到百分之一。
senses.why: once demographers wanted to compare places, the phrase needed a denominator, and rate supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 当人口学家需要比较各地，这个短语就需要一个分母，rate 提供了它。

senses.title: Natural increase
senses.definition: growth produced by births exceeding deaths, without migration
senses.definitionCN: 出生数超过死亡数所带来的增长，不计迁移
senses.example: Natural population growth turned negative as births fell.
senses.exampleCN: 随着出生数下降，人口自然增长转为负值。
senses.why: demographers separate the two books that change a population, and natural increase is the one kept without migration.
senses.whyCN: 人口学家把改变人口的两本账分开，自然增长就是不计迁移的那一本。

senses.title: Growth through migration
senses.definition: growth produced by more people arriving than leaving
senses.definitionCN: 迁入人数多于迁出人数所带来的增长
senses.example: Most of the city's population growth came from newcomers rather than births.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的人口增长多来自外来者，而非出生。
senses.why: the second book is net migration, and a city can grow through arrivals even when its own birth rate is low.
senses.whyCN: 第二本账是净迁移：即使本地出生率很低，城市也能靠迁入而增长。

senses.title: The steep phase of a curve
senses.titleCN: 指数增长阶段：曲线陡升
senses.definition: the phase in which numbers rise faster and faster because growth feeds on itself
senses.definitionCN: 数量因增长自身而越来越快地上升的阶段
senses.example: During the steep phase of population growth, schools were built every year.
senses.exampleCN: 在人口增长的陡升阶段，每年都要新建学校。
senses.why: growth that feeds on itself bends the curve upward, which is why the phrase is often used with steep and exponential.
senses.whyCN: 自我推动的增长把曲线向上掰弯，因此这个短语常与 steep、exponential 连用。

senses.title: Growth of non-human populations
senses.definition: an increase in the numbers of animals, plants or microbes rather than people
senses.definitionCN: 指动物、植物或微生物数量的增加，而非人口
senses.example: Deer population growth followed the removal of predators.
senses.exampleCN: 捕食者消失之后，鹿群数量随之增长。
senses.why: the same arithmetic governs animals, so population growth is also the standard term in ecology.
senses.whyCN: 同一套算术也管动物，因此 population growth 同样是生态学的标准术语。

senses.title: The end of growth
senses.titleCN: 零增长或负增长：增长的终止
senses.definition: the condition in which numbers stop rising, as in zero population growth
senses.definitionCN: 数量停止上升的状态，如人口零增长
senses.example: Zero population growth was reached in the 1990s.
senses.exampleCN: 人口零增长在 1990 年代实现。
senses.why: once growth became a policy variable, its absence needed a name, and zero growth supplies the target.
senses.whyCN: 一旦增长成为政策变量，它的缺席也需要一个名称，零增长正好提供这个目标。

senses.title: Growth of a market or audience
senses.titleCN: 经济义：市场或受众规模的扩大
senses.definition: an increase in the number of customers or users seen as a population
senses.definitionCN: 把客户或用户视作人群时的数量扩大
senses.example: The app's population growth attracted advertisers.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用用户规模的增长吸引了广告商。
senses.why: business counts users as a population, so the phrase transfers without changing its arithmetic.
senses.whyCN: 商业把用户当作人群来计数，因此这个短语在转用时算术并未改变。

intro.en: Population comes from Latin populatio 'a peopling', from populus 'people'; growth is native English from grow. The phrase is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: population 来自拉丁 populatio「使有人居住、人群」，源自 populus「人民」；growth 是英语本族词，来自 grow。这个短语是近代组合。年代均为约数。

items.en: Populus meant 'people, nation'. Its own origin is uncertain; the proposal that it came through Etruscan is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: populus 意为「人民、民族」。其自身来源不确定；认为它经埃特鲁里亚语而来的说法属假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Populatio named a peopling or a multitude; English took population in the sixteenth century for the people of a place.
items.cn: populatio 指使有人居住或人群；英语在 16 世纪以 population 指某地的人口。

items.en: Grow descends from Old English growan 'to grow, increase', of Germanic stock, and its noun growth followed in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: grow 承自古英语 growan「生长、增加」，属日耳曼语；其名词 growth 于 14 世纪出现。

items.en: Population growth became a fixed phrase in the nineteenth century, when censuses made the count comparable across decades.
items.cn: population growth 在 19 世纪成为固定短语，当时人口普查使跨年代的计数可以比较。

items.en: The twentieth century turned the phrase into a subject of policy, from Malthus's arithmetic to the population conferences of the 1990s.
items.cn: 20 世纪把这个短语变成政策议题，从马尔萨斯的算术到 1990 年代的人口会议。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest use of the exact phrase is not precisely recorded, and the origin of Latin populus remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这一确切短语的最早使用没有精确记录；拉丁 populus 的来源仍无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words of the populus family that are easily confused; group two holds phrases for numbers rising.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 populus 词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是数量上升的其他说法。

entries.definition: The number of people or organisms; population growth is the change in that number over time.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或生物的数量；population growth 是这个数量随时间的变化。

entries.definition: Full of people, as a populous country; it describes a state, not a trend.
entries.definitionCN: 指人口众多，如人口大国；描述状态，不描述趋势。

entries.definition: To fill a place with people or to enter data into a system; it names an act, not a trend.
entries.definitionCN: 指使人居住于某地或向系统填入数据；命名动作，而非趋势。

entries.definition: De- 'away from' plus population: the losing of people from a place, the mirror image of growth.
entries.definitionCN: de-「离开」加 population：某地失去人口，是增长的镜像。

entries.definition: A neutral statement that the number has risen, without implying a rate or a phase.
entries.definitionCN: 中性说明数量已上升，不含速率或阶段的意味。

entries.definition: Growth described through births, deaths and age structure rather than a single total.
entries.definitionCN: 通过出生、死亡与年龄结构描述的 growth，而非单一总量。

entries.definition: A short surge in births; it is one cause of population growth, not the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 指出生数的短促激增；它是人口增长的一个原因，而非总称。

entries.definition: The largest population an environment can support; growth stops when it is reached.
entries.definitionCN: 指环境能支撑的最大人口量；达到它时增长就停止。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: population 'the people counted' + growth 'increase': the count going up.
normal.cn: population「被计数的人口」+ growth「增加」：数目在上升。

normal.en: The family runs population, populous, populate, depopulation, growth, grow.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 population、populous、populate、depopulation、growth、grow。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: population growth rate, natural population growth, zero population growth.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：人口增长率、人口自然增长、人口零增长。

normal.en: Demographers split growth into natural increase and net migration.
normal.cn: 人口学家把增长拆成自然增加与净迁移。

normal.en: Growth without a rate is a fact; growth with a rate is a comparison.
normal.cn: 不带速率的增长是事实；带速率的增长是比较。

abstract.en: Picture a line on paper that bends upward and will not straighten.
abstract.cn: 想象纸上的线向上弯，弯得收不回来。

abstract.en: Picture a lifeboat taking on people faster than it can take on water.
abstract.cn: 想象救生艇上人的增加快过它能进水的速度。

abstract.en: Picture a queue that doubles while the door stays one door wide.
abstract.cn: 想象队伍不断翻倍，而门始终只有一扇宽。

examples.en: Population growth slowed once girls stayed in school longer.
examples.cn: 女孩在校时间延长后，人口增长放缓了。

examples.en: The graph shows population growth against grain output.
examples.cn: 这张图把人口增长与粮食产量并列显示。

examples.en: Wildlife population growth can overshoot the food supply.
examples.cn: 野生动物种群的增长可能超过食物供给。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「population（人口）+ growth（增长）」——被计数的人越来越多 → 人口增长

root: 拉丁 populus「人民」（更早来源不确定）+ populatio「人群、使有人居住」+ 古英语 growan「生长、增加」；英语 population growth。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a count rises, and that rise is then read as a rate, a natural surplus, a migration effect, a steep curve, a wildlife trend, a halt, and a market.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个变化展开：某个计数上升，这个上升再被读成速率、自然盈余、迁移效应、陡升曲线、野生动物趋势、停止，以及市场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curve that lifts gently and then shoots upward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条先缓抬、后猛冲的曲线。

branches.en: FACT AND RATE: the bare increase, then the same increase divided by time.
branches.cn: 事实与速率：先是不加修饰的增加，再是除以时间后的同一增加。

branches.en: TWO SOURCES: births exceeding deaths, or arrivals exceeding departures.
branches.cn: 两个来源：出生多于死亡，或迁入多于迁出。

branches.en: SELF-FEEDING GROWTH: the steep phase, whether of people or of deer.
branches.cn: 自我推动的增长：陡升阶段，人或鹿皆然。

branches.en: THE HALT: zero growth is the phrase turned into a target.
branches.cn: 停止：零增长就是把短语变成目标。

branches.en: BORROWED MARKET: users are counted as a population and their rise becomes growth.
branches.cn: 借用的市场：用户被当作人群计数，其上升便成为增长。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin noun of people to a native English noun of increasing; neither half carries a prefix or suffix of its own.
intro.cn: 这个短语把表示人民的拉丁名词与表示增加的本族英语名词并置；两半本身都不带前缀或后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin populus yields population, populous, populate and depopulation; Old English growan yields grow, growth and growing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 populus 衍生 population、populous、populate 与 depopulation；古英语 growan 衍生 grow、growth 与 growing。

items.example: The Latin noun names a people as a body.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词把人民视为一个整体。

items.example: The population passed one million.
items.exampleCN: 人口突破一百万。

items.example: The delta is the most populous region.
items.exampleCN: 三角洲是人口最稠密的地区。

items.example: Settlers populated the valley within a century.
items.exampleCN: 定居者在一个世纪内住满了这条谷地。

items.example: Depopulation closed the village school.
items.exampleCN: 人口流失使村校关闭。

items.example: The town grew along the river.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇沿着河生长。

items.example: Growth slowed after the drought.
items.exampleCN: 干旱之后增长放缓。

items.example: Population growth outpaced the water supply.
items.exampleCN: 人口增长超出了供水能力。

items.example: A growing population needs more housing.
items.exampleCN: 不断增长的人口需要更多住房。

senses.title: The book that holds the entries
senses.definition: an official book or list in which names, events, or amounts are written down and kept
senses.definitionCN: 正式记录姓名、事件或金额并加以保存的册子或名单
senses.example: The parish register records every birth and marriage since 1700.
senses.exampleCN: 这个教区登记簿记录了 1700 年以来每一次出生与婚姻。
senses.why: The Latin verb regerere meant 'carry back': events were carried back into a book so that they would not be lost. The book is that carried-back record.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 regerere 意为“带回来”：发生的事情被带回一本册子里，以免丢失。这本册子就是那份被带回的记录。

senses.title: The machine that rings up a sale
senses.definition: a machine that records the amount of money taken in a sale and keeps a running total
senses.definitionCN: 记录每笔交易金额并累计总额的机器
senses.example: She opened the cash register and counted the morning's takings.
senses.exampleCN: 她打开收银机，清点了上午的收入。
senses.why: Once entries were kept by a machine rather than a clerk, the name of the book moved to the box: the register registers each sale as it happens.
senses.whyCN: 当条目由机器而不是店员来记录，这本册子的名字就转移到了那只箱子上：收银机在每笔交易发生时把它记下来。

senses.title: The range of a voice or instrument
senses.definition: the range of pitches that a voice or instrument can produce, or a part of that range with a distinct quality
senses.definitionCN: 人声或乐器能发出的音高范围，或其中音质独特的一段
senses.example: The soprano's upper register was clear and effortless.
senses.exampleCN: 那位女高音的高音区清亮而毫不费力。
senses.why: A register was first a list, then the compass of a voice — the full list of notes it can reach. The musical sense, recorded in 1811, treats pitch as entries on a scale.
senses.whyCN: register 先是一份名单，再是一个声音的“音域”——它能达到的全部音符的名单。音乐义记录于 1811 年，把音高当作同一把尺子上的条目。

senses.title: The level of language a situation calls for
senses.definition: in linguistics, a style or level of language used in a particular social situation
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中指在特定社会场合所使用的语言风格或层次
senses.example: The report was written in a formal academic register.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告用的是正式的学术语体。
senses.why: The musical idea of a range or level was carried into language: a speaker moves between formal and casual registers much as a voice moves between high and low.
senses.whyCN: 音乐里“音域、层次”的观念被带进了语言：说话人在正式与随意之间切换语体，正如人声在高音与低音之间移动。

senses.title: A slot inside a processor
senses.titleCN: 处理器里的一个存储槽
senses.definition: in computing, a small, fast storage location inside a processor that holds one piece of data during an operation
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中指处理器内部容量很小、速度很快的存储位置，在一次运算中存放一项数据
senses.example: The program loads both numbers into registers before adding them.
senses.exampleCN: 程序先把两个数装进寄存器，然后再相加。
senses.why: A processor register is a numbered slot where a value is entered and kept, the smallest version of the ledger's ruled line.
senses.whyCN: 处理器寄存器是一个编号的格子，一个数值被“写进去”并保存在那里，它是账簿横线的最小版本。

senses.title: Write it into the record
senses.definition: to write a name, fact, or amount into an official list or system
senses.definitionCN: 把姓名、事实或金额写进正式的名单或系统
senses.example: The clerk registered the deed at the county office.
senses.exampleCN: 职员在县办事处登记了这份契约。
senses.why: This is the verb built directly on the noun: to register is to put an entry into the register.
senses.whyCN: 这是直接由名词构成的动词：to register 就是把一个条目放进登记册。

senses.title: Put your own name down
senses.definition: to add your own name to a list in order to take part in something
senses.definitionCN: 为参加某项活动而把自己的名字加入名单
senses.example: You must register to vote before the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 你必须在本月底之前登记才能投票。
senses.why: The verb turned reflexive in ordinary use: the person becomes both the writer and the entry. This sense is recorded from 1848.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词在日常使用中转向了自身：人既是书写者，也是被写下的那一条。这个义项记录于 1848 年。

senses.title: Show a reading on a dial
senses.definition: of an instrument, to show or record a measured value
senses.definitionCN: 指仪器显示或记录某个测得的数值
senses.example: The thermometer registered thirty degrees at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午时温度计显示三十度。
senses.why: An instrument registering is the machine doing the clerk's work: it enters the measurement into its own record and displays it.
senses.whyCN: 仪器 register，就是机器在做店员的活：它把测量结果写进自己的记录，并显示出来。

senses.title: Let an expression show
senses.definition: of a feeling, to appear on a face or in a voice before it is put into words
senses.definitionCN: 指某种情绪在说出口之前先显现在脸上或声音里
senses.example: Surprise registered on her face before she spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 她还没开口，惊讶就先显在了脸上。
senses.why: The 1901 sense treats the face as an instrument: the feeling reaches the surface and the dial moves.
senses.whyCN: 1901 年的这个义项把脸当作一台仪器：情绪抵达表面，表盘便动了。

intro.en: Register comes from Medieval Latin registrum, a much altered form of regestum, from Latin regerere 'carry back'. The second -r- was added by analogy, and some later senses were coloured by the unrelated regere 'rule'. Dates follow standard etymological references.
intro.cn: register 来自中世纪拉丁语 registrum，它是 regestum 经过大幅变形的形式，源头是拉丁语 regerere“带回”。第二个 -r- 是类比加上的，后来某些义项又受到无关的 regere“统治”影响。年代依据通行词源资料。

items.en: The noun registre is first recorded meaning 'public record book, private account book, an official written account regularly kept'.
items.cn: 名词 registre 最早记录于 14 世纪晚期，意为“公共记录簿、私人账簿、定期保存的正式书面记录”。

items.en: From Old French registre (13c.) and directly from Medieval Latin registrum, regestrum, properly regestum, from Late Latin regesta 'list, matters recorded'. The unetymological second -r- came by influence of Latin nouns in -istrum.
items.cn: 来自古法语 registre（13 世纪），并直接来自中世纪拉丁语 registrum、regestrum，本作 regestum，出自晚期拉丁语 regesta“清单、被记录的事项”。非词源的第二个 -r- 是受拉丁语 -istrum 类名词影响而加上的。

items.en: Regesta is the neuter plural of regestus, past participle of regerere 'to record; retort', literally 'to carry back, bring back', from re- 'back' + gerere 'carry, bear'. The record is what has been carried back.
items.cn: regesta 是 regestus 的中性复数，后者是 regerere 的过去分词，意为“记录；反驳”，字面是“带回、携回”，由 re-“回”加 gerere“携带、承载”构成。记录就是被带回来的东西。

items.en: Some later senses seem to have been influenced by association with unrelated Latin regere 'to rule, to guide, to keep straight'. Regere is not the source of register; the two families only resemble each other.
items.cn: 后来某些义项似乎受到无关的拉丁语 regere“统治、引导、使笔直”的联想影响。regere 并不是 register 的来源；两个词族只是形似。

items.en: The printing sense 'exact alignment of presswork' is from the 1680s. The musical sense 'compass or range of a voice or instrument' is from 1811, hence 'a series of tones of the same quality'. The sense 'device by which data is automatically recorded' is by 1830, from the verb.
items.cn: 印刷义“印件的精确对齐”始于 17 世纪 80 年代。音乐义“人声或乐器的音域”始于 1811 年，由此引申为“同一音质的一组音”。义项“自动记录数据的装置”到 1830 年已出现，来自动词。

items.en: The verb registren 'to record, enter in a listing' is late 14c.; 'enroll someone' is c.1400; instruments 'show a reading' 1797; 'enter one's own name' 1848; persons and feelings 'make an impression' by 1901. Registered nurse is attested from 1879.
items.cn: 动词 registren“记录、列入清单”为 14 世纪晚期；c.1400 起有“使某人登记入册”；仪器“显示读数”始于 1797 年；“写下自己的名字”始于 1848 年；人或情绪“留下印象”到 1901 年已出现。registered nurse（注册护士）见于 1879 年。

note.en: The first group separates register from its derived nouns, each of which names a different part of the act: the process, the office, the official, the person enrolled. The second group compares the verbs of putting something on a list.
note.cn: 第一组把 register 与它的派生名词分开，每个派生词命名这个行为的不同部分：过程、机构、官员、被登记的人。第二组比较几个“把某物列入名单”的动词。

entries.definition: the act or process of registering. It names the procedure, while register is the book or the act itself.
entries.definitionCN: 登记或注册的行为与过程。它命名程序，而 register 是册子或动作本身。

entries.definition: an office where records are kept, or a formal list or database. It is the place or the collection, not the single book on the counter.
entries.definitionCN: 保存记录的机构，或正式的名单、数据库。它是场所或集合，而不是柜台上那一本册子。

entries.definition: the official who keeps a register, especially at a university or hospital. It is the person, not the record.
entries.definitionCN: 保管登记册的官员，尤指大学或医院中的注册主任。它是人，而不是记录。

entries.definition: a person who registers, especially for a course, exam, or event. It is the person on the list, not the person keeping it.
entries.definitionCN: 进行登记的人，尤指报名课程、考试或活动者。它是名单上的人，而不是保管名单的人。

entries.definition: to store information so that it can be found later. It is broader than register: you can record a sound or a fact without entering it in an official list.
entries.definitionCN: 把信息存下来以便日后查找。它比 register 宽：你可以记录一段声音或一个事实，而不必把它写进正式名单。

entries.definition: to join a school, course, or organization by having your name entered on its list. It focuses on becoming a member, while register focuses on the act of writing the name down.
entries.definitionCN: 通过把名字列入名单而加入学校、课程或组织。它强调成为成员，而 register 强调写下名字这个动作。

entries.definition: to put your name down for something, usually in everyday speech. It is the informal phrasal equivalent of register for a course or event.
entries.definitionCN: 报名参加某事，通常用于日常口语。它是 register 用于课程或活动时的非正式短语对应语。

entries.definition: to write down events in a regular record as they happen, especially for technical or official purposes. A log is continuous; a register is often a formal list of names or transactions.
entries.definitionCN: 随着事件发生而定期写入记录，尤用于技术或正式目的。日志是连续的；登记册通常是姓名或交易的正式名单。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin re- 'back' + gerere 'carry', the Medieval Latin registrum, and the English family registration, registry, registrar and registrant.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 re-“回”加 gerere“携带”、中世纪拉丁语 registrum，以及英语词族 registration、registry、registrar、registrant。

normal.en: regerere means 'carry back': an event is carried back into a book so that it can be found again.
normal.cn: regerere 意为“带回”：一件事被带回册子里，以便日后还能找到。

normal.en: The second -r- in registrum is unetymological, added by analogy with nouns ending in -istrum. It is not part of the root.
normal.cn: registrum 里的第二个 -r- 不是词源原有的，而是类比 -istrum 结尾的名词加上去的。它不属于词根。

normal.en: regere 'rule' is a different verb. It coloured some later senses but did not father the word.
normal.cn: regere“统治”是另一个动词。它影响了后来某些义项，却不是这个词的来源。

normal.en: The verb has two everyday branches: write something in (register a deed), and put your own name down (register to vote).
normal.cn: 动词有两个日常分支：把某物写进去（登记契约），以及写下自己的名字（登记投票）。

normal.en: An instrument registers a reading, and a face registers a feeling: both are dials that move when something arrives.
normal.cn: 仪器 register 一个读数，脸 register 一种情绪：两者都是“有东西到达时表盘就动”的仪器。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger open on a counter. Every arrival gets one line, and the line stays after the person has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一本摊在柜台上的账簿。每来一个人就添一行，人走了，这一行还留着。

abstract.en: From that book the word spreads in three directions: the machine that writes the lines, the range of notes written on a musical scale, and the slot where a processor keeps one value.
abstract.cn: 从这个册子出发，这个词向三个方向扩散：替人写行的机器、写在音阶上的音域，以及处理器保存一个数值的格子。

abstract.en: Register is about entry, not memory: the point is that the name or number has been formally put in, not that someone remembers it.
abstract.cn: register 的关键是“入册”，而不是记忆：重点在于姓名或数字已被正式写进去，而不在于有人记得它。

examples.en: All births and deaths are registered at the town hall.
examples.cn: 所有出生与死亡都在市政厅登记。

examples.en: The university requires new students to register before orientation.
examples.cn: 大学要求新生在迎新之前完成注册。

examples.en: The gauge registered a sudden drop in pressure.
examples.cn: 压力表显示压力突然下降。

dict_mnemonic.text: “日记斯特”——日记斯特把每天来往的人和账都记进一本厚册子 → register 登记；登记册（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自中世纪拉丁语 registrum，上溯拉丁语 regerere“带回、记录”（re- 回 + gerere 携带），核心是“把发生的事带回册子里写下来”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of register, all from one object: a ruled book in which each name, sale, note, or value gets its own line, and the act of putting that line there.
sensesIntro.cn: register 的九个义项都围绕同一件东西：一本划了格子的册子，每个姓名、每笔交易、每个音符、每个数值都占一行；以及把这一行写进去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger open on a counter, one line added for each entry.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本摊在柜台上的账簿，每记一项就添一行。

branches.en: THE BOOK: the original sense is the official volume itself, where names and events are kept in ruled lines.
branches.cn: 册子：最原始的义项就是这本正式簿册，姓名与事件被保存在划好的行里。

branches.en: MACHINES AND SLOTS: the cash register writes the line for us, and the processor register is the smallest ruled slot of all.
branches.cn: 机器与存储槽：收银机替我们写这一行，处理器寄存器则是所有格子里最小的一个。

branches.en: RANGE AND LEVEL: a voice's register is its full list of notes; a language register is the level a situation calls for.
branches.cn: 范围与层次：人声的音域是它全部音符的名单；语域则是场合所要求的语言层次。

branches.en: WRITING NAMES IN: the verb records someone else's entry, or turns reflexive and writes one's own name.
branches.cn: 写入姓名：动词既记录别人的条目，也可转向自身、写下自己的名字。

branches.en: SHOWING: instruments and faces register readings and feelings, as if a dial moved when something arrived.
branches.cn: 显示：仪器与脸分别 register 读数和情绪，仿佛有东西到达时表盘就动了。

intro.en: Register is a Latin-derived noun whose visible ending is -ister/-istery in its medieval forms, not a living English suffix. English builds registration, registry, registrar and registrant on the finished word, and the root gerere also reaches English through gesture, suggest and digest.
intro.cn: register 是源自拉丁语的名词，其中世纪形式里看得见的词尾是 -ister／-istery，并非活的英语后缀。英语在成品词上构成 registration、registry、registrar、registrant；词根 gerere 还通过 gesture、suggest、digest 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is regerere 'carry back, record' (re- 'back' + gerere 'carry, bear'). Its past participle regestus became regesta 'things recorded', then Medieval Latin registrum. Gerere is a busy verb: it also gives gesture, digest, suggest, congest and register itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 regerere“带回、记录”（re-“回”+ gerere“携带、承载”）。其过去分词 regestus 变成 regesta“被记录的事项”，再变成中世纪拉丁语 registrum。gerere 是个繁忙的动词：gesture、digest、suggest、congest 以及 register 本身都出自它。

items.meaning: a book of carried-back records; to enter in it
items.meaningCN: 把记录带回的册子；登记入册（re- 回 + gerere 携带，经 regestus／registrum）
items.example: The hotel keeps a register of all guests.
items.exampleCN: 旅馆保存着所有客人的登记册。

items.meaningCN: 登记；注册（过程）（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Registration closes on the first of September.
items.exampleCN: 注册在九月一日截止。

items.meaning: an office or list where records are kept
items.meaningCN: 登记处；注册表（-y 表示机构或集合）
items.example: The land registry holds every title deed.
items.exampleCN: 土地登记处保存着每一份地契。

items.meaning: the official who keeps the register
items.meaningCN: 登记员；注册主任（-ar 表示任职者）
items.example: The registrar signed the marriage certificate.
items.exampleCN: 登记员签署了结婚证书。

items.meaningCN: 登记者；注册人（-ant 表示行为者）
items.example: Each registrant receives a badge at the door.
items.exampleCN: 每位登记者在门口领取一张胸牌。

items.meaningCN: 已登记的；注册的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: It is a registered charity.
items.exampleCN: 这是一个注册慈善机构。

items.meaning: to remove from an official register
items.meaningCN: 注销登记；撤销注册（de- 去除 + register）
items.example: The company deregistered for tax purposes.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司为税务目的注销了登记。

items.meaningCN: 手势；姿态（gest- 承载、表演 + -ure）
items.example: He made a small gesture of welcome.
items.exampleCN: 他做了一个小小的欢迎手势。

items.meaning: to bring an idea under someone's notice
items.meaningCN: 建议；暗示（sug- 在下 + gerere 携带，即“带到下面给人看”）
items.example: Her tone suggested that the plan was already agreed.
items.exampleCN: 她的语气暗示这个计划已经谈妥。

items.meaning: to break down and absorb; a summary
items.meaningCN: 消化；摘要（di- 分开 + gerere 携带，即“分开带走”）
items.example: The body digests food slowly at night.
items.exampleCN: 夜间身体消化食物较慢。

latinEntries.structure: neuter plural of regestus, past participle of regerere

definition_zh: 唯美主义；审美崇拜；为艺术而艺术的主张
definition_en: the belief that art should be valued for beauty alone, especially the late nineteenth-century movement of art for art's sake
core_image: 一间把实用物件全部移走、只留下颜色与线条的房间
scene: 展厅里，导览说这批画家拒绝让画承担道德说教，只谈颜色与形状。 The guide explained that aestheticism rejected any moral duty for painting.
sceneCN: 这里 aestheticism 指「主张艺术只应追求美、不承担道德或实用任务的理论」（第 2 个义项：为艺术而艺术的信条）；句意为导览说明唯美主义拒绝让绘画承担道德义务。

pos.zh: 唯美主义；审美崇拜（通常不可数）

collocations.zh: 维多利亚时期的唯美主义
19 世纪 90 年代的唯美主义
为艺术而艺术的唯美主义

forms.label: 可数用法（少见，指多种形态）

derivatives.zh: 希腊 aisthētikos「可感知的」→ 审美的；从「感知」转到「美」
aesthetic + -ics（学问）→ 美学；从「性质」转到「学科」
aesthetic + -e（人）→ 审美者；从「性质」转到「以美为价值的人」
aestheticism + -ist（信奉者）→ 唯美主义者；从「主义」转到「持此主张的人」
aesthetic + -ize（使……化）→ 使带上审美色彩；从「性质」转到「施加动作」

senses.title: The late nineteenth-century movement
senses.titleCN: 19 世纪后期的唯美主义运动
senses.definition: the late Victorian movement that made beauty the chief aim of art and life
senses.definitionCN: 维多利亚后期把美作为艺术与生活首要目标的运动
senses.example: The novel is usually read as a document of aestheticism.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说通常被读作唯美主义的一份文献。
senses.why: The suffix -ism names a movement as well as a doctrine, so aestheticism can denote the historical circle around Pater and Wilde.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ism 既可命名主张，也可命名运动，因此 aestheticism 能指佩特与王尔德周围的那个历史圈子。

senses.title: Art for art's sake
senses.definition: the principle that art owes nothing to morality, utility or social purpose
senses.definitionCN: 艺术不对道德、实用或社会目的负有任何义务的原则
senses.example: Aestheticism holds that art owes no moral lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 唯美主义认为艺术不欠任何道德教训。
senses.why: The movement's core claim is that beauty is the only end of art; the name of the movement became the name of that claim.
senses.whyCN: 这场运动的核心主张是美是艺术的唯一目的；运动的名称于是成了这条主张的名称。

senses.title: Devotion to beauty as a value
senses.definition: a personal commitment to beauty as the highest good
senses.definitionCN: 把美视为最高善的个人承诺
senses.example: Her aestheticism extended to the arrangement of a dinner table.
senses.exampleCN: 她的唯美追求连餐桌的摆法都不放过。
senses.why: A doctrine can become a temperament: when someone lives by the primacy of beauty, the word describes the commitment rather than a movement.
senses.whyCN: 主张可以变成性情：当一个人按美的优先性生活，这个词描述的就是这种承诺，而不是一场运动。

senses.title: Life treated as a work of art
senses.definition: the attitude that experience itself should be shaped aesthetically
senses.definitionCN: 认为经验本身应按审美方式塑造的态度
senses.example: Pater's aestheticism treated life itself as a work of art.
senses.exampleCN: 佩特的唯美主义把生活本身当作艺术品。
senses.why: If art needs no purpose outside beauty, then a life can be composed like an artwork; the doctrine extends from objects to conduct.
senses.whyCN: 如果艺术在美之外无需目的，那么生活也可以像艺术品一样被经营；主张因此从物件扩展到行为。

senses.title: A decorative style
senses.definition: the visual style associated with the aesthetic movement, especially in interiors and dress
senses.definitionCN: 与唯美运动相关的视觉风格，尤见于室内与服饰
senses.example: The house is a monument of eighteen-nineties aestheticism.
senses.exampleCN: 这座房子是 19 世纪 90 年代唯美主义风格的纪念碑。
senses.why: A movement leaves objects behind; its characteristic palette and patterns come to be called by the movement's name.
senses.whyCN: 运动会在物件上留下痕迹；其特有的色彩与纹样便被以运动之名相称。

senses.title: Over-concern with appearance
senses.titleCN: 对外观的过度讲究（贬义）
senses.definition: a pejorative term for excessive attention to surface beauty
senses.definitionCN: 贬义用法，指对表面之美的过度关注
senses.example: Critics attacked the aestheticism of the campaign as mere decoration.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抨击这场宣传活动只是装饰性的唯美做派。
senses.why: Any value can be mocked when it looks like evasion; aestheticism became a label for prettiness that avoids harder questions.
senses.whyCN: 任何价值在被视为逃避时都可能被讥讽；aestheticism 成了「只顾好看、回避难题」的标签。

senses.title: A stance in literary criticism
senses.titleCN: 文学批评中的一种立场
senses.definition: an approach that judges literature by formal beauty rather than moral or social effect
senses.definitionCN: 按形式之美而非道德或社会效果来评判文学的路径
senses.example: His aestheticism shaped a generation of literary criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 他的唯美立场塑造了一代文学批评。
senses.why: Literary criticism borrowed the movement's name for a method: reading for form, texture and pleasure rather than message.
senses.whyCN: 文学批评借用了这场运动的名字来命名一种方法：为形式、质感与愉悦而读，而非为信息而读。

senses.title: Beauty as the chief criterion in a field
senses.titleCN: 某一领域以美为主要标准
senses.definition: the tendency to put aesthetic appeal first in a domain outside art
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术之外的领域中把审美吸引力放在首位的倾向
senses.example: The brand's aestheticism puts beauty ahead of function.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌的唯美取向把美观放在功能之前。
senses.why: The doctrine's single criterion can be imported anywhere, so design, advertising or even engineering may be charged with aestheticism.
senses.whyCN: 这条主张的唯一标准可以被输入任何领域，因此设计、广告甚至工程都可能被指为唯美主义。

intro.en: Aestheticism is a nineteenth-century English formation: aesthetic plus -ism, recorded in 1855 and later tied to the art-for-art's-sake circle. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: aestheticism 是 19 世纪英语构词：aesthetic 加 -ism，1855 年有记录，后来与「为艺术而艺术」的圈子联系在一起。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aisthēsis 'perception' supplied the root of aesthetic; the sensory meaning is older than the meaning 'beautiful'.
items.cn: aisthēsis「感知」提供 aesthetic 的词根；感官义比「美」义更早。

items.en: Baumgarten's eighteenth-century coinage made aesthetics a name for the science of sensory knowledge.
items.cn: 鲍姆加登 18 世纪的造词使 aesthetics 成为感官知识之学的名称。

items.en: English aesthetic appeared in 1798; by the 1830s it commonly meant the appreciation of beauty.
items.cn: 英语 aesthetic 于 1798 年出现；到 1830 年代，它通常指对美的欣赏。

items.en: The suffix -ism, from Greek -ismos through Latin -ismus, names a practice, doctrine or movement.
items.cn: 后缀 -ism 经拉丁 -ismus 来自希腊 -ismos，命名一种实践、主张或运动。

items.en: Aestheticism is recorded in 1855 in the sense 'devotion to what is sensuously beautiful'.
items.cn: aestheticism 于 1855 年有记录，意为「对感官之美的献身」。

items.en: Later in the century the word was attached to Pater, Wilde and the art-for-art's-sake programme, and that historical sense now leads.
items.cn: 到该世纪后期，这个词与佩特、王尔德及「为艺术而艺术」纲领联系在一起，这一历史义如今最突出。

note.en: Group one separates aestheticism from the aisth- words it is built on; group two separates it from neighbouring movements and doctrines of art.
note.cn: 第一组把 aestheticism 与它所由来的 aisth- 词分开；第二组把它与邻近的艺术运动与主张分开。

entries.definition: A quality or principle of beauty; aestheticism is the doctrine that makes beauty supreme.
entries.definitionCN: 美的性质或原则；aestheticism 是把美置于至高位置的主张。

entries.definition: The philosophical study of beauty and art; it can analyse aestheticism without adopting it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究美与艺术的哲学；它可以分析唯美主义而不采纳它。

entries.definition: A devotee of beauty; aestheticism is the creed such a person may hold.
entries.definitionCN: 美的崇拜者；aestheticism 是此人可能持有的信条。

entries.definition: Loss of sensation; it shares the perceptual root but has no connection with the art movement.
entries.definitionCN: 感觉丧失；同出感知词根，但与这场艺术运动无关。

entries.definition: The French-derived phrase l'art pour l'art, translated in 1824; it is the slogan of aestheticism rather than its name.
entries.definitionCN: 源自法语 l'art pour l'art，1824 年有英译；它是唯美主义的口号，而不是其名称。

entries.definition: A late nineteenth-century literary mood of refinement and decline; it overlaps with aestheticism but adds exhaustion and perversity.
entries.definitionCN: 19 世纪后期的文学情绪，讲究精致与衰颓；与唯美主义重叠，但多了疲惫与乖僻。

entries.definition: The critical priority of formal structure over content; aestheticism is broader and adds a doctrine about beauty's value.
entries.definitionCN: 批评上把形式结构置于内容之上；aestheticism 更广，并附加关于美之价值的主张。

entries.definition: The cultivation of an elegant, conspicuous self-presentation; it is a social cousin of aestheticism, not the same programme.
entries.definitionCN: 对优雅而惹眼的自我呈现的经营；是唯美主义的社会近亲，而非同一纲领。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: aesthetic + -ism: the doctrine that beauty is the point.
normal.cn: aesthetic + -ism：以美为要旨的主张。

normal.en: -ism names movements as well as beliefs, so the word covers both a creed and a circle.
normal.cn: -ism 既命名主张也命名运动，因此这个词既指信条也指圈子。

normal.en: Fixed phrases date it: Victorian aestheticism, the aestheticism of the eighteen-nineties.
normal.cn: 固定搭配为它标年代：维多利亚唯美主义、19 世纪 90 年代的唯美主义。

normal.en: The family runs aesthetic, aesthetics, aesthete, aestheticism and aestheticist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 aesthetic、aesthetics、aesthete、aestheticism 与 aestheticist。

normal.en: The slogan art for art's sake translates French l'art pour l'art, recorded in English in 1824.
normal.cn: 口号「为艺术而艺术」译自法语 l'art pour l'art，英语 1824 年有记录。

abstract.en: Picture a room with every useful object removed and only colour left.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，实用物件全被移走，只剩下颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a frame that refuses to hold anything but the surface it shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个画框，只肯装它展示的那层表面。

abstract.en: Picture a life arranged with the same care as a shelf of porcelain.
abstract.cn: 想象一段生活被安排得像一柜瓷器那样精心。

examples.en: Aestheticism is often taught through the trial of Oscar Wilde.
examples.cn: 唯美主义常通过王尔德的审判来讲授。

examples.en: The movement's aestheticism did not deny politics; it refused to let politics judge art.
examples.cn: 这场运动的唯美主义并不否认政治，而是拒绝让政治评判艺术。

examples.en: Modern branding repeats the aestheticism of the eighteen-nineties in a commercial key.
examples.cn: 现代品牌以商业调子重复着 19 世纪 90 年代的唯美主义。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「aesthetic（审美的）+ -ism（主义）」——审美至上主义 → 唯美主义

root: aesthetic 来自希腊 aisthētikos「可感知的」，词根 aisthēsis「感知」；-ism 经拉丁 -ismus 来自希腊 -ismos，命名主张或运动。aestheticism 于 1855 年出现。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the historical movement to its doctrine, then to a personal creed, a way of life, a decorative style, a pejorative label, a critical method and finally a general criterion outside art.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从历史运动转到其主张，再到个人信条、生活方式、装饰风格、贬义标签、批评方法，最后落到艺术之外的普遍标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room emptied of useful things, where only colour and line remain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间移走实用物件、只留下颜色与线条的房间。

branches.en: THE MOVEMENT AND ITS CRITERION: a historical circle, then the same priority applied anywhere.
branches.cn: 运动及其标准：先是一个历史圈子，再是同一优先性被用到任何领域。

branches.en: THE DOCTRINE AND THE METHOD: art owes no moral lesson, and criticism reads for form.
branches.cn: 主张与方法：艺术不欠道德教训，批评则为形式而读。

branches.en: A CREED LIVED: devotion to beauty becomes a way of composing experience.
branches.cn: 被实践的信条：对美的献身变成安排经验的方式。

branches.en: A STYLE LEFT BEHIND: the movement survives in palettes, patterns and interiors.
branches.cn: 留下的风格：运动在色彩、纹样与室内中继续存在。

branches.en: THE MOCKING NAME: concern with surface becomes a charge of evasion.
branches.cn: 被讥讽之名：对表面的关注被指控为逃避。

intro.en: Aestheticism is a Greek root plus two suffixes, one making an adjective and one making a doctrine, so the whole word can be read in layers.
intro.cn: aestheticism 是希腊词根加两个后缀，一个构成形容词，一个构成主张，因此整个词可以分层读出。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek, not Latin; Latin contributes only the shape of the suffix -ismus, which English took through French -isme.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是希腊语而非拉丁语；拉丁语只提供后缀 -ismus 的形状，英语经法语 -isme 取得。

items.example: The root begins the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根开启整个词族。

items.example: The suffix makes aesthetic an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀使 aesthetic 成为形容词。

items.example: The aesthetic argument came first.
items.exampleCN: 审美论证先出现。

items.example: Realism and formalism use the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: realism 与 formalism 用的是同一个后缀。

items.meaning: the doctrine of beauty for its own sake
items.example: Aestheticism rejected moral instruction.
items.exampleCN: 唯美主义拒绝道德训诫。

items.example: The aestheticist wrote only about surfaces.
items.exampleCN: 这位唯美主义者只写表面。

items.example: The film aestheticizes the factory.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片把工厂审美化了。

items.meaning: from an aesthetic point of view
items.example: The street is aesthetically coherent.
items.exampleCN: 这条街在审美上是一致的。

items.example: Aesthetics can study aestheticism coldly.
items.exampleCN: 美学可以冷静地研究唯美主义。

definition_zh: 解放；使脱离控制、监禁或束缚；释放（气体等）；解放运动
definition_en: the act of setting someone free from control, confinement or a constraining condition
core_image: 牢门被推开，光从走廊尽头照进来，门槛上落着一串钥匙
scene: 清晨的营区大门被从里面推开，人们沿着泥路走出来，等在门外的家人举起写着名字的纸牌。 The archive records the liberation of the camp, the act of setting the prisoners free, in the spring of nineteen forty-five.
sceneCN: 这里 liberation 指「使被关押者脱离控制」（第 1 个义项：把人从拘禁中放出）；句意为档案记录了那处营地在四五年春天获得解放。可辨识物件：推开的大门、泥路、姓名纸牌、走廊尽头的晨光、落在地上的钥匙。

pos.zh: 解放；释放；解放运动（可数，复数 liberations）

derivatives.zh: 解放；释放
解放者
被解放的；思想开放的
解放性的
自由
自由的；开明的
递送；解救

senses.title: The act of setting someone free
senses.titleCN: 使某人获得自由的行为
senses.definition: the act of releasing a person or people from confinement, control or servitude
senses.definitionCN: 把人从拘禁、控制或奴役中放出的行为
senses.example: The archive records the liberation of the camp in the spring of nineteen forty-five.
senses.exampleCN: 档案记录了那处营地在四五年春天获得解放。
senses.why: liberare is 'to make free', from liber 'free'; the noun names the moment the condition changes.
senses.whyCN: liberare 是「使自由」，来自 liber「自由的」；名词指状态改变的那一刻。

senses.title: Military liberation of a place
senses.definition: the recapture or freeing of a territory by armed force
senses.definitionCN: 以武力收复或解救一片地区
senses.example: The liberation of the port cut the enemy's supply line.
senses.exampleCN: 港口的解放切断了敌方的补给线。
senses.why: armies describe recapture as liberation when they are welcomed as freeing the inhabitants.
senses.whyCN: 当军队被视为解救居民时，他们就把收复称为解放。

senses.title: National or colonial liberation
senses.definition: the ending of foreign rule and the achievement of independence
senses.definitionCN: 结束外国统治并取得独立
senses.example: National liberation movements reshaped the map after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 战后，民族解放运动重划了地图。
senses.why: a people under external rule experiences the end of that rule as a release, so the word joins national claims.
senses.whyCN: 受外来统治的民族把统治的结束体验为释放，因此这个词与民族诉求结合。

senses.title: Social liberation of a group
senses.definition: the removal of legal and social restraints from a class, gender or minority
senses.definitionCN: 解除对某一阶级、性别或少数群体的法律与社会束缚
senses.example: The liberation of women from restrictive property laws took decades.
senses.exampleCN: 女性从限制性财产法中的解放花了数十年。
senses.why: the word is borrowed from physical release to describe the removal of legal chains.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从身体释放借来，用来描述法律锁链的解除。

senses.title: Personal or intellectual liberation
senses.definition: a private release from fear, habit, ignorance or an oppressive belief
senses.definitionCN: 个人从恐惧、习惯、无知或压抑性信念中解脱
senses.example: Learning to read was a personal liberation for him.
senses.exampleCN: 学会阅读对他而言是一种个人的解放。
senses.why: the outer act has an inner analogue: what holds a mind can also be opened.
senses.whyCN: 外在动作有内在对应：锁住心智的东西也能被打开。

senses.title: A liberation movement or organization
senses.definition: an organized political force that describes its goal as liberation
senses.definitionCN: 以解放为目标的组织化政治力量
senses.example: The liberation front controlled three provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 解放阵线控制着三个省。
senses.why: when a cause organizes, the abstract noun becomes part of its name.
senses.whyCN: 当一项事业组织起来，抽象名词就成为其名称的一部分。

senses.title: Release of a substance, especially a gas
senses.definition: the freeing of a gas, energy or chemical from a bound state
senses.definitionCN: 使气体、能量或化学物质从束缚状态中释放
senses.example: The liberation of gas from the rock warned the miners.
senses.exampleCN: 岩石中气体的释出警告了矿工。
senses.why: chemistry uses the same word for physical freeing, which shows how literal the core sense remains.
senses.whyCN: 化学用同一个词指物理释放，可见核心义仍然很字面。

senses.title: Abstraction: removal of any constraint
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何束缚的解除
senses.definition: any process by which a limit on action is removed, whether physical, legal or mental
senses.definitionCN: 任何解除行动限制的过程，无论物理、法律或心理
senses.example: Liberation begins when a rule loses its power to frighten.
senses.exampleCN: 当一条规则失去吓人的力量，解放就开始了。
senses.why: the deepest sense is negative: not the gaining of something new but the lifting of a weight.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是否定性的：不是获得新东西，而是移走一份重量。

intro.en: Liberation comes from Latin liberare 'to set free', from liber 'free'. The Latin word liber also means 'book' but is a different word. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: liberation 来自拉丁 liberare「使自由」，源于 liber「自由的」。拉丁语中 liber 也指「书」，但那是另一个词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Liber meant 'free, unrestricted'; it is a different word from liber 'book', which belongs to another stem.
items.cn: liber 意为「自由的、不受限制的」；它与表示「书」的 liber 是另一个词，属不同词干。

items.en: Liberare meant 'to set free, release, acquit'; it turned the adjective into an action.
items.cn: liberare 意为「使自由、释放、宣告无罪」；它把形容词变成动作。

items.en: Liberatio named a setting free or acquittal, and English liberation came from this noun.
items.cn: liberatio 指释放或宣告无罪，英语 liberation 来自这个名词。

items.en: The word entered English through Old French in the fifteenth century, first in legal and religious senses.
items.cn: 这个词在十五世纪经古法语进入英语，最初用于法律与宗教语境。

items.en: From the eighteenth century liberation was applied to nations, slaves and social classes, and the political sense now dominates.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，liberation 被用于民族、奴隶与社会阶级，政治义如今占主导。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin): the deeper root of liber is often reconstructed with a sense such as 'to grow up', but no single reconstruction is proven.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拉丁语前来源）：liber 的更深词根常被重构为带有「成长」之义的形状，但没有哪一种重构得到证明。

note.en: Group one holds liberty-family words easily confused with liberation; group two holds neighbouring ideas of being freed.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 liberation 混淆的自由类词；第二组是「获得自由」的邻近概念。

entries.definition: The condition of being free; liberation is the act or process that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指自由的状态；liberation 是产生这一状态的行为或过程。

entries.definition: Originally 'befitting a free man', now a political and social label; it does not mean the act of freeing.
entries.definitionCN: 原指「适合自由人的」，现为政治与社会标签；不表示「解放」这个动作。

entries.definition: One who liberates; the noun names the agent, while liberation names the deed.
entries.definitionCN: 指实施解放的人；名词命名施动者，而 liberation 命名行为。

entries.definition: Being saved from danger or captivity; it stresses rescue from a threat more than the ending of a system.
entries.definitionCN: 指从危险或囚禁中被救出；更强调脱离威胁，而非终结制度。

entries.definition: The formal legal freeing of a person from slavery or authority; liberation is broader and can be military or personal.
entries.definitionCN: 指法律上正式使某人脱离奴役或支配；liberation 更宽，可指军事或个人层面的解放。

entries.definition: The state of a nation governing itself; liberation can be the struggle that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家自治的状态；liberation 可以是产生它的斗争。

entries.definition: The act of letting a person or thing go; it is physical and neutral, without the political weight of liberation.
entries.definitionCN: 指放开人或物；是物理性、中性的，没有 liberation 的政治分量。

entries.definition: The general condition of not being constrained; liberation is one route to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指不受约束的一般状态；liberation 是通向它的一条路径。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin adjective, the real family and the physical picture of an opening door.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：那个拉丁形容词、真实词族，以及「门被打开」的身体图景。

normal.en: liber 'free' + -ation: the act of making free.
normal.cn: liber「自由的」+ -ation：使自由的行为。

normal.en: The family runs liberate, liberator, liberty, liberal, liberation, deliver.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 liberate、liberator、liberty、liberal、liberation、deliver。

normal.en: Do not confuse liber 'free' with liber 'book': same spelling, different stem.
normal.cn: 不要混淆 liber「自由的」与 liber「书」：拼写相同，词干不同。

normal.en: The core picture is a door opened from the inside.
normal.cn: 核心图景是一扇从里面被打开的门。

normal.en: Typical partners are national, movement, war of and women's.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「民族的」「运动」「……战争」与「妇女的」。

abstract.en: Picture a key left on the threshold after the lock has already been opened.
abstract.cn: 想象锁已打开之后，钥匙留在门槛上。

abstract.en: Picture a window opened in a room that had forgotten the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一间忘了天空的房间被打开一扇窗。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that still exists but no longer makes anyone afraid.
abstract.cn: 想象一条仍然存在却不再让人害怕的规则。

examples.en: The city celebrated its liberation with a quiet procession.
examples.cn: 这座城市以一场安静的游行庆祝解放。

examples.en: Literacy brought a kind of liberation that no law could grant.
examples.cn: 识字带来一种法律无法给予的解放。

examples.en: The experiment measured the liberation of hydrogen from the sample.
examples.cn: 实验测量了样品中氢气的释放。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「lib（自由 libr）+ eration（变成）」——把人变成自由的状态 → 解放

root: 拉丁 liber「自由的」+ -atio（行为名词）→ liberatio「释放」。拉丁语 liber 另指「书」，属不同词干；liber 的拉丁语前词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one opening: a door is unlocked. The opening becomes a military recapture, a national end of foreign rule, a social removal of restraints, a private release, an organized cause, a chemical freeing and finally the lifting of any limit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次开启展开：门被打开。这次开启先成为军事收复，再成为民族结束外来统治，再成为社会束缚的解除，再成为个人解脱，再成为组织化事业，再成为化学释放，最后成为任何限制的移走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lock opened from within, light entering a long corridor, keys left on the sill.
core.cn: 核心意象：锁从里面被打开，光进入长走廊，钥匙留在窗台上。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL OPENING: a person or a place is released by force or by arrival.
branches.cn: 身体开启：一个人或一个地方因武力或到来而获释。

branches.en: THE COLLECTIVE CLAIM: a people or a class claims release from a system.
branches.cn: 集体诉求：一个民族或阶级要求从制度中释放。

branches.en: THE INNER DOOR: what confined a mind can also be opened.
branches.cn: 内门：困住心智的东西也能被打开。

branches.en: THE ORGANIZED CAUSE: the noun becomes a banner for a movement.
branches.cn: 组织化事业：这个名词成为运动旗帜。

branches.en: THE LIFTED WEIGHT: chemistry and abstraction both mean a restraint removed.
branches.cn: 移走的重量：化学与抽象义都指束缚被解除。

intro.en: Liberation is a Latin adjective turned into an action noun, and the same stem builds a large English family.
intro.cn: liberation 是由拉丁形容词变成的行为名词，同一词干构成庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin liber and liberare give liberty, liberal, liberate, liberation and deliver; the separate liber 'book' gives library and libretto.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 liber 与 liberare 衍生 liberty、liberal、liberate、liberation 与 deliver；另一个 liber「书」衍生 library 与 libretto。

items.example: The adjective described a free person, not a book.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述自由人，而非书。

items.example: The verb turned the state into an act.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把状态变成动作。

items.example: Liberation names the change, not the condition.
items.exampleCN: liberation 指变化，不指状态。

items.example: The unit liberated the town at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 部队在黎明解放了小镇。

items.example: The liberator refused a statue.
items.exampleCN: 这位解放者拒绝立像。

items.example: Liberty of speech has limits in law.
items.exampleCN: 言论自由在法律上有边界。

items.example: The word later became a political label.
items.exampleCN: 这个词后来成为政治标签。

items.example: The courier delivered the letter.
items.exampleCN: 信使投递了那封信。

items.example: The movement had a liberatory aim.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动带有解放目标。
